538.look: A river village of reed-thatched houses where reed flutes hang drying from the eaves.
538.lore: Its fishers play reed flutes at dusk, answering the songs of the boats on the river. In 803 the flutes fell silent with the boats, and the village still plays one tune less on that dusk.

539.name: Ngưng Tử Mạch
539.look: A hollow among badland hills where the dusk light pools in a deep purple long after sunset.
539.lore: An Earth vein runs under the hollow, and it holds the purple of the evening hills longest. Lạc Hà's disciples cultivate here in the last light.

540.name: Phí Thạch Tuyền
540.look: A boiling spring among red crags, its water bubbling up through stones too hot to touch.
540.lore: It is the only water for a day's walk in the waste. Copper miners cool its water in jars overnight before they drink.

541.name: Tử Đồng Khoáng
541.look: Shallow pits in the red badlands, half filled with sand, beside old heaps of green-stained rock.
541.lore: Lạc Hà once dug its coin and bell copper here, but the shallow ore is nearly spent. A few miners still pick over the heaps in summer; in winter the pits are left to the wind.

542.name: Chung Nhũ Quật
542.look: A deep cave among the karst pillars whose roof hangs with milky stone icicles, many of them cut short.
542.lore: Cutters take the stalactite stone here for the alchemists, who grind it into pills for the lungs. They work in groups and leave before dark, for other caves in the pillars are dens.

543.name: Oanh Hồi Hạp
543.look: A narrow karst gorge that winds back and forth between grey walls, so that a walker sees the same pillar three times.
543.lore: Its name comes from the old line about islands and isles winding round. The gorge floods in the rains, and gypsum cutters cross it only in the dry season.

544.name: Bạch Cao Động
544.look: A cave in the karst whose walls are crusted with soft white gypsum, scraped in long grooves.
544.lore: Cutters scrape gypsum here for the alchemists, who use it in cooling pills, and for the plaster of fine halls. The cave is cold even in summer.

545.name: Cuồng Trư Lâm
545.look: A high forest whose floor is rooted up and torn, with tusk marks on the trunks.
545.lore: Spirit boars as heavy as an ox root here and charge anything that moves. They break the mushroom racks of Hầu Đầu, and the village hires Lạc Hà's outer disciples to drive them back each autumn.

546.name: Hầu Đầu Thôn
546.look: A forest village where stacks of cut logs lean in the shade, studded with dark wood-ear mushrooms.
546.lore: Its villagers grow wood-ear mushrooms on cut logs and gather herbs in the high forest. Their dried mushrooms go down to Hạc Đinh Thị.

547.name: U Lan Cốc
547.look: A narrow karst valley where wild orchids grow on the damp walls.
547.lore: The orchids grow only in its shade, and herbalists climb its walls for them. The lime-burners leave its stone alone.

548.name: Hãm Thạch Trấn
548.look: A ring of broken walls in the forest around a deep round pit where the town's centre used to be.
548.lore: Lime-burners built the town in 340 on the edge of the karst. In 912 the ground under its market fell into a cave, and the rest of the town was left within a year. Its people moved to Hôi Diêu and have never built on bare karst since.

549.name: Hôi Diêu Thôn
549.look: A forest village of white-dusted houses beside smoking lime kilns.
549.lore: Its villagers burn the karst stone into lime for the plaster of Lạc Hà's halls. Everything in the village is white, and its children are called the ghosts of Ngư Ca.

550.name: Tằng Thúy Lâm
550.look: An old forest on the hills, its layers of green rising one above the other like stacked ranges.
550.lore: Its name comes from the old line about layered ranges rising green. The timber cutters of Phóng Mộc take only the trees at its edge.

551.name: Phóng Mộc Thôn
551.look: A river village where cut logs are rolled into the water and floated off in long chains.
551.lore: Its villagers fell timber in the hills and float it down to the plain. Each log is branded with the family's mark, and the downriver towns pay by the mark.

552.name: Quần Lang Lĩnh
552.look: A high forested ridge where wolf trails run under the trees and howls carry at night.
552.lore: Spirit grey wolves hunt the ridge in packs. In hard winters they come down to the camellia terraces, and the villagers light fires all night.

553.name: Sơn Trà Thôn
553.look: A mountain village on a river where camellia bushes line every terrace.
553.lore: Its villagers grow camellias for their oil and their tea. The oil goes to the lamps of Lạc Hà's halls.

554.name: Vân Tiêu Mạch
554.look: A grassy hollow inland where the clouds break first after rain and the light pours through.
554.lore: A Water vein runs under the hollow, named for the old line about clouds melting and rain clearing. The fishers of Vãn Đăng say the weather turns here first.

555.name: Vãn Đăng Thôn
555.look: A forest village on the coast where every boat hangs a lamp at the stern.
555.lore: Its fishers put out at dusk with lamps and come home singing. On the dusk of the mourning for 803 they light the lamps but do not put out.

556.name: Phong Ảnh Mạch
556.look: A grove of red maples on the higher ground whose shadows lie unusually sharp and still.
556.lore: A Wood vein runs under the maples. Lạc Hà's disciples say it is a cutting from the maples of the founder's first hall.

557.name: Lăng Hoa Thôn
557.look: A river village of grassy banks and ponds covered with the floating leaves of water chestnuts.
557.lore: Its villagers grow water chestnuts in the river ponds and gather them from small round tubs. Girls who can paddle a tub without spilling are thought to make good wives.

558.name: Vân Kiều Trấn
558.look: Ruined stone houses on a high mountain shoulder, reached by a broken stone bridge over a gorge.
558.lore: Silver miners built the town in 520 under Lạc Hà Tông, and reached it by a stone bridge often lost in cloud. By 1040 its silver was gone and its people had moved down to Vân Gian. The bridge broke in a storm a few years later.

559.name: Cổ Bách Mạch
559.look: A high slope of ancient cypresses whose trunks are twisted like rope.
559.lore: A Wood vein runs under the cypresses, the oldest trees in Ngư Ca Xuyên. Lạc Hà's elders go there to cultivate in solitude.

560.name: Vân Gian Thôn
560.look: A mountain village in the forest, often wrapped in cloud, with chestnut trees around its houses.
560.lore: Its villagers gather herbs and chestnuts in the mountain forest. They are descended from the miners of Vân Kiều Trấn and still keep their picks over the door.

561.name: Địa Hỏa Mạch
561.look: Cracked badland ground that steams in the cold and is warm to the hand.
561.lore: Its qi runs to Fire. The sulphur workers of Lưu Hoàng say its heat is why the pans never freeze.

562.name: Đan Nhũ Thang
562.look: A warm, milky-red pool in a steppe hollow below the cinnabar terraces.
562.lore: Miners of Thần Sa wash the red dust off here after each shift. Alchemists warn them not to drink it.

563.name: Bán Nguyệt Hồ
563.look: A crescent-shaped lake just east of Tinh Lạc Hồ, its reedy shallows full of nesting geese.
563.lore: It is fed by the overflow of Tinh Lạc Hồ and is too reedy to hold the stars. Thanh Khoa's people cut its reeds for thatch.

564.name: Tinh Kính Khoáng
564.look: A high cut in bare mountain rock, glittering with clear crystal, at the edge of the seat's warded slopes.
564.lore: Rock crystal from here is ground into lenses and array crystals for the Pivot's formation masters and for the armillary of Củng Tinh Quán.

565.name: Hoa Cái Đường
565.look: A compact hall of dark stone on a forested shoulder below the seat, its chimneys trailing thin coloured smoke from the furnaces within.
565.lore: Pill refiners (luyện đan) who use the cinnabar and sulphur of the red badlands founded this hall in 1060 under Thiên Xu, naming it for the canopy of stars over the pole. Its pills are sold through Thiên Quyền Thị and weighed there like everything else.

566.name: Tây Quan Bảo
566.look: Tumbled stone walls across a forested saddle on the seat's west road, with an empty gate arch standing alone.
566.lore: It guarded the west road to the seat from 340 and held it through the War of the Pivot. After the Compact was set the garrison stood down in 520, and its stones were carried off to build Thanh Khoa.

567.name: Thanh Khoa Thôn
567.look: Flat-roofed stone houses on the river, with barley fields and yaks grazing the far bank.
567.lore: Its people grow highland barley and roast it into flour, and send yak butter up to the Pivot's kitchens. They are the highest farmers on the plain.

568.name: Dương Hòa Tuyền
568.look: A warm, clear spring in a sheltered hollow of the hills, ringed with green grass in the depth of winter.
568.lore: The yurt herders winter beside it. Lambs born near it are said never to take cold.

569.name: Khuy Thiên Các
569.look: A roofless stone tower on a mountain shoulder, with a stair spiralling up to an empty platform open to the sky.
569.lore: Star-readers founded it in 380, rivals of Củng Tinh Quán. In 650 its head went blind, and its disciples joined the abbey and carried their charts with them; the tower has stood empty since.

570.name: Khung Lư Thôn
570.look: A ring of white felt yurts on the steppe, with horses tethered between them and dung fires smoking.
570.lore: Its herders move with the grass and come back here each winter. The village is wherever the yurts stand, but it always returns to the same ring of stones.

571.name: Kim Sa Khoáng
571.look: Wooden sluices in a mountain stream, with gold-washers bent over pans in the cold water.
571.lore: Gold is washed from the stream gravel in summer. Every washer pays a tenth to the Pivot by weight at Thiên Quyền.

572.name: Tùng Ảnh Phong
572.look: A forested peak whose pines throw long shadows across the plain at sunset.
572.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders on the plain tell the hour by how far its shadow has run.

573.name: Thiết Sa Khoáng
573.look: Black sand washed in a mountain gully and heaped on hide sheets to dry.
573.lore: Iron sand from here is carried up to the seat's smithies and smelted for the sect's tools.

574.name: Cửu Diệu Phong
574.look: A tall grey peak south of the seat with nine rock knobs around its summit.
574.lore: The Pivot's disciples go there to sit alone, one on each of the nine knobs, and the first to come down loses. Its qi runs to Metal, and a cultivator who sits through a night there finds the stars seem close enough to steady the spirit sense.

575.name: Câu Trần Phong
575.look: A low, curved ridge-peak bending like a hook above the steppe.
575.lore: Named for the star group that curls around the pole, it hooks round the beacon fort below it. Its qi runs to Earth, and formation masters walk its curve to learn how a ward should bend around what it guards.

576.name: Phong Toại Bảo
576.look: A small stone fort on a mountain spur, its beacon tower still standing with a blackened fire basket on top.
576.lore: From 505 its beacon passed warnings from the borders to the seat. After the truce of 805 the Pivot stood down its beacon line, and the fort was left in 806.

577.name: Mã An Phong
577.look: A double-humped peak on the steppe with a deep saddle between its summits, where the caravan path crosses.
577.lore: Caravans between Thiên Quyền and the southern mines cross its saddle. Its qi runs to Earth.

578.name: Đới Văn Khoáng
578.look: Banded agate nodules broken from grey mountain rock and sorted into baskets by colour.
578.lore: Banded agate is broken from the grey rock here in summer and carried to Thạch Kiều, where it is cut into beads and seals. Stones with a ring like an eye fetch the most, for star-readers set them in their charts.

579.name: Xa Luân Phong
579.look: A round-topped peak ringed by a circle of rock ribs like the spokes of a wheel.
579.lore: Herders say the five chariots of the sky rest on it at night. Its qi runs to Metal and turns slowly around the summit, and cultivators sit at its hub to circulate their own qi in the same wheel.

580.name: Đồn Điền Trại
580.look: Low stone walls around overgrown fields in a grassy valley, with a ruined barracks along one side.
580.lore: Soldier-farmers held it from 290, growing their own grain while they watched the south. After the Compact of 510 the Pivot no longer paid them, and by 530 the last had gone to Thạch Kiều.

581.name: Hồi Thủ Phong
581.look: A lonely peak on the steppe rim from which the whole plain can be seen behind and the grey waste ahead.
581.lore: Soldiers going west to Cố Lũy are said to have looked back at the plain from here. Its qi runs to Metal.

582.name: Lang Yên Trại
582.look: A ring of tumbled stones on a mountain flank with a heap of scorched signal stones at its centre.
582.lore: An outpost of Cố Lũy's line from 798, where signal smoke was lit to warn the ramparts. After the battle of 803 no one came to relieve it, and it was abandoned at the truce of 805.

583.name: Thái Bạch Mạch
583.look: A pale band of white quartz across a bare mountain face, bright in the evening light.
583.lore: Named for the evening star, its qi runs to Metal. Sword cultivators of the plain come to temper their blades on it.

584.name: Hồng Quả Thôn
584.look: A forest-edge village of grey roofs among hawthorn hedges red with berries in autumn.
584.lore: Its people make hawthorn sweets and medicine for the markets of Thiên Quyền. Children are paid in candied berries for picking.

585.name: Bạch Phàn Khoáng
585.look: White-crusted pits in grey mountain rock, with crystals drying in shallow trays.
585.lore: Alum from here fixes dyes and stops bleeding. The day crews leave before dusk and never sleep on the ridge.

586.name: Tê Mã Phong
586.look: A bare steppe peak above the grey edge of the waste, its rocks scoured by wind.
586.lore: Herders say they hear horses neighing from it on still nights, as others hear them in the miasma. Its qi runs to Earth.

587.name: Tẩy Giáp Trì
587.look: A steaming pool in a fold of the high plain, its rim of rust-stained stones.
587.lore: Quý Trường Kích's soldiers washed their armour here in the five years they held Cố Lũy. Herders say the rust in its stones is theirs.

588.name: Mao Ngưu Thôn
588.look: Low stone houses with yak-hair tent roofs on the open high plain, the yaks grazing up to the doors.
588.lore: Its herders keep yaks and sheep on the short grass near Cố Lũy. They leave a bowl of butter on the old ramparts each spring.

589.name: Thanh Kim Khoáng
589.look: A narrow, fallen-in adit in grey mountain rock, the old spoil flecked with deep blue stone.
589.lore: Lapis lazuli was once dug here in small blocks and carried down to Thạch Kiều. The adit fell in long ago, but the deep blue of the Pivot's star charts and of Củng Tinh's painted ceilings came from here.

590.name: Lão Mã Bảo
590.look: Long stone stables and a walled yard on the high plain, empty but for grass and wind.
590.lore: The Pivot bred remounts for its riders here from 600. After the battle of 803 no riders came back to claim the horses; the herds were sold and the fort was left by 806.

591.name: Thổ Long Mạch
591.look: A long ochre ridge of badland winding beside the river like a sleeping beast.
591.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, heavy and slow like the river beside it. The herders will not dig into it or pitch tents on its back, and Earth cultivators walk its whole length to steady their foundation.

592.name: Tô Du Thôn
592.look: Stone houses on the river with butter churns at every door and cheese drying on the roofs.
592.lore: Its herders make yak butter and cheese and carry them to Thạch Kiều. Butter tea is offered to every traveller, and it is rude to refuse a third bowl.

593.name: Đại Giả Khoáng
593.look: A badland slope dug into red-brown terraces, with ochre cakes drying in rows.
593.lore: Its ochre is used for paint and in medicine. The diggers' hands stay red for a season.

594.name: Lưu Tinh Mạch
594.look: A shallow dish in the steppe, its rocks scorched black and glassy.
594.lore: Said to be where one of the stones of the nine days struck, its qi runs to Metal. Củng Tinh's star-readers visit it each year.

595.name: Thạch Ốc Thôn
595.look: Thick-walled stone houses huddled on a river bend, with barley and pea fields on the flats.
595.lore: Its houses are built of stone against the plateau wind. Each house keeps one stone from the falling stars of the Wild Age in its wall, or says it does.

596.name: Tử Thạch Khoáng
596.look: Purple crystal geodes cracked open in a mountain cut.
596.lore: Amethyst geodes are cracked from the mountain rock here and sorted by colour. The deepest purple goes into the Pivot's ceremonial seals, and the pale stones are sold to cultivators who hold them to calm the mind.

597.name: Cương Phong Mạch
597.look: A bare steppe shoulder high above the river where the wind never stops and the grass grows flat.
597.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, sharp as the wind. Cultivators sit here to hone their spirit sense.

598.name: Xa Ngưu Thôn
598.look: Stone cattle pens and low houses on the steppe, with herds dust-brown on the slopes.
598.lore: Its people raise oxen for the caravans and the Pivot's carts. An ox from here is sold with its weight written on its horn.

599.name: Bạch Diêm Tuyền
599.look: A warm brine spring on the steppe, crusted with white salt around its rim.
599.lore: Hồ Dương's people boil its brine for salt. The salt is weighed at Thạch Kiều and sold across the heart.

600.name: Hồ Dương Thôn
600.look: A river village under gnarled desert poplars gold in autumn, with salt pans by the bank.
600.lore: Its people farm the river flats and boil salt from the warm brine spring in the hills. Caravans bound for the desert water here.

601.name: Thủ Linh Phong
601.look: A dark mountain standing over the grey waste, its foot lost in haze.
601.lore: Thiên Xu's patrols climb it to look over Chiết Kích Nguyên without entering it. Its qi runs to Earth, heavy and dark.

602.name: Hoàng Yên Tuyền
602.look: A sulphurous spring in red badland, wrapped in yellow steam.
602.lore: It smells of eggs and heals the skin. The goatherds bathe their flocks in its runoff against mites.

603.name: Tập Trận Khoáng
603.look: A soft grey soapstone pit on the high plain, its walls smooth and greasy to the touch.
603.lore: Soapstone from here is carved into bowls and into the practice array discs of novice formation masters.

604.name: Thạch Điền Thôn
604.look: Tiny stone-walled terraces stepping up a high slope, with a village of flat roofs at their foot.
604.lore: Its people farm barley in walled terraces and keep goats. Every stone in the walls was cleared from the fields by hand.

605.name: Ngân Sa Khoáng
605.look: Glittering grey sand dug from a mountain pocket and washed in leather troughs.
605.lore: The silver sand is sent to the Pivot's mint. Washers are searched at the gate each night.

606.name: Tảo Xuân Mạch
606.look: A forested fold of the hills where the leaves come out a month before anywhere else.
606.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, quick and green. Herders bring sick lambs here in early spring, and herb gatherers find the first shoots of the year in its shade.

607.name: Bách Linh Thôn
607.look: A steppe village on the river, its fields loud with larks in spring.
607.lore: Its people herd sheep and farm the river flats. Lark cages hang at every door, and a good singer is worth a sheep.

608.name: Lục Ngọc Khoáng
608.look: A cut in a high mountain face showing veins of dark green stone.
608.lore: Green jade from here is carved at Bích Khê and sold back to the plain at twice the price.

609.name: Thạch Dương Thôn
609.look: A cluster of stone huts on high stony steppe with goats on every rock.
609.lore: Its herders keep goats under the hawk cliffs. They say the grey hawks take only the goats that stray.

610.name: Thứu Chủy Phong
610.look: A hooked rock beak jutting from a forested mountain.
610.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Bark peelers use it to find their way back to their camps.

611.name: Quảng Dã Mạch
611.look: A broad, gently rising stretch of steppe where the grass grows waist-high.
611.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, spread wide and even across the steppe. Horses grazed on it grow strong and steady, and the herders of Mã Nãi keep it for their best mares.

612.name: Mã Nãi Thôn
612.look: Felt and stone houses by the river, with leather bags of fermenting milk hanging from posts.
612.lore: Its herders brew fermented mare's milk and trade it at Thạch Kiều. A guest is offered a bowl before a word is spoken.

613.name: Thạch Chung Phong
613.look: A bell-shaped peak of grey rock above the ruined city.
613.lore: Its rocks ring like bells when struck, and herders say they rang by themselves the night Lục Hợp Thành's cistern split. Its qi runs to Metal, and cultivators listen to the ringing to tune their own meridians.

614.name: Lục Hợp Thành
614.look: Long walls and a grid of empty streets on a mountain shelf, with a cracked stone cistern at the centre.
614.lore: A caravan city built on the southern road in 330, under Thiên Xu's protection. In 912 an earthquake split its cistern and dried its springs, and within a year its people had moved to Thạch Kiều.

615.name: Kim Hạt Cốc
615.look: A shallow sandy valley in the steppe, its sand ridged by the tracks of many legs.
615.lore: Golden spirit scorpions as big as dogs bury themselves here. Their venom is prized by alchemists, and their hunters seldom grow old.

616.name: Đông Noãn Tuyền
616.look: A steaming spring among rocks on the steppe, warm enough to bathe in during snow.
616.lore: The nomads of Du Mục winter by it and bathe in it together on New Year's night. Its warm water keeps a ring of grass green around it, and the herds graze there when the steppe is under snow.

617.name: Tiêu Thạch Khoáng
617.look: A cave in the mountain whose walls are crusted with white salt, scraped into sacks.
617.lore: Saltpetre from here is sold to Thiên Xu for fire powders, mixed with the sulphur of Lưu Hoàng.

618.name: Du Mục Thôn
618.look: A winter camp of stone-walled yurts on the steppe, with dung stacked high against the walls.
618.lore: Herders who move with the grass all summer winter here. The camp's stone walls are older than anyone can remember.

619.name: Sương Đầu Phong
619.look: A high mountain whose summit stays white with frost and snow most of the year.
619.lore: Falconers of Liệp Ưng release their old birds from its slopes to die free. Its qi runs to Metal, cold and clear, and cultivators who sit in its frost find their thoughts slow and sharpen.

620.name: Liệp Ưng Thôn
620.look: A steppe village of stone houses with hooded hawks on perches at every door.
620.lore: Its people fly hawks and falcons for hares and foxes and sell trained birds at Thạch Kiều.

621.name: Hồng Ngọc Khoáng
621.look: A few narrow, long-empty adits in a high mountain face, red grains still glinting in the spoil.
621.lore: Small crews once dug rubies here in summer, the best for the Pivot and the rest for Thạch Kiều. The seam has played out, and only children climb up to sift the spoil.

622.name: Thọ Tinh Phong
622.look: A tall, broad peak on the southern rim, its summit catching the light of the southern sky.
622.lore: Old cultivators climb it near the end of their years to watch the longevity star. Its qi runs to Earth.

623.name: Hải Lam Khoáng
623.look: Blue-stained rock in an old mountain cut above the coast, where a stream still runs blue past the abandoned washing floors.
623.lore: Azurite and a little malachite were dug here until the cut flooded. Smelted, the ore gave copper; ground, it gave the blue paint still on the Pivot's halls.

624.name: Lục Bình Phong
624.look: A grassy-topped mountain whose long green summit looks out over the coast.
624.lore: From its grassy summit the far water can be seen on clear days. Its qi runs to Wood and Earth, and herb gatherers find mountain gentian on its top that grows nowhere else on the rim.

625.name: Bạch Trâm Phong
625.look: A thin, pale spire of rock standing above the forest and the morning cloud.
625.lore: It can be seen from Mộc Hương Thôn on clear days, standing above the cloud. Its qi runs to Metal, thin and bright, and sword cultivators sit on its narrow tip to train a single-pointed mind.

626.name: Liên Hoa Phong
626.look: A ring of rock petals around a central summit north of the seat's mountains.
626.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Travellers from the north see it first of all the seat's mountains.

627.name: Tùng Nhân Thôn
627.look: A forest-edge village with sacks of pine cones heaped by every door and sheep on the steppe beyond.
627.lore: Its people gather pine nuts in the forests each autumn and herd sheep on the steppe the rest of the year. The nuts are roasted in big iron pans and sold at Thiên Quyền, and the best go up to the Pivot's kitchens.

628.name: Huyền Cương Khoáng
628.look: A dark adit in mountain rock with heaps of black, heavy ore at its mouth.
628.lore: Its dark iron-manganese ore is carried down by mule and smelted into a tough black steel. The plain's carpenters and herb diggers swear by tools made from it.

629.name: Tiên Nhân Phong
629.look: A forested peak topped by a rock shaped like a seated figure.
629.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Villagers leave food at the rock for the immortal they say sits there.

630.name: Đương Quy Thôn
630.look: A forest village on a high slope, with angelica beds and roots drying on bamboo trays.
630.lore: Its people grow and dig angelica root for the alchemists of the plain. A root that grows forked is given to a newly married couple.

631.name: Kim Tinh Khoáng
631.look: A small, guarded adit in bare mountain rock, its mouth closed with an iron grille.
631.lore: There is gold here, but the sect keeps the adit shut against its own need, and none of it has ever been weighed in the market.

632.name: Thái Nhất Phong
632.look: A sharp high peak north of the seat, lined up with the pole star at night.
632.lore: The Pivot's watchmen keep a post on its shoulder and sight the pole star over its tip each night. Its qi runs to Metal, and the sect's elders send disciples here to sit facing the pole until their minds are as still as it.

633.name: Cam Lộ Mạch
633.look: A forest glade where a sweet dew beads on the leaves every dawn.
633.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Children lick the leaves in spring, and the alchemists collect the dew in jars.

634.name: Hoàng Kỳ Thôn
634.look: A village at the forest edge with bundles of yellow root drying on the eaves.
634.lore: Its people dig milkvetch root on the steppe and sell it to physicians and alchemists.

635.name: Tị Xà Khoáng
635.look: Orange-red realgar crystals in grey mountain rock, untouched but for a few broken out long ago.
635.lore: The realgar here is good against snakes and for some pills, but its dust sickens those who break it out, and the cut has been left since the last crew fell ill.

636.name: Bách Tuế Mạch
636.look: A stand of enormous old trees high in the forest, the ground soft with centuries of needles.
636.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herb gatherers say a plant that grows here lives a hundred years.

637.name: Tầm Dược Thôn
637.look: A high forest village of log houses with baskets of herbs hung from every beam.
637.lore: Its people climb the forested slopes for mountain herbs. They rope themselves together on the steep ground.

638.name: Tẩy Tâm Tuyền
638.look: A clear warm spring in a mountain cleft, its water so still it seems not to move.
638.lore: Carpenters rest their backs here. Cultivators say it calms the heart before a breakthrough.

639.name: Xảo Tượng Thôn
639.look: A forest village of fine timber houses with carved beams and workshops full of shavings.
639.lore: Its carpenters make beams, carts and array frames for the plain. The Pivot's formation masters order their frames here.

640.name: Thập Giáp Thôn
640.look: A river village of stone houses with iron-grey beast plates stacked against the walls.
640.lore: Its people gather the plates the beasts of Thiết Bối Cốc shed and sell them to smiths. They herd goats and keep out of the herd's path.

641.name: Phi Hoàng Cương
641.look: A dry steppe ridge stripped bare of grass, the ground pocked with egg holes.
641.lore: Spirit locusts hatch here and rise in swarms in late summer. Their swarms strip fields bare, and their wings are used in talismans.

642.name: Lục Đồng Khoáng
642.look: Green-stained rock in a mountain cut, with a broken ore cart left on the overgrown road below.
642.lore: Its green copper ore was once hauled by ox over the ridge and weighed at Song Kiều like all the ore of Ngọc Hành, until richer cuts nearer the scales took its trade.

643.name: Đồng Trụ Phong
643.look: A tall bronze-brown pillar of rock above the ore roads, its flanks streaked green where copper weathers out.
643.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore drivers touch its foot for luck, and cultivators of Metal arts climb its pillar to feel the ore singing in the rock.

644.name: Thủ Hỏa Bảo
644.look: A squat stone fort below the warding pillars, its walls glazed by heat.
644.lore: From 460 a garrison kept watch on the vent here. When the warding pillars were raised in 1040 the Pivot withdrew the garrison, and the fort was left.

645.name: Sa Nhãn Tuyền
645.look: A small warm pool among dunes, its water bubbling up through clean sand.
645.lore: It is the only sure water on the shifting plain. Travellers mark it with a tall pole so the dunes do not hide it, and replace the pole when it falls.

646.name: Khổ Tu Viện
646.look: Bare stone cells cut into a mountainside above the desert, each just big enough to sit in.
646.lore: Ascetics who fasted in the desert founded it in 610. Fewer and fewer came to take up the hard life, and by 880 the cells were empty.

647.name: Liệt Nhật Mạch
647.look: A patch of steppe where the ground is hot even at night and the grass is scorched yellow.
647.lore: Its qi runs to Fire and Earth. Fire cultivators sit here at noon, and the ascetics of the mountain above once walked here barefoot as a trial.

648.name: Hôi Mãng Cương
648.look: A ridge of grey dunes marked with long, smooth, curving tracks.
648.lore: Grey spirit pythons as long as boats bury themselves here and take camels. Their skins are prized for drums, and the caravans pay well for them.

649.name: Thanh Đăng Tự
649.look: A small temple on a mountain shoulder, its roof gone and a bronze lamp still hanging in the hall.
649.lore: A small sect of monks who kept a lamp burning for travellers founded it in 450. Its last abbot died in 760 with no disciple, and the lamp went out.

650.name: Ô Ngân Khoáng
650.look: A narrow adit in dark mountain rock, its spoil black and heavy.
650.lore: Its black silver ore, silver darkened with sulphur, is refined at Song Kiều. The crews come up the desert edge in spring and leave before the autumn wind.

651.name: Ỷ Thiên Phong
651.look: A tall peak leaning over the desert edge, as if propping up the sky.
651.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Caravans steer by it across the desert, and sword cultivators climb its overhang to practise against the wind.

652.name: Bạch Kim Khoáng
652.look: A small mine high on the mountain, with heavy grey grains washed in a cold stream.
652.lore: Its rare white metal does not rust or melt in a common forge. It goes straight to the Pivot's own forges for array anchors.

653.name: Thiên Môn Phong
653.look: Two high summits with a deep gap between them, where the old ore road passes.
653.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore drivers call the gap the gate of heaven, and cultivators sit in it at dawn, when the wind through the gate is said to clear the meridians.

654.name: Thiết Môn Bảo
654.look: A stone stockade across the old ore road, its iron gate rusted open.
654.lore: The miners' bosses held this stockade from 140 to tax the ore at the gate. When Thiên Xu's assayers began to weigh ore in public at Song Kiều in 235, the miners stopped coming, and it was left.

655.name: Hoàng Thiết Khoáng
655.look: Brassy cubes of pyrite glittering in an abandoned grey mountain cut.
655.lore: No one works it now: its pyrite fetched too little as fire-strikers or roasted sulphur. Passing travellers still fill their pockets with it, thinking it gold.

656.name: Thạch Kính Phong
656.look: A peak with a smooth, polished rock face that flashes in the sun.
656.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Miners use its flash to signal across the valleys, and cultivators gaze into its face to calm the mind before a breakthrough.

657.name: Lô Cam Khoáng
657.look: Pale, crumbly ore pits in a low valley at the mountain's foot, with ore spread to roast on stone hearths.
657.lore: Calamine from here is carried to Thối Tinh Môn and alloyed with copper into brass for fittings and array rings. The roasting fumes turn the valley's grass white.

658.name: Ngân Giáp Phong
658.look: A great snow peak of the north-eastern massif, its snowfields plated in overlapping scales like armour.
658.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water, cold enough to bite through robes. No one has climbed it; cultivators who meditate on its lower snowfields say it hardens the body like quenched steel.

659.name: Huân Yên Phong
659.look: A high peak streaked black by the smoke of small vents on its flanks.
659.lore: Its qi runs to Fire. The ground near its vents is warm all winter, and Fire cultivators camp beside them to temper their spirit fire.

660.name: Tuần Hải Bảo
660.look: A stone fort on a coastal headland, its seaward wall cracked and its beacon cold.
660.lore: Thiên Xu built it in 650 to watch for the pirates of Thôn Hải Môn. After the Pirate Purge destroyed them in 781 the fort was not needed, and it was stood down in 790.

661.name: Hùng Điêu Nhai
661.look: High cliffs above the steppe, streaked white below the nests of great golden eagles.
661.lore: Spirit eagles nest here and take lambs and young camels. Their feathers are prized by fletchers, and Đà Đội's children are taught to lie flat when a shadow passes.

662.name: Đà Đội Thôn
662.look: A steppe village of stone houses with camels kneeling in the yards and bells hanging from the eaves.
662.lore: Its people keep camels and hire them to the desert caravans. Each camel's bell has its own note, and the owners know them in the dark.

663.name: Nham Diêm Khoáng
663.look: A pink-white salt cut in the mountain, with salt blocks stacked for the mule trains.
663.lore: Its rock salt goes to the mining villages of Ngọc Hành. A block of it is given to every new miner's family.

664.name: Lạc Đà Phong
664.look: A two-humped peak above the steppe, brown and bare.
664.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, slow and enduring. Caravans know they are near Đà Đội when they see it, and Earth cultivators sit in the saddle between its humps.

665.name: Tích Lương Trại
665.look: Stone granaries inside a broken palisade on the high plain.
665.lore: It stored grain for the miners from 300. When the grain road moved to Song Kiều in 640 the stockade was left.

666.name: Mã Ẩm Tuyền
666.look: A warm spring on the high ground above the sand, its rim trampled by hooves.
666.lore: Caravans water their horses here. It is said a horse that drinks here will not tire for a day.

667.name: Ải Ngọc Khoáng
667.look: A cut on a lower shoulder of the mountain, just below the haze line, where a soft blue-grey jade shows in the abandoned face.
667.lore: The jade from here has the colour of Thanh Ải's haze. The miners never climbed above the haze line, and on the day the haze lifted in 1180 they left the cut and did not come back.

668.name: Hành Vân Phong
668.look: A high bare peak with clouds always drifting across its summit.
668.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Ore trains cross the pass below it in summer, and cultivators climb above the clouds to sit in the clear air.

669.name: Giới Bi Phong
669.look: A high peak with a stone stele on its summit facing the east.
669.lore: Thiên Xu's boundary with Phượng Minh is marked on its summit. Its qi runs to Metal and Fire, and on clear nights the glow of the cinnabar ridge can be seen from it.

670.name: Ngân Thuyền Bảo
670.look: A stone fort on the shore, its harbour silted up into a reed marsh.
670.lore: It guarded silver shipped by sea from 460. Its harbour silted up, and by 1003 the silver went overland to Song Kiều and the fort was left.

671.name: Mục Đồng Phong
671.look: A grassy peak with herders' stone shelters on its top.
671.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, mild and green. Herd boys play pipes on its summit in summer, and young cultivators find it a gentle place to first open their meridians.

672.name: Bạch Thạch Phong
672.look: A peak of white stone above the steppe, bright against the autumn sky.
672.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. It can be seen from the caravan road, and cultivators climb it in autumn when the dry wind sharpens its qi.

673.name: Vọng Phàm Phong
673.look: A high peak above the river mouth, looking far over the water.
673.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Families of sailors climb it to watch for returning sails, and leave a stone on the cairn for each one.

674.name: Quải Vân Phong
674.look: A great snow peak above the sea cliffs, clouds hanging from its shoulders like banners.
674.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Fishermen see it from far out on the inland sea, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its lower cliffs to draw on the sea mist.

675.name: Hắc Sa Khoáng
675.look: Black magnetite sand washed in a gully and heaped on mats, clinging to any iron tool laid on it.
675.lore: Its magnetite sand is smelted into iron for tools. The washers pull it from the gravel with lodestones on strings.

676.name: Quân Tử Phong
676.look: A peak with bamboo on its flanks and a straight, upright rock summit.
676.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Scholars come to paint its bamboo, and cultivators sit among the stems to practise stillness.

677.name: Lục Nhung Mạch
677.look: A grassy slope covered in soft green moss like velvet.
677.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Cattle grazed here give rich milk, and the village keeps it for the calving cows.

678.name: Hoàng Hoa Thôn
678.look: A grassland village among fields of yellow daylilies, with cattle on the slopes.
678.lore: Its people grow daylilies for food and medicine and graze cattle. Dried flowers from here are sold in Tinh Hán as far as the quays.

679.name: Cô Tháp Phong
679.look: A tower-like peak standing alone above the grassy plateau.
679.lore: Its qi runs to Earth. Cloud lies around its foot most mornings, and Earth cultivators sit on its top above the cloud.

680.name: Lựu Thạch Khoáng
680.look: Dark red garnets in grey mountain rock, picked out by hand.
680.lore: Its garnets are cut into beads, and the small ones are crushed into polishing grit for the forges of Thối Tinh.

681.name: Thạch Căn Mạch
681.look: A rock outcrop on the high plain, its grey stone veined like roots.
681.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, deep and steady. Herders say no storm has ever knocked down a cairn built on it.

682.name: Mục Khuyển Thôn
682.look: A steppe village with sheepdogs lying at every door and flocks on the hills.
682.lore: Its herders breed sheepdogs for all of Ngọc Hành. A pup from here is paid for in silver.

683.name: Ngân Ti Khoáng
683.look: Thin threads of native silver in a damp mountain face beside the falls.
683.lore: Its silver is picked out by hand with fine chisels and refined at Song Kiều. Silversmiths value the threads for wire.

684.name: Ngọc Lâu Phong
684.look: A tall pale peak above the falls, its walls stacked like the floors of a tower.
684.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Cultivators sit behind the falls at its foot to temper the body under the water's weight.

685.name: Cẩm Thạch Khoáng
685.look: A quarry of banded marble on a low shoulder, its blocks patterned like woven silk.
685.lore: Its marble is carved into tables and screens for the halls of Tinh Hán. Blocks are lowered down the slope on ropes from Thằng Ma.

686.name: Hồng Nhạn Phong
686.look: A high peak where wild geese rest on its ledges on their migration.
686.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Hunters do not shoot the geese here, and cultivators read the seasons by their coming and going.

687.name: Đồng Tỉnh Khoáng
687.look: A deep copper shaft in the gully with a windlass and leather buckets.
687.lore: Its copper ore comes up by bucket and is weighed at Song Kiều. The shaft floods every spring and must be bailed by hand.

688.name: Thanh Loa Phong
688.look: A spiral-ridged green peak above the river, like a conch shell.
688.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Herders summer below it, and cultivators climb its spiral path in one breath as a test.

689.name: Lam Lục Khoáng
689.look: Red cliffs by the river streaked green and blue with copper ore.
689.lore: Its copper ore is broken from the cliffs and floated by river to the landing at Mã Đầu.

690.name: Xích Dực Phong
690.look: A red peak above the badland gully, its two ridges spread like wings.
690.lore: Its qi runs to Fire with a base of Earth. Fire cultivators sit between its wings at sunset, when the red rock glows.

691.name: Cửu Tiêu Phong
691.look: A very high peak above the forest, its summit often lost in sky.
691.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, thin and sharp. Cultivators who reach its summit say the air there makes the spirit feel weightless.

692.name: Thủ Bi Trại
692.look: Broken walls under an avalanche slope, half buried in rock.
692.lore: From 520 a garrison guarded a boundary stele set after the Compact. An avalanche buried the stockade in 1006, and the stele was moved lower.

693.name: Hoàng Ngọc Khoáng
693.look: Golden crystals in grey mountain rock above the river, in a cut half full of spring water.
693.lore: Topaz from here was once cut at Tinh Hán into ring stones and seals, but the springs have not run low in the dry months for years, and the crews no longer come.

694.name: Tử Cái Phong
694.look: A peak with a cap of purple rock over the twin springs.
694.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Herb gatherers find a purple lichen on its cap that alchemists buy for calming pills.

695.name: Hắc Ưng Phong
695.look: A dark peak above the eastern coast, black hawks wheeling around its summit.
695.lore: Below it opens the mouth of Cửu U Động, which Thối Tinh's miners do not enter. Its qi runs to Metal, and the hawks are said to hunt only those who sleep on its summit.

696.name: Tử Ngọc Khoáng
696.look: A high cut showing veins of purple stone under the sheer wall.
696.lore: Its purple jade is rare and goes to the Pivot for seals. The crews work only in high summer.

697.name: Tuyệt Bích Phong
697.look: A sheer high peak on the southern rim, its walls dropping toward the south.
697.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. From its edge the Pivot's old watchmen could see as far as Kinh Lôi Mạch, and climbers still use their iron pegs.

698.name: Nam Vọng Bảo
698.look: A stone fort on the heights, its walls broken and its watch platform facing south.
698.lore: The Pivot's border watch on the south ridge from 512, looking down toward Kinh Lôi Mạch. It was stood down in 806 after the truce.

699.name: Xích Ngân Khoáng
699.look: Dark red silver ore glinting in a mountain cut by the old road.
699.lore: Its red silver ore is roasted on site and refined at Song Kiều. It is richer in silver than any other mine on the old road.

700.name: Ưng Sào Phong
700.look: A peak with hawks' nests on its cliffs above the orchid brook.
700.lore: Its qi runs to Metal. Young cultivators climb its cliffs for hawk chicks to tame.

701.name: Hạp Khẩu Trại
701.look: A stockade half buried under a landslide at the mouth of a gorge.
701.lore: A toll stockade on the ore road from 300. A landslide buried it in 718, and the road was moved to the other bank.

702.name: Hắc Phong Trại
702.look: A stockade of rough stone on the windy heights, its walls broken.
702.lore: A bandit hold of rogue cultivators (tán tu) from 880, who robbed the ore trains. Thiên Xu cleared it in 940.

703.name: Lưu Kim Khoáng
703.look: Wooden sluices in the green torrent, with washers in leather aprons.
703.lore: Gold is washed from the torrent's gravel after the spring floods. Every washer pays a tenth to the Pivot by weight.

704.name: Ngọc Nữ Phong
704.look: A slender pale peak above the torrent, like a standing woman.
704.lore: Its qi runs to Metal and Water. Women cultivators of Water arts come to meditate at its foot by the torrent.

705.name: Phù Dung Phong
705.look: A forested peak above the shore that flowers pink each summer.
705.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Sailors on the inland sea say summer has come when its slopes turn pink.

706.name: Trấn Sơn Phong
706.look: A massive dark peak above the winch house of Huyền Thiết.
706.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Metal, heavy as the iron below it. Body cultivators carry stones up it to temper their bones.

707.name: Lục Ấm Mạch
707.look: A shady forest grove above the hemp fields where the air is always cool.
707.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. Hemp seed soaked in its spring is said to grow the strongest fibre.

708.name: Thằng Ma Thôn
708.look: A grassland village among hemp fields, with long rope walks along the lane.
708.lore: Its people twist hemp into rope for the mines' winches. A rope that breaks is traced back to its maker.

709.name: Thư Hoàng Khoáng
709.look: Bright yellow orpiment in grey mountain rock.
709.lore: Its yellow pigment is sold to talisman makers and painters. It is poisonous, and the diggers wear cloth over their faces.

710.name: Xích Long Mạch
710.look: A red badland ridge winding like a dragon, warm to the touch.
710.lore: Its qi runs to Earth and Fire. No grass grows on its spine, and herders say it shifts a little each century.

711.name: Hắc Ngưu Cương
711.look: A steppe ridge trampled by a herd of black bulls.
711.lore: Wild spirit bulls graze here and charge anything that comes near. Their horns are carved into bows.

712.name: Hoành Đao Môn
712.look: A ruined gate and halls on the grassland, with a stone sabre rack in the yard.
712.lore: A small sect of saber fighters founded in 560. Its head left on a journey in 870 and never returned, and the disciples scattered by 872.

713.name: Mã Đầu Thôn
713.look: A river village with boats tied at a long timber landing.
713.lore: Its people load ore and wool onto river boats bound for the coast. They are paid by the load and counted by a tally stick.

714.name: Thanh Thiết Khoáng
714.look: Blue-grey iron ore in a mountain cut above the sea.
714.lore: Its iron ore is carried down to boats and shipped to Tinh Hán's quays. Smiths say it takes a fine edge.

715.name: Ngư Ông Phong
715.look: A peak on the cape shaped like a fisherman bent over his line.
715.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Fishermen steer by it, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its spray-wet ledge at dawn.

716.name: Ô Thiết Khoáng
716.look: Adits in a black rock face high on the mountain, with a stone smelting hearth on a ledge below.
716.lore: Phượng Minh's smiths take its black iron for blades and the bronze-and-iron frames of the palace bells.

717.name: Xích Tiêu Phong
717.look: A tall bare peak of reddish rock on the western wall, often lit red at sunset while the valleys are dark.
717.lore: Phượng Minh keeps a beacon on its top, lit only in war. Its qi runs Kim (metal) through the iron in the rock.

718.name: Phượng Dực Phong
718.look: A peak with one long sloping arm of rock and bamboo, like a raised wing, above ravines of wutong.
718.lore: Fire disciples run up its arm at dawn as a training climb. Its qi runs Mộc (wood), carried up from the bamboo.

719.name: Vân Trúc Lâm
719.look: Tall pale bamboo on a steep rocky slope, its tops often hidden in low cloud.
719.lore: Its canes grow thin and strong in the thin soil, and Trúc Ly's weavers prize them for fine work.

720.name: Trúc Ly Thôn
720.look: A valley village where every yard is fenced in woven bamboo and half-finished baskets stand stacked by the doors.
720.lore: Its weavers make baskets, screens and the great stone-filled baskets of Bích Lãng's sea wall.

721.name: Nguyệt Ngân Khoáng
721.look: A narrow silver working in pale rock, its spoil heaps glinting white in moonlight.
721.lore: Its silver goes to the palace's inlay makers. Miners say the best seams show themselves on full-moon nights.

722.name: Thê Hoàng Phong
722.look: A white crag crowned by a single old wutong growing from a crack in the summit rock.
722.lore: Phượng Minh's wood cultivators sit under the tree for trial. Its qi runs Mộc (wood), unusually for so bare a rock.

723.name: Thực Thiết Cốc
723.look: A bamboo valley stripped bare in patches, its stream banks littered with chewed cane and gnawed iron pots.
723.lore: Black-and-white spirit bears, the iron-eaters of the old books, live here on bamboo and steal any iron they can find. Villagers leave old pots at the valley mouth to keep them away from the forge.

724.name: Kích Khánh Đường
724.look: A roofless stone hall high on the crags, its floor scattered with broken L-shaped slabs of chime stone.
724.lore: Cửu Thiều Cung's chime makers cut and tuned their stone chimes here. The hall was smashed in the War of the Nine Shao in 340, and the broken chimes still ring faintly when stepped on.

725.name: Cầm Huyền Hương
725.look: A river hamlet of silkworm sheds, with skeins of twisted silk string hung to dry on long racks by the water.
725.lore: Its people twist silk into strings for zithers and pipas and sell them to Thiều Âm Thị. They boil the cocoons in river water and say it makes the strings sing true.

726.name: Vịnh Trúc Lĩnh
726.look: A rocky ridge above the bamboo where a short poem is cut into a flat rock face.
726.lore: Phượng Minh's founder Ngô Thê Đồng is said to have cut the bamboo ode here in the palace's first years. Its qi runs Mộc (wood).

727.name: Trúc Phiệt Thôn
727.look: A riverside village among dense bamboo, its bank lined with great half-lashed rafts of cut cane.
727.lore: Its cutters float bamboo downriver to the coast every spring flood and walk home along the bank.

728.name: Xích Đồng Khoáng
728.look: Copper workings cut into the foot of the sea cliffs, the rock stained green and red where the waves wash it, with a timber landing for the ore boats.
728.lore: Miners from Thanh Khê work the seams at low tide and pull back when the sea turns. Its copper goes by boat to the port for the bronze bells of the palace and the frames of the harbour lanterns.

729.name: Vọng Dương Phong
729.look: A tall bare peak above the gulf, its eastern face scorched dark by the morning sun.
729.lore: Phượng Minh's fire disciples climb it to take in the first sun. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

730.name: Hàm Đan Phong
730.look: A bamboo-clad peak whose rock shows through in streaks of bright red.
730.lore: Cinnabar runs in thin streaks through the rock, too thin to mine. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

731.name: Thạch Thanh Khoáng
731.look: Shallow pits by the shore where the rock is veined bright blue.
731.lore: Its azurite is ground for blue pigment and sold to painters and to the palace's lacquer workers.

732.name: Lâm Hải Nhai
732.look: A sheer bamboo-topped cliff dropping straight into the gulf, white with sea birds.
732.lore: Gulf fishers steer by it in fog. Its qi runs Thủy (water), drawn up from the sea.

733.name: Ngưng Hà Lĩnh
733.look: A rocky ridge above the bamboo that glows red on clear evenings long after the sun has set.
733.lore: The villagers say the sunset clouds gather here to sleep. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

734.name: Sa Trúc Thôn
734.look: A fishing village of thatched bamboo houses on a sandy cove, with rows of cone-shaped fish traps of split cane drying on the beach.
734.lore: Its people set their traps in the shallows at dusk and lift them at dawn, and cut cane on the slopes behind to sell to passing boats. When the ridge above glows red after sunset, they say the next day's catch will be good.

735.name: Quy Vũ Lĩnh
735.look: A long brown ridge where migrating birds rest in thousands every autumn and spring.
735.lore: The villagers say the birds come back each year to the phoenix's land. Its qi runs Thổ (earth), steady and slow.

736.name: Kiều Mạch Thôn
736.look: A handful of stone houses on a dry hillside, ringed by fields of white-flowered buckwheat.
736.lore: Buckwheat grows where the rain is short and there is no river, and the village has lived on it and on goats for generations. Its noodles are sold in Thiều Âm Thị.

737.name: Chung Nhũ Động
737.look: A sea-facing karst cave hung with pale dripping stalactites, many broken off at the tips.
737.lore: Alchemists' miners take the stalactite milk-stone for pills of the bones and lungs. Phượng Minh allows only fallen and broken pieces to be taken from the inner hall.

738.name: Lôi Hậu Thôn
738.look: A bamboo-walled fishing village on the storm shore, its sheds stacked with scarred wutong logs under palace seals.
738.lore: After each storm clears, its gatherers go into Lôi Ngô Lâm for fallen struck wood and carry it out for Phượng Minh's workshops; on cloudy days they fish instead.

739.name: Đan Hoàng Quật
739.look: Orange-red workings on the flank of an old volcanic cone high above the sea, the spoil bright as rust.
739.lore: Its realgar is used in alchemy and in charms against snakes and poison. Miners work with cloth over their faces and never stay past noon.

740.name: Thanh Hòa Mạch
740.look: A low rise in the open fields where the rice grows taller and greener than anywhere around it.
740.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein close under the soil. The farmers of Tiêu Giang plant the rise first each year, and the palace takes a share of its grain for seed.

741.name: Tiêu Giang Thôn
741.look: A river-mouth village on stilts among banana groves, fish weirs set across the brown water below.
741.lore: Its people grow bananas and rice and fish the river mouth, and send dried fish up to Trúc Thực Viên for its beasts.

742.name: Cuồng Tượng Nguyên
742.look: Tall grass under the hills trampled into broad paths, with broken trees along its edge.
742.lore: Wild spirit elephants come down from the jungle hills to graze here in the dry season, and a bull in musth will charge anything that moves. Hunters come for tusks; few come twice.

743.name: Bạch Lộ Thôn
743.look: A shore village of thatched houses where white egrets stand in the shallows among the moored boats.
743.lore: Its people fish the shallows and keep water buffalo on the shore grass, and bar their gates in the dry season when the elephants come down.

744.name: Long Não Lâm
744.look: A lowland forest of tall smooth-trunked trees whose air smells sharp and cool even at noon.
744.lore: Its trees give borneol camphor, which Thanh Khê's healers use for wounds and fevers.

745.name: Đằng Khê Thôn
745.look: A jungle village on a slow brook, coils of cut rattan soaking in the water beside the houses.
745.lore: Its people cut rattan and camphor and weave rattan mats and chairs for the ports.

746.name: Ẩn Phàm Trại
746.look: Charred stockade posts in the jungle above a hidden creek, where a boat slip has rotted into the mud.
746.lore: Thôn Hải Môn's shore camp, where its pirates hid boats and stores within reach of the southern coast. Phượng Minh's fleet burned it in 780, a year before the Purge ended at Thôn Hải's own islet.

747.name: Ngô Căn Mạch
747.look: A wild wutong in the jungle with roots spread over a slab of mossy rock, the ground around it springy and warm.
747.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the tree. No one knows who planted a wutong so far into the jungle.

748.name: Ô Mộc Thôn
748.look: A village on low mangrove ground behind an earth bank, with black ebony logs stacked under its eaves.
748.lore: Its people cut ebony in the jungle and fish from the mangrove edge; the wood goes to Thiều Âm for flutes and zither pegs.

749.name: Hắc Ngạc Chử
749.look: A mud shore between jungle and sea, scored with long drag marks and the dark backs of basking crocodiles.
749.lore: Black spirit crocodiles hold the shore and take anything that comes to drink. The village's fishers launch their boats well beyond it.

750.name: Khổng Tước Thôn
750.look: A small jungle-edge village by the sea, bundles of long green-and-gold feathers hanging in its doorways.
750.lore: Its people fish and gather the feathers wild peacocks shed in the jungle, and sell them to fan makers and to Bách Vũ Các.

751.name: Kê Huyết Khoáng
751.look: A small quarry at the jungle's foot where the pale stone is splashed with blood-red cinnabar.
751.lore: Its chicken-blood stone is carved into seals for Phượng Minh's elders. The miners come only in the morning and leave fruit at the jungle edge for the apes.

752.name: Ngô Diệp Trì
752.look: A warm pool in a wood above the tea slopes, its surface carpeted every autumn with broad yellow wutong leaves.
752.lore: Tea pickers bathe here at the end of the season. The leaves are never cleared; the villagers say the phoenix likes the pool as it is.

753.name: Trà Pha Thôn
753.look: A hill village of grey roofs above rows of dark green tea bushes clipped into waist-high hedges.
753.lore: Its tea is carried down to Mạch Điền and the plain; the first picking of spring goes to the palace's dawn rites.

754.name: Triều Tịch Nhãn
754.look: A round rock pool on the shore that fills and empties with the tide, ringed by smooth white stones.
754.lore: A Thủy (water) vein that swells at high tide and fades at low. The fishers say it breathes with the sea, as the lake at Hồ Tâm does.

755.name: Hải Giác Thôn
755.look: A handful of fishing huts on a grassy cape at the end of the coast, with shallow salt pans cut into the flat rock below and boats pulled up in a cleft.
755.lore: Its people fish the currents off the point and boil sea salt in the dry season, and say they live at the corner of the sea. They read the tide by the rock pool on the shore, which fills and empties a little before the sea does.

756.name: Đan Hà Huyệt
756.look: A cleft in a red sandstone outcrop on the hill, its rock warm to the touch even in the rain.
756.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein comes close to the surface here. Phượng Minh's young fire disciples are sent to sit in the cleft for their first winter.

757.name: Thạch Lựu Thôn
757.look: A river village of grey roofs above terraced pomegranate orchards, red with flowers in early summer.
757.lore: Its pomegranates go down to the palace and the markets, and a bride of the village carries one on her wedding day for many children.

758.name: Xích Thổ Thang
758.look: A hot spring in a hollow of red badland clay, its water opaque and rust-coloured, with gullies of bare red earth running down to it.
758.lore: Herders from Đan Kiều soak their stiff joints here after the horse fairs, and its water stains skin red for days. Phượng Minh's fire disciples say the iron in the clay warms the blood, and come in winter.

759.name: Đan Kiều Trấn
759.look: A walled river town on the edge of the steppe, its two halves joined by a humped bridge lacquered bright red.
759.lore: Herders bring horses, goats and hides to its market, and Phượng Minh's disciples cross the bridge on the road north. The palace relacquers the bridge every ten years.

760.name: Hồng Lang Cương
760.look: A forested ridge where rust-red wolves can be seen at dusk slipping between the trees.
760.lore: Packs of red spirit wolves hunt the forest and the sheep. They whistle to each other instead of howling, and the shepherds listen for it.

761.name: Mục Dương Thôn
761.look: Stone sheepfolds and low houses by a river on the upland grass, big dogs lying at every gate.
761.lore: Its shepherds sell wool down the river and keep their dogs against the red wolves.

762.name: Thanh Minh Lĩnh
762.look: A bare ridge above the bamboo where any shout comes back clearly three times.
762.lore: Young disciples of Phượng Minh practise their first sword cries here. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

763.name: Ngô Miêu Thôn
763.look: A village by the palace road ringed by beds of young wutong in neat rows, each tagged with a strip of red cloth.
763.lore: Since Phượng Minh's founding its people have raised the wutong for the palace terraces. Every sapling that leaves the village has a red tag tied by the child who watered it.

764.name: Huyền Tiêu Phong
764.look: A thin spire of rock above the singing ravine, pierced near its top by a hole the wind whistles through.
764.lore: Its whistle carries far on stormy nights, and the palace's elders tell disciples not to follow it. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

765.name: Xích Ngọc Khoáng
765.look: A narrow cut in grey rock high under the clouds, its floor scattered with chips of red-veined jade.
765.lore: Its red jade is carved into the palace's rite vessels and the pendants of its elders.

766.name: Lạc Vũ Phong
766.look: A high cloud-wrapped summit where a flat ledge is strewn with feathers blown up from the valleys.
766.lore: Once a year Phượng Minh's disciples climb to gather the feathers for the palace's rites. Its qi runs Thổ (earth).

767.name: Hồng Bích Nhai
767.look: A long cliff of red rock above the jungle, streaked black where the rain runs down, with a ledge near its top where the old mountain road once ran.
767.lore: The cinnamon cutters of Nhục Quế steer home by it when the jungle closes in, and the road along its ledge once led to the empty market town of Tiêu Sơn. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire), warm in the red rock.

768.name: Tiêu Sơn Thị
768.look: Grass-grown walls on a high shoulder of rock, with rows of stone stall bases lining a single street.
768.lore: A mountain market town of Cửu Thiều Cung where pipes and flutes were sold to the palace and the plain. After the palace fell in 340 its people left within a year, like those of Vân Môn, and the town was never resettled.

769.name: Nhục Quế Thôn
769.look: A jungle village where rolled strips of bark dry on racks in every yard and the air smells sweet and hot.
769.lore: Its people strip cinnamon from the hill trees and sell it in Thanh Khê to the ships.

770.name: Quần Sài Cương
770.look: A low grassy rise pocked with dens, where gaunt red-brown jackals watch the road.
770.lore: Spirit jackals hunt in packs here and follow travellers at a distance. The goatherds bring their flocks in before dark.

771.name: Hoàng Lương Thôn
771.look: A dry hill village of mud-walled houses among fields of tall yellow millet.
771.lore: Its people grow millet and herd goats. Travellers who nap at its inn while the millet cooks are teased that they will dream a whole life before supper.

772.name: Đan Sa Quật
772.look: A guarded grotto in red rock below the ridge, its walls glittering crimson in torchlight.
772.lore: Phượng Minh digs cinnabar here near the vein, under guard since the war of 1150. Its cinnabar goes to the palace's alchemists.

773.name: Liệp Điêu Nhai
773.look: A cliff above the meadows whitened with droppings, great stick nests on its ledges.
773.lore: Spirit golden eagles nest here and take lambs and goats from the hills. Young cultivators climb for the chicks and seldom manage it.

774.name: Phong Mật Thôn
774.look: A hill village among flowering meadows, its walls lined with log beehives.
774.lore: Its beekeepers sell honey and wax to Lai Nghi and Hoàng Vân, and Lễ Tuyền buys its honey for wine.

775.name: Hàm Ôn Tuyền
775.look: A warm spring on the flat steppe, its rim crusted white with salt.
775.lore: Its water is salt and warm, and the laver gatherers soak their cracked hands in it.

776.name: Hải Diêm Trấn
776.look: Burned walls on the shore among old salt pans, the pans cracked and grown over with samphire.
776.lore: A salt town of the southern gulf, burned by Thôn Hải's pirates in 764, two years after Châu Lệ Cảng. Its salt makers never came back, and their pans lie dry.

777.name: Tử Thái Thôn
777.look: A low shore village where dark sheets of laver dry on bamboo frames along the beach.
777.lore: Its people gather laver from the rocks at low tide and sell it pressed and dried.

778.name: Xích Nghĩ Nguyên
778.look: Grassland studded with red earth mounds taller than a man, the grass around them stripped bare.
778.lore: Spirit red ants the size of a hand build here, and a column of them can strip an ox to bone. The salt makers burn the grass between their bank and the mounds each dry season.

779.name: Hàm Trạch Thôn
779.look: A village behind an earth bank below the tide line, its salt pans shining white beyond the houses.
779.lore: Its people make salt in shallow pans and sell it up the coast; the bank is raised a little every winter.

780.name: Chu Đồng Khoáng
780.look: Open copper workings stepped into red badland rock below the peak, the spoil heaps streaked green and a line of mule tracks winding down toward the plain.
780.lore: Miners come up from the plain in the dry season and leave before the rains wash the badlands out. Its copper goes to Lai Nghi, where it is cast into the bronze bells of the nine tiers.

781.name: Xích Vũ Phong
781.look: A bare red peak above the badlands, its rock shading from orange to deep crimson, its summit split into thin blades like the feathers of a raised wing.
781.lore: The copper miners below say a red bird dropped one feather here and the mountain grew from it. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire), dry and fierce, and Phượng Minh's fire disciples cross the badlands to sit on it in the hottest month.

782.name: Ô Ngọc Khoáng
782.look: A summer working high on the mountain where black jade is cut from grey rock.
782.lore: Its ink-black jade is carved into seals and inkstones for Phượng Minh's scribes.

783.name: Bích Tiêu Phong
783.look: A high grey peak behind the plain, its forested shoulders rising to bare rock and its top usually wrapped in a single white cloud.
783.lore: The rice farmers of Hoàng Vân read the weather by its cloud: when it lifts, they cut; when it thickens, they cover the threshing floors. Its qi runs Kim (metal) through the hard grey rock.

784.name: Vân Thạch Khoáng
784.look: A marble quarry at the shore, its white blocks veined with grey like clouds.
784.lore: Its cloud stone paves the courts of Hoàng Vân's counting hall and goes by boat along the gulf.

785.name: Ngọa Ngưu Sơn
785.look: A broad forested mountain shaped like an ox lying with its head on its forelegs.
785.lore: The herders of Hoàng Ngưu bow to it when they drive their oxen west. Its qi runs Thổ (earth).

786.name: Thần Chung Phong
786.look: A tall peak above folded forest, its bare top shaped like an upturned bell.
786.lore: On still mornings the bells of Lai Nghi's nine tiers echo back from it across the plain. Its qi runs Kim (metal).

787.name: Đông Thăng Nhãn
787.look: A round patch of bare earth in the grass, warm at dawn and cold by noon.
787.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein that is strongest at sunrise. Phượng Minh's fire disciples come to sit in it before dawn.

788.name: Nhật Xuất Thôn
788.look: A fishing village on the far eastern shore, every door facing the sea.
788.lore: Its fishers launch at first light and say they see the sun before anyone else on the plain.

789.name: Kim Ô Phong
789.look: A bare peak above the western gulf whose sunward face of pale rock shines gold at noon, too hot to touch in summer.
789.lore: It is named for the golden crow that lives in the sun, and gulf sailors use its noon glare to find the coast. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire), and Phượng Minh's fire disciples sit on its sunward face at midday until they can bear it no longer.

790.name: Thiết Giác Nguyên
790.look: Wide grass where a herd of huge dark buffalo grazes, their horns grey as iron.
790.lore: Wild spirit buffalo whose horns can split a cart. Hải Mục's herders keep their cattle well away from the herd's bulls.

791.name: Hải Mục Thôn
791.look: A shore village behind a low dyke, its cattle grazing the salt grass right down to the tide.
791.lore: Its herders say salt grass makes the sweetest beef, and they fish when the cattle are in.

792.name: Hậu Thổ Huyệt
792.look: A low earth mound in the steppe topped by a small altar of piled stones.
792.lore: A Thổ (earth) vein. The shepherds of Thâm Tỉnh pour the first water of every new well on its altar.

793.name: Thâm Tỉnh Thôn
793.look: A steppe village gathered round a single deep stone well with a long sweep pole.
793.lore: Its people live by the well and their sheep. The well is so deep that a dropped stone is counted to ten before it splashes.

794.name: Phủ Điền Lĩnh
794.look: A high ridge of grass and rock whose crest bends forward over the rice plain like a bowed head, with the broken sea fort on its far side.
794.lore: Farmers say it bows to the first rice that Thủy Điền plants each spring, and they bow back. Its qi runs Thổ (earth), heavy and slow, and the fort's old garrison said it was the steadiest ground on the coast.

795.name: Liệu Phàm Bảo
795.look: A broken stone fort on the seaward slope, its signal tower toppled and its seaward wall gone into the gulf.
795.lore: Phượng Minh raised it in the pirate years to watch for Thôn Hải's sails. After the Purge the garrison was withdrawn in 790, and the empty fort crumbled.

796.name: Ngân Lộ Khoáng
796.look: Narrow adits enter a grey mountain wall above the steppe, the rock around their mouths beaded with grey drops of weathered silver ore.
796.lore: Silver has been dug here since 520. The miners say the seam sweats fresh silver like dew each night, so they work only before sunrise.

797.name: Vọng Vũ Phong
797.look: A tall, lone grey peak stands up out of the dry steppe, its summit wrapped in cloud while the grass below it is brown.
797.lore: Herders of the rain-shadow steppe watch this peak to know when rain will reach them, and drive their flocks toward it when its cloud darkens. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

798.name: Hưởng Lôi Bảo
798.look: On a mountain spur above the western pass, a square fort of dark stone stands broken open, a round drum platform still raised over its gate.
798.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built this watch fort over its western approach, and its drum answered the thunder of the peaks. When the Tower was raised on this ground in 380 the garrison went home to the Gate, and the Tower never manned it again.

799.name: Thạch Nhân Phong
799.look: A tall pillar of weathered rock on a steppe ridge, shaped from the west like a man standing with his head bowed against the wind.
799.lore: Travellers crossing the dry waste steer by it and leave a mouthful of water at its foot for luck. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

800.name: Hoàng Sa Đỉnh
800.look: A broad summit over the steppe, its upper slopes heaped with wind-blown yellow sand that drifts like snow against the rocks.
800.lore: The hot wind of the plain carries sand all the way up and piles it on the crest. Loose cultivators of Earth (Thổ) qi climb it to sit out the sandstorms.

801.name: Kính Thủy Đàm
801.look: A small clear pool in the steppe grass, fed by a channel from the larger grey lake nearby, so still that it holds the Tower's cone upside down.
801.lore: Unlike Tàn Hà Hồ beside it, no lotus has ever grown in this pool. The herders of Thảo Lư water their goats here, and the Tower's disciples come to look at the reflection rather than the Tower.

802.name: Thảo Lư Thôn
802.look: A scatter of low thatched huts and stone goat pens on the steppe slope below the Tower's cone, with felt rugs drying on every roof.
802.lore: Herders settled here in 620 to sell milk and felt to the Tower. Since 906 they keep the lamp shutters closed on the side that faces the cone, though no one has ever told them to.

803.name: Bích Thảo Mạch
803.look: A long fold of hillside stays a deep blue-green all year, with a faint shimmer over the grass on still mornings.
803.lore: A modest Wood (Mộc) vein above the camphor village. Loose cultivators (tán tu) rent rooms from the distillers to sit here and pay in labour at the stills.

804.name: Chương Thụ Thôn
804.look: A forest village of steep-roofed houses around a smoking row of copper stills, the air so sharp with camphor that insects will not cross the fence.
804.lore: The camphor distillers of Chương Thụ have worked here since 590. Sect libraries across the south keep their books in camphor chests, and the village sells to the Tower first.

805.name: Dã Trư Cương
805.look: A low forested ridge whose earth is turned over everywhere as if ploughed, with mud wallows in every hollow.
805.lore: A herd of spirit-touched wild boars led by a great tusker roots across this ridge and raids the pulp pits of Trúc Chỉ in the wet season. Hunters prize the tusker's bristles for brushes and have never taken him.

806.name: Phi Anh Quán
806.look: In the broadleaf forest the low walls of a small abbey stand among wild peach trees, its stone courtyard carpeted with petals each spring.
806.lore: When Lạc Anh Phái broke apart in 610, a handful of its disciples came inland and founded this abbey in its name. It lasted eight years: Lạc Hà and Thính Vũ disciples passed through in the Petal Shore fighting, and when they had gone the abbey was empty. Its peach trees still flower.

807.name: Trúc Chỉ Thôn
807.look: Stone pulp pits and drying frames hung with sheets of pale paper fill the clearing around a village of bamboo houses.
807.lore: Paper has been made here from bamboo pulp since 650, and since the Night Rain Market opened its oiled awnings have come from Trúc Chỉ. The papermakers oil each sheet twice, for the market's rain must never touch the goods.

808.name: Mai Vũ Tuyền
808.look: On a grassy hilltop a ring of stones holds a shallow spring that overflows in the plum-rain season and shrinks to a damp hollow by autumn.
808.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein that waxes and wanes with the rains. Cultivators time their retreats to the early summer rains, when its qi runs strongest.

809.name: Mộc Miên Thôn
809.look: A hill village of grey-tile houses under huge kapok trees, whose red flowers fall on the roofs in spring and whose white floss blows through the lanes in summer.
809.lore: The village gathers kapok floss for quilts and padded jackets, and the Tower's servants winter in jackets stuffed here. A bride of Mộc Miên brings a quilt as her dowry, and its weight is talked about for years.

810.name: Thanh Đăng Trấn
810.look: On the steppe below the Tower's mountains lie the walls and empty lanes of a small town, its doorways still fitted with rusted iron lamp hooks.
810.lore: Thanh Đăng was the lamp-makers' town that lit the Tower's windows with blue-glazed lamps for five centuries. When the lamps went dark in 906 its trade died with them, and by 930 the last families had moved to Hạnh Hoa Thị.

811.name: Xuân Nha Nhãn
811.look: On a hillside above the tea gardens a single wild tea bush grows taller than a house, and the ground around it puts out new buds even in winter.
811.lore: A small spirit eye of Wood (Mộc) qi. Its leaves are picked once a year and sent to the Tower, and the pickers of Vũ Tiền may not drink them.

812.name: Vũ Tiền Thôn
812.look: Neat tea gardens climb the grassy hills in green steps around a village of whitewashed houses and charcoal roasting sheds.
812.lore: Since 700 the village has picked its first tea in the days before the spring rains, and Vũ Tiền tea is drunk in the Tower itself. A picker who lets rain touch the first leaves gives up her share of the season.

813.name: Trúc Căn Huyệt
813.look: In a bamboo grove on a hill a hollow opens among the roots, and the stems around it lean inward as if toward a fire.
813.lore: A Wood (Mộc) vein that runs through the root mat of the whole grove. The Tower's outer disciples stop here on the road south, and each leaves a cut bamboo tally with a name on it.

814.name: Tượng Lộ Thôn
814.look: A village of tall stilted houses along a broad, deeply rutted road, with elephant stalls of heavy timber larger than the houses.
814.lore: The village has kept working elephants since 730, hauling logs from the forest to the rivers. Each child is given a calf to grow up with, and the two work together all their lives.

815.name: Thiết Vũ Khoáng
815.look: Shallow pits and spoil heaps scar a steep mountain flank, where the rain has washed loose iron ore down the rock in dark streaks.
815.lore: Seasonal miners dig red iron ore here in the dry months and carry it down to the Tower's smiths. The pits close when the storms come, and the ore each season's rain washes down is gathered first the next year.

816.name: Chu Nham Đỉnh
816.look: A blunt summit of vermilion rock rises over the northern badlands, banded red and ochre and bare of any plant.
816.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies heavy on this crest. Herders say the rain stops at its foot, and prospectors use its red crown to find the iron workings below.

817.name: Dung Thụ Lâm
817.look: Just inland from the river mouth a handful of enormous banyans have spread into a whole wood, their hanging roots grown into a maze of grey pillars.
817.lore: Lạc Triều carries its dead here and ties their names to the hanging roots. When a new root reaches the ground, the villagers say an ancestor has come home.

818.name: Lạc Triều Thôn
818.look: Stilt houses of bamboo and thatch stand over the mud at a river mouth, with fish-drying racks and crab traps stacked along the walkways.
818.lore: The villagers go out at every ebb to work the channels and come back before the flood. They mark the tides on a carved post, and anyone who moves it must feast the whole village.

819.name: Hương Lệ Lâm
819.look: Inland from the coast, old agarwood trees stand in the grass, many scarred with cuts that weep dark, fragrant resin.
819.lore: Agarwood forms only in wounded trees, and the cutters of Da Âm wound them carefully and wait decades. Hồng Đậu Trang buys the resin by weight in silver, and the village does not ask what it is burned for.

820.name: Da Âm Thôn
820.look: A shore village of palm-thatched houses under tall coconut palms, with long coils of brown coir rope drying on frames along the beach.
820.lore: The village has twisted coir rope since 680 and sells it to the ships at Thu Trì. Its children climb palms before they can swim, and its boats are sewn together with its own rope.

821.name: Độc Thiềm Lâm
821.look: A wet jungle hollow full of black pools, loud at night with a deep croaking, the leaves around the water spotted with yellow slime.
821.lore: Toads the size of dogs breed in these pools, and the largest, a spirit beast the villagers call the Old Mother, has not been seen in years but still sings. Their venom is a staple of Hồng Đậu Trang's poisons.

822.name: Lăng Đường Thôn
822.look: A coastal village of low houses on banks between brackish ponds, the water dark green with floating water-chestnut leaves.
822.lore: Villagers harvest water chestnuts from tubs pushed across the ponds and fish the channels to the sea. They also bring in poison-toad skins from the jungle for Hồng Đậu Trang, wearing gloves of oiled leather.

823.name: Ủng Vân Phong
823.look: A forested summit in the far north-east, its moss-hung upper slopes buried in a slow cloud that clings even on clear days.
823.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the mist on its crown. Thính Vũ's disciples climb it to train their hearing blind, learning to fight by the drip of the mist from the leaves.

824.name: Thiết Tú Trì
824.look: In the cracked badlands a steaming pool of rust-red water lies in a basin of iron-stained rock, crusted orange at its edges.
824.lore: The water tastes of iron and is said to harden the bones of those who bathe in it. Miners from the malachite workings soak here after each shift.

825.name: Lục Vũ Khoáng
825.look: Open trenches in the red badlands expose seams of banded green malachite, bright as peacock feathers against the rock.
825.lore: The mine yields copper and malachite, which is ground into the green paint of the south's temple roofs. Its miners walk in from Hạn Tỉnh and carry their water.

826.name: Lôi Cốt Phong
