826.look: A narrow, jagged peak of dark rock above the badland cliffs, its crest scored with black lightning tracks like veins.
826.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in the dark rock, and the lightning finds it every storm. The Tower's sword disciples leave their blades on the crest overnight in thunderstorms.

827.name: Hồi Lôi Phong
827.look: A grey peak over a ring of ravines, its walls curved so that each thunderclap rolls back from it two and three times.
827.lore: Metal (Kim) qi lies in its grey rock. The Tower's disciples test their hearing here by counting the echoes, and say a master can hear five.

828.name: Hôi Lang Cương
828.look: A rocky spur above the steppe, its boulders worn smooth where wolves have lain, with bones scattered in the grass below.
828.lore: A pack of grey wolves under a spirit-touched leader dens here and takes foals from Mã Lan each spring. The herders leave the leader alone and hunt only the young wolves.

829.name: Mã Lan Thôn
829.look: A high steppe village of stone houses and long dry-stone horse pens, with herds of small shaggy horses grazing the slope below.
829.lore: Mã Lan has bred hill horses since 560, and the Tower's messengers ride them on the mountain roads. Each spring the best foal is led up to the Tower.

830.name: Vũ Giác Phong
830.look: Two bare horns of rock rise side by side from one mountain shoulder north of the Tower, the gap between them just wide enough to walk through.
830.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi gathers between the horns. Herders say whoever walks through the gap in a storm comes out a year older.

831.name: Vũ Đồng Khoáng
831.look: Terraced cuts in a red badland slope expose dull red copper ore, with a small smelting floor of blackened stone below.
831.lore: The Tower's smiths take copper from here for their bronze rain-chains and bells. They quench the castings in storm rain, and say bronze quenched dry will not sing.

832.name: Thụ Lôi Đỉnh
832.look: A rounded summit east of the Tower's cone, its crown fused into black, glassy rock by countless strikes.
832.lore: The Metal (Kim) qi in its rock draws lightning more often than any other summit in Tiêu Vũ Lâm. The Tower's disciples sit just below the crown in storms to feel the strikes through the stone.

833.name: Dạ Ngọc Khoáng
833.look: A cramped tunnel mouth in a grey mountain wall, its spoil heap glittering with chips of black, glossy stone.
833.lore: Black jade (mặc ngọc) has been cut here since 820 and carved in Thu Trì into seals and sword fittings. Since the lamps went dark the Tower's masters favour it, because it holds no gleam of lamp or moon.

834.name: Thụy Ngưu Sơn
834.look: A long, humped mountain over the steppe, shaped like a resting ox, with grass on its back and bare rock on its flanks.
834.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies deep in it. The herders of Hạn Tỉnh say that if the ox ever stands up, the well will run dry.

835.name: Hạn Tỉnh Thôn
835.look: A steppe village of flat-roofed stone houses around a single wide well, its rope so long that a mule turns the windlass.
835.lore: The well was dug in 610, and it takes a mule half the morning to raise a day's water. The village keeps goats and millet and sends its young men to the mines in the ridges.

836.name: Hồng Văn Khoáng
836.look: Shallow galleries in a mountain foot expose pale stone shot through with bright red veins, like blood in milk.
836.lore: Chicken-blood stone (kê huyết thạch) is cut here for seals, and a seal of it is a gift fit for an elder. The red is cinnabar, and the cutters wear masks against the dust.

837.name: Hắc Diệu Phong
837.look: A blunt peak over the scorched badlands, its crown fused by lightning into black glass that gleams after rain.
837.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its fused crown. Herders say a storm that does not strike it is not a real storm.

838.name: Lôi Ngân Khoáng
838.look: Adits in a mountain slope above the high grass, their spoil sparkling with flakes of bright silver ore.
838.lore: The silver here is found in seams that lightning has opened, so the miners follow the storms. Silver from it is used in the Tower's warding talismans.

839.name: Lôi Chủy Phong
839.look: A hooked spur of bare rock juts from the northern ridge like the beak of a stooping eagle.
839.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers at its tip, and the lightning strikes the beak first. Eagles nest under its hook and are said to fly out into the storms.

840.name: Hạ Lôi Thành
840.look: In the mountain hollows beside the cone, the tops of thick walls and gate towers stick up out of grey ash hardened to stone.
840.lore: Khải Lôi Môn built this upland city on the cone's flank as its western market. In 352 the cone woke and buried it in ash, and the Gate never rebuilt; the cone fell quiet again, and in 380 Phó Tiêu Tương raised her tower on it.

841.name: Hậu Thổ Nhãn
841.look: On the dry steppe beside the Tower's cone, a round hollow of ash-grey soil lies warm to the touch, with tough grass growing in rings around it.
841.lore: A spirit eye of Earth (Thổ) qi rising through the old ash of the cone. The Tower's outer disciples keep it, and sit here in the dry months when the rain on the cone is too loud for them.

842.name: Thanh Minh Phong
842.look: A clean grey summit over the ravines, its rock washed pale and sharp by the storms.
842.lore: In the clear days after a storm it stands out so sharp that the farmers on the coast can count its ledges. Its rock holds Metal (Kim) qi.

843.name: Lập Xuân Phong
843.look: A broad peak above the stone-furrowed steppe, where the first green of the year shows on its southern face.
843.lore: Farmers below begin the year's work when its southern face turns green. Its rock holds Earth (Thổ) qi.

844.name: Thanh Hoạt Khoáng
844.look: A low quarry face at the mountain's foot, its pale green stone so soft that the walls shine where hands have rubbed them.
844.lore: Soapstone from here is carved into seals and pill boxes and ground for alchemists' powders. It is carried down to Lãng Hoa on mules.

845.name: Vũ Bút Phong
845.look: Three sheer points of rock stand in a row on the high crest, like the points of a scholar's brush rest.
845.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in the cliffs. Scholars in Lãng Hoa say a student who can see all three points from the city on the morning of an examination will pass.

846.name: Ám Thiết Khoáng
846.look: Narrow cuts in a high slope expose seams of dull black ore, and the spoil stains the scree black down to the valley.
846.lore: The dark iron ore here is smelted for blades that do not shine. The Tower's masters have favoured it since 906.

847.name: Thùy Liêm Phong
847.look: A tall summit in the middle of the range from which dark clouds seem to hang like curtains on its southern side.
847.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the clouds that hang on it. The Tower's disciples read the coming weather of the whole south from its curtains.

848.name: Ban Văn Khoáng
848.look: A cut in the highland slope exposes ore banded yellow and dark grey, like the stripes of the crouching ridge nearby.
848.lore: The banded iron ore is good, but the beasts of Phục Hổ Cương make it dangerous, and miners come only in large parties. They leave a goat at the ridge's foot before each season's work.

849.name: Thanh Thạch Bảo
849.look: A small fort of blue-grey stone on the highland road, its gate torn off and its walls scored with deep claw marks.
849.lore: The Tower kept this fort on the highland road for five centuries. In 1041 its garrison was called east to the Thunder Vein War, and the tiger-kind beasts of Phục Hổ Cương came down and took it; it was never manned again.

850.name: Dẫn Lôi Phong
850.look: A sharp, bare peak above the forges of Kinh Điện, its crest bristling with old iron rods driven into the rock.
850.lore: Khải Lôi's smiths drove rods into its crest to lead the lightning down to the forges, and Thính Vũ's smiths keep them. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on it with every storm.

851.name: Vân Hải Đỉnh
851.look: A high summit in the eastern range that stands above the clouds on most mornings, an island of grey rock in a white sea.
851.lore: Water (Thủy) qi gathers in the cloud sea around it. The hunters of Tàng Trập Động climb it on the eve of Kinh Trập to watch for the first thunder.

852.name: Thủ Động Trại
852.look: On a ledge near the cave of Tàng Trập Động, the low dry-stone walls of a stockade enclose a hearth and a row of collapsed huts.
852.lore: Khải Lôi Môn kept wardens here to watch the cave mouth and keep order among the hunters on the day of Kinh Trập. When the Gate fell, its wardens went home, and the hunters have kept their own order since.

853.name: Hấp Thiết Khoáng
853.look: A cut in a grey mountain flank where rusted iron tools still cling to the rock face, and the old spoil heaps bristle with filings.
853.lore: Lightning has made the ore here into lodestone, fit for compasses and array-makers' needles. Few know the cut; the miners who found it left their iron tools stuck to the rock and never came back with bronze.

854.name: Ngưng Lôi Phong
854.look: A heavy grey summit at the head of the cloud valleys, often hidden under a lid of dark cloud that flickers from inside.
854.lore: Storms gather over it for hours before they break. Its rock holds Metal (Kim) qi, and herders on the steppe take its flicker as the warning to drive their flocks down.

855.name: Thủy Tinh Khoáng
855.look: Low, abandoned galleries cut into the cliff above the surf, their walls studded with clear six-sided crystals beaded with sea damp.
855.lore: Rock crystal from here would make array focuses and scholars' lenses, but the rope path to the galleries broke in a gale and no digger has gone down since.

856.name: Vọng Triều Phong
856.look: A steep peak rising straight from the sea cliffs, its upper rocks streaked white by the nesting seabirds.
856.lore: Fishers along the coast watch its foot to read the tides when the mist lifts. Water (Thủy) qi rises to it off the sea.

857.name: Hải Giác Phong
857.look: A sheer headland peak over booming sea caves, the waves breaking white on its foot even in calm weather.
857.lore: It is the last land the Lãng Hoa fishers see when they sail east, and they bow to it on leaving. Water (Thủy) qi gathers in its spray.

858.name: Giảng Đạo Phong
858.look: A flat-topped peak above the pebble sluices, its summit a broad bare platform like a preaching terrace.
858.lore: The pickers of Vũ Hoa say the master whose sermon made the flowers fall as rain preached from this summit. Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its rock, and pebbles washed down from it are said to be the brightest.

859.name: Hộ Khoáng Bảo
859.look: Low on the slope below the pebble beds, the walls of a guard fort lie half buried under a great tongue of fallen rock and mud.
859.lore: The Tower built the fort in 505 to guard the road to Vũ Hoa Khoáng. A storm in 1102 brought the slope down on its lower court, and the guard moved up to the mine itself.

860.name: Phi Lôi Phong
860.look: A high, sharp summit over the purple-gold cliffs, where the lightning seems to leap from it to the clouds rather than fall.
860.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs through it from the purple-gold seams below. Miners of Tử Kim watch its crest and leave the tunnels when the leaping lightning starts.

861.name: Lôi Tinh Khoáng
861.look: On a high slope below the split summit, diggers break open the sand and scree to pull out glassy, branching tubes fused by lightning.
861.lore: Thunder crystal (lôi tinh), sand fused by lightning, is gathered here for thunder talismans and arrays. The diggers come only between storms and leave their iron at the bottom of the trail.

862.name: Nghênh Lôi Trại
862.look: High on the shoulder of Liệt Khuyết Phong, a ring of fire-blackened stone walls encloses the hearths of a camp, open to the sky.
862.lore: Khải Lôi's disciples camped here to wait for the storms before climbing the summit to invite the lightning. When the Gate fell in 480 the camp was left to the weather, and the Tower's disciples now pass it on their way to drill.

863.name: Tử Tinh Khoáng
863.look: A guarded cut in a bare high ridge, its walls lined with violet crystal that brightens faintly when thunder rolls.
863.lore: The amethyst grows along the edges of the Thunder vein and takes some of its colour. Lệ Tiêu Hồn allows the mine to be worked only under the Tower's guard, and every stone is counted.

864.name: Tân Lục Mạch
864.look: A strip of meadow above the hat village where the grass is always the bright green of a new spring.
864.lore: A Wood (Mộc) vein kept for the Tower's outer disciples. Villagers cut palm leaf on its edge and say hats woven from it never fade.

865.name: Đấu Lạp Thôn
865.look: A bamboo village where every porch is stacked with conical hats of split bamboo and palm leaf, drying in rows like mushrooms.
865.lore: The village has woven rain hats since 640, and a Đấu Lạp hat is said to keep its wearer dry for twenty rainy seasons. The Tower's servants wear them, and their brims are left plain and undyed.

866.name: Lạc Nhật Phong
866.look: A peak of red badland rock above the salt-wind plain that burns crimson at sunset.
866.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its red rock. Salt-gatherers on the coast stop work when its crown goes dark.

867.name: Vọng Phàm Bảo
867.look: On a mountain spur above the coast, the square walls of a fort look out to sea, with a fallen signal tower at one corner.
867.lore: The Tower built the fort in the pirate years to watch for Thôn Hải's sails. After the Pirate Purge there was nothing left to watch for, and its garrison was sent home in 810.

868.name: Lôi Trụ Phong
868.look: A very tall, slender summit of pale grey-green rock rising like a pillar above the gullies of the eastern range.
868.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs up it like water up a reed. Cloudbursts break on it first, and the torrents from its flanks are heard for miles.

869.name: Sơn Khẩu Trại
869.look: A stockade of stone and timber at the mouth of a high pass, split in two by a fresh crack in the ground that runs straight through its gate.
869.lore: The Tower kept a small guard here on the eastern pass for six centuries. The earthquake of 1199 that raised the isle at Hà Châu split the stockade from end to end, and the guard has not been sent back.

870.name: Tình Tiêu Phong
870.look: A high summit that rises above the joined clouds of its ridge into clear blue sky on most afternoons.
870.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its clear crown. Xuyên Lâm's guides take it as their mark, for it can be seen from the gate above every cloud.

871.name: Đảm Phàn Khoáng
871.look: Wet galleries at the foot of the grey slope drip blue water, and crusts of bright blue crystal coat their walls.
871.lore: Blue vitriol is scraped from the galleries for dyers, alchemists and the poison-makers of Hồng Đậu Trang. The miners' hands are stained blue for life.

872.name: Hạc Đầu Phong
872.look: A peak of pale, crumbling rock whose top is white as an old man's head against the grey ridges around it.
872.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its pale rock. Herders say it turned white the night Khải Lôi's last head fell, though older songs already call it white.

873.name: Sa Kim Khoáng
873.look: Stream beds below the drum peak are dammed with rock into little pools, and pans of black sand glitter with gold flakes.
873.lore: The storms cut into the gold-bearing rock above, and the streams wash the gold down. Panners work only after storms and pay a tithe to the guards of the vein.

874.name: Thần Cổ Phong
874.look: A massive round-shouldered summit beside the Thunder vein, its hollow rock booming like a drum when thunder strikes it.
874.lore: Metal (Kim) qi fills its hollow rock. The guards of Kinh Lôi Mạch say the peak warns them of storms a day before they come.

875.name: Thủ Lôi Bảo
875.look: On a lower ridge near the vein stands the burned shell of a fort, its gate tower collapsed and its stones cracked by fire.
875.lore: The Tower built this fort to guard Kinh Lôi Mạch soon after it took the thunder mountains. In 1042, during the Thunder Vein War, Phượng Minh's disciples took it and burned it, and when the vein was kept the Tower built its new guard higher on the ridge.

876.name: Vũ Hoàn Khoáng
876.look: Pits in the riverbank at the mountain's foot turn up nodules of grey stone that split open into banded red and white agate.
876.lore: Agate from here is polished in Không Mông for beads and the counters of games. Diggers say the bands are the rings of old storms.

877.name: Bích Loa Phong
877.look: A small round peak above the misty ravines, forested green to its top like a coiled snail shell.
877.lore: Wood (Mộc) qi gathers in its forest. Charcoal burners never cut on it, saying it is the forest's own pillow.

878.name: Huyết Thiết Khoáng
878.look: Open cuts in a mountain slope expose blood-red iron ore, and a smelter below sends up a column of grey smoke.
878.lore: The red ore is smelted with charcoal from Ô Diêu and sent down to the Tower's smiths. The miners' clothes are red with dust, and they are called the red men in Không Mông.

879.name: Hỏa Quan Phong
879.look: A ragged crest of red-brown rock rises over the kilns in a row of points like a rooster's comb.
879.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its red rock. The kiln village says a fire lit when its comb glows at dawn will burn clean.

880.name: Ô Diêu Thôn
880.look: A hill village of soot-darkened houses around a row of domed earth kilns, smoke drifting through the trees in every direction.
880.lore: The village has burned charcoal since 680 for the smelters of the iron mine above. Its children are said to be born grey, and they wash in the stream only at New Year.

881.name: Mộ Vũ Phong
881.look: A forested peak among the green screens, gathering a cloud each afternoon that breaks into rain at dusk.
881.lore: Wood (Mộc) qi gathers in its forest. Woodcutters work its slopes only until the cloud forms, and are home by the first drops.

882.name: Nam Mộc Lâm
882.look: On the grassy hills above the village stand tall, straight nanmu trees with golden-grained trunks, widely spaced like the pillars of a hall.
882.lore: Nanmu timber does not rot in the rain, and the Tower's halls are framed with it. Each tree cut must be marked with the Tower's seal first.

883.name: Xuân Duẩn Thôn
883.look: A bamboo village where racks of split bamboo shoots dry over smoky fires under every eave.
883.lore: Each spring the whole village digs bamboo shoots before they break the soil and dries them for the cities. A shoot left to grow by mistake is tied with a red cord and never cut.

884.name: Xích Túc Cốc
884.look: A damp bamboo valley where the leaf litter rustles constantly, and red-legged centipedes as long as a man's arm move under it.
884.lore: Spirit-touched centipedes breed in the rotting bamboo, and their master is said to be longer than a boat. Xuyên Lâm's apprentices learn here to strike with the staff before they see what moves.

885.name: Dẫn Lộ Thôn
885.look: A village of bamboo houses at the foot of Xuyên Lâm's long stair, with worn guide staffs leaning by every door.
885.lore: The households of Xuyên Lâm's guides have lived here since the school was founded. When a guide does not come home, the family hangs the returned staff over the door and leaves it there.

886.name: Phạt Trúc Thôn
886.look: A bamboo village on a low hill, its yards stacked high with cut poles and its paths ringing with the sound of blades.
886.lore: Bamboo cutters have lived here since 700 and sell poles in every town of the coast. They leave the clearing of stumps in Đả Diệp Lâm alone, and in a downpour they talk in hand signs.

887.name: Hải Trúc Lâm
887.look: A grove of tough, salt-stunted bamboo on the shore, its stems silvered by the sea wind.
887.lore: The salt-hard bamboo makes the best fish traps on the coast. Cố Trạch cuts it in winter and soaks it in the marsh for a year.

888.name: Cố Trạch Thôn
888.look: A huddle of reed-thatched houses on stilts at the edge of the marsh, with the black walls of Lôi Trạch Thành visible across the water.
888.lore: Eel fishers settled here in 760, three centuries after the city burned. They do not enter the ruin after dark, and on the thunder-day they beat drums with the people of Không Mông.

889.name: Triều Tịch Tuyền
889.look: In the meadow behind the shore a stone-rimmed spring rises and sinks twice a day, in time with the sea out of sight.
889.lore: A Water (Thủy) vein that breathes with the tides. Cultivators sit here at high water, when its qi is strongest, and leave at the ebb.

890.name: Tảo Điền Thôn
890.look: A shore village where rows of bamboo frames stand in the shallows, hung with dark seaweed, and purple sheets dry on mats along the beach.
890.lore: The village has farmed laver since 820, and its dried sheets are sold in Không Mông and Lãng Hoa. Children here are taught to read the tides before their letters.

891.name: Lệ Chi Lâm
891.look: On the grassy hill above the village, a grove of old lychee trees hangs heavy with red fruit in early summer.
891.lore: The first lychees of the grove are carried to the Tower each year by relay runners so that they arrive fresh. The village eats the rest and gets fat for a month.

892.name: Tiêu Viên Thôn
892.look: A jungle village under the tattered leaves of banana gardens, its houses roofed with banana leaf and its paths lined with fibre drying on lines.
892.lore: The village grows bananas and plantains and weaves mats from the fibre. Its people say the rain on banana leaves is the first sound a child of Tiêu Viên hears.

893.name: Lão Lộc Phong
893.look: A grassy summit above the cloud meadows, where deer graze up to the very top.
893.lore: Herders say an old white stag has grazed this summit for longer than anyone remembers. Wood (Mộc) qi lies in its high grass.

894.name: Đằng La Lâm
894.look: A wet jungle where vines hang from every branch in curtains so thick that the forest is dim at noon.
894.lore: Villagers cut rattan and vine here for baskets and rope. Children are warned not to play in the curtains, for some vines close on whatever touches them.

895.name: Đạo Hoa Thôn
895.look: A low village of thatched houses among flat green paddies, with fish traps set in every channel between the fields.
895.lore: The village takes two rice harvests a year and raises fish in the flooded fields. When the rice flowers, no one in Đạo Hoa may sing, lest the blossom fall.

896.name: Hoàng Diễm Trấn
896.look: On the volcano's flank, roof lines and a market gate stick up out of a field of grey ash and yellow sulphur crusts.
896.lore: Hoàng Diễm was a town of sulphur gatherers, named for the yellow flames of its vents. In 1013 the small volcano woke and buried it in ash; most of its people escaped to the shore and founded Ôn Sa.

897.name: Địa Hỏa Huyệt
897.look: In a rocky fold at the volcano's foot a hollow glows a dull red from cracks in its floor, and the rain turns to steam before it reaches the ground.
897.lore: A Fire (Hỏa) vein rising from the small volcano, rare in the Tower's wet lands. Few of the Tower's disciples can use it, and it is rented to visiting cultivators of fire.

898.name: Ôn Sa Thôn
898.look: A fishing village on a black-sand beach that steams faintly after rain, below the slopes of a small volcano.
898.lore: Villagers bury eggs in the warm sand to cook them and gather sulphur from the vents above. They moved down to the shore after the mountain buried their old town.

899.name: Tượng Trủng Cương
899.look: A low grassy ridge strewn with the bleached bones and tusks of elephants, guarded by a herd of huge grey bulls.
899.lore: Old wild elephants walk out of the jungle to die on this ridge, and a herd of spirit-touched bulls guards their bones. The raftsmen of Tống Mộc say no ivory from it has ever reached a market and come to good.

900.name: Tống Mộc Thôn
900.look: A jungle village at a river mouth, its landing crowded with long timber rafts lashed together and the huts of the raftsmen built on them.
900.lore: The raftsmen float hardwood down from the forest and sell the timber at Phong Đăng and Không Mông. A raftsman who loses his raft walks home, and is not allowed to sleep under a roof until he has built another.

901.name: Tử Đằng Nhãn
901.look: In the jungle above the river an ancient wisteria has climbed a dead tree and covered a whole clearing in hanging purple flowers.
901.lore: A spirit eye of Wood (Mộc) qi under the wisteria. The villagers of Phù Ốc bring their newborns here for a single breath of its air.

902.name: Phù Ốc Thôn
902.look: A village of houses built on bamboo rafts moored along a jungle river, rising and falling with the water.
902.lore: Floods come every wet season here, and since 840 the villagers have simply floated with them. A family's raft is its land, and it is divided among the children by cutting the lashings.

903.name: Cự Giác Nguyên
903.look: A broad stretch of tall coastal grass trampled into wallows, where great dark buffalo stand with only their horns showing above the grass.
903.lore: A herd of spirit-touched wild buffalo led by a bull with horns wider than a cart roams this plain. The herders of Yên Vũ keep their own cattle well clear of the herd, and no one crosses the bull.

904.name: Yên Vũ Trấn
904.look: A walled harbour town on a wide grass coast, its grey roofs and sea wall softened by a fine rain that drifts in from the sea most afternoons.
904.lore: Yên Vũ grew up in 860 as a harbour for the grain and bamboo of the eastern coast. Its people say the misty rain is the sea's breath, and its sailors will not leave harbour on a clear day.

905.name: Lão Ngạc Chử
905.look: Low waterlogged grass flats behind the shore, where long dark shapes lie motionless in the shallow channels.
905.lore: Great saltwater crocodiles bask here, led by a spirit beast the fishers call the Old Log. The fishers leave it their fish heads and say it has never taken a villager.

906.name: Mãn Võng Thôn
906.look: A shore village of palm-thatched huts in the jungle edge, its beach covered in nets spread to dry and racks of split fish.
906.lore: The fishers of Mãn Võng have brought in full nets since 790, and they credit the crocodiles behind the shore for scaring off thieves. Every catch begins with one fish thrown back for the sea.

907.name: Dạ Bức Lâm
907.look: A stretch of jungle whose trees hang with thousands of roosting fruit bats, the ground beneath white with droppings.
907.lore: Huge spirit-touched fruit bats roost here, and at dusk they pour out over the coast like smoke. The fishers of Dạ Chúc say the bats follow their torches out to sea.

908.name: Dạ Chúc Thôn
908.look: A jungle shore village whose boats are drawn up on the sand by day, each with an iron torch basket fixed at the bow.
908.lore: The fishers of Dạ Chúc fish at night by torchlight, and the lights of their fleet are the brightest thing on the dark coast below the Tower. The Tower has never forbidden them, and the village takes care never to ask.

909.name: Vũ Ngọc Khoáng
909.look: A narrow quarry high on the ridge, its floor littered with chips of milky white stone that shine in the rain.
909.lore: White jade from here is carved into seals and hairpins in Không Mông. The quarry is worked only in summer, when the herders are on the pasture to carry the stone down.

910.name: Thiên Đăng Phong
910.look: A tall summit above the sky pastures, on which a pale blue light flickers along the crest in storms.
910.lore: Herders call the storm light the sky's lantern, and say it is the only lamp lit in the Tower's mountains. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its crest.

911.name: Khu Xà Khoáng
911.look: A short gallery in a mountain slope where the walls glow orange-red with realgar crystals.
911.lore: Realgar is dug here for medicines, festival wine and the poisons of Hồng Đậu Trang. The miners work short shifts and drink milk after each.

912.name: Lang Yên Phong
912.look: A steppe-flanked peak whose summit carries the ruined platform of an old beacon, blackened by long-dead fires.
912.lore: Khải Lôi's signallers lit smoke here to warn of trouble on the western road, and the Tower kept the beacon for a time after. Earth (Thổ) qi lies in its rock.

913.name: Tây Vọng Bảo
913.look: A small stone fort on a mountain spur over the western road, its towers split and blackened by lightning.
913.lore: The Tower built the fort to watch the western road after it let the old stockade below go. Lightning struck it so often that by 980 its garrison begged to leave, and the Tower let it stand empty.

914.name: Vô Tú Khoáng
914.look: A gallery mouth high on a cliff, its rope ladders long rotted away, where the ore lies in dark seams cold to the touch even at noon.
914.lore: The cold iron of this mine keeps an edge through rain and does not rust. Miners were once lowered to it on ropes to live in it a month at a time, but no crew has gone down in living memory.

915.name: Kình Thiên Phong
915.look: A sheer, square-topped summit of grey rock that seems to hold up the storm clouds on its flat crown.
915.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs in its cliffs. It is one of the first summits in the range to catch the storms, and herders on the northern steppe watch it for them.

916.name: Thiên Thanh Khoáng
916.look: A cut in the mountainside where the rock is crusted deep blue with azurite, bright against the grey scree.
916.lore: Azurite from here is ground for blue paint and smelted for copper. The painters of Không Mông buy the deepest blue for their skies.

917.name: Muộn Lôi Phong
917.look: A massive summit over forested valleys, its bare crest shaped like the head and shoulders of a giant.
917.lore: Earth (Thổ) qi lies deep in its bulk. The thunder rolls around it low and long, and herders say the giant is grumbling in its sleep.

918.name: Thiên Bộc Phong
918.look: A high peak whose cliffs pour a dozen waterfalls after every storm, blown into white veils by the wind.
918.lore: Water (Thủy) qi runs down its cliffs with the falls. The Tower's disciples stand under its falls after storms to train their footing.

919.name: Tinh Kỳ Phong
919.look: A tall peak on the northern edge of the range, its crest still marked by a stone socket where a great banner once flew.
919.lore: The Tower once flew its banner here in sight of Thiên Xu's lands. Metal (Kim) qi gathers on its crest.

920.name: Vọng Xu Bảo
920.look: A stone fort on a high spur facing north, its walls pulled down to knee height on purpose and its gate stones laid flat.
920.lore: The Tower built this fort to watch Thiên Xu's border. When the North Star Compact was sworn again at the truce, the Tower pulled its walls down as a sign of good faith, and they have never been raised.

921.name: Quần Lang Lâm
921.look: A dark fir wood on low wet ground, its trails beaten hard by many paws, with gnawed antlers scattered under the trees.
921.lore: Several wolf packs share this wood and fight over it in winter, and their howling carries to the tundra. Trappers take pelts from its edge and never camp inside.

922.name: Điêu Bì Trấn
922.look: On a wooded hill, the log walls of a small town have fallen inward, and rusted traps still hang on pegs inside the roofless fur store.
922.lore: Fur traders built Điêu Bì Trấn when sable fur was worth its weight in silver. By 1020 the sables were trapped out of the hills, and within two years the last traders left for the lake towns.

923.name: Lão Căn Mạch
923.look: On a rise in the forest, a tangle of huge exposed pine roots arches over bare ground that hums faintly when pressed with a palm.
923.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the roots of the oldest pines here. Resin from these trees is said to stay soft for a hundred years.

924.name: Tùng Chi Thôn
924.look: Log houses among old pines, each trunk scarred with neat V-shaped cuts above a clay cup, and pitch kettles smoking in the yard.
924.lore: The village taps resin and boils it into pitch for the lake boats, cutting no living tree. Its pitch-makers say the best resin comes from trees older than Tùng Đào Cung.

925.name: Dạ Kiêu Lâm
925.look: A swampy pine wood where pellets of fur and bone lie thick under hollow trees, and at dusk great pale owls drift between the trunks.
925.lore: Owls as big as children nest in its hollow trees and hunt the swamp edge at night. Villagers say an owl that follows a boat home means a death in the house.

926.name: Ngư Đăng Thôn
926.look: A shore village of low grey roofs where dozens of boat lanterns hang from poles along the beach, lit together on autumn nights.
926.lore: Its fishers draw fish to their nets with lantern light in autumn, and from the far shore the boats look like a second string of stars. They sell their smoked catch at Quy Điểu.

927.name: Vạn Tùng Lâm
927.look: An endless stand of straight red-brown pines on gentle ground, so even that the trunks seem to repeat to the edge of sight.
927.lore: Tùng Đào's surveyors once tried to count its trees and stopped at ten thousand, which gave the forest its name. Woodsmen get lost in it because every view looks the same.

928.name: Tùng Than Thôn
928.look: Grey-roofed houses along a pale beach under tall pines, boats drawn up on log rollers and pitch pots smoking by the water.
928.lore: Its people build small boats from windfallen pine and caulk them with their own pitch. Lake fishers from all along the shore come here to buy a hull.

929.name: Tố Hoa Lâm
929.look: A pale, quiet birch wood on flat ground, its white trunks peeling in long curls and the floor carpeted with yellow leaves.
929.lore: The villages strip bark here for boxes and writing sheets, never more than one strip from a tree in a year. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's records are kept on its bark.

930.name: Hồi Lưu Thôn
930.look: Stilt houses stand over a still backwater where the river meets the shore, wicker eel traps stacked on every porch.
930.lore: The villagers trap eels in the river's backwaters and smoke them over birch. Hàm Nguyệt Trang takes its dues in eel each autumn and serves them at its moon feast.

931.name: Lạc Diệp Lâm
931.look: A larch forest that turns gold in autumn and drops every needle, leaving the trunks bare and the ground soft and bright.
931.lore: Larch is the one conifer here that sheds its needles, and the burners gather the fallen wood for their kilns. In winter the bare forest is the easiest place in the north to track game.

932.name: Thán Diêu Thôn
932.look: A clearing ringed by earth-covered charcoal mounds, smoking day and night, with soot-black houses and stacks of deadwood.
932.lore: The burners make charcoal only from dead and fallen wood, as Tùng Đào requires, and haul it to the lake towns before the snow. Their children are black to the elbows by the age of five.

933.name: Tẩy Nguyệt Đàm
933.look: A small, clear lake in the pines near the river, its pebble bed visible far out from the shore.
933.lore: Fishers say the moon comes down to wash here before it rises over the long lake. Hàm Nguyệt Trang's disciples once kept spirit fish in it, and a few still swim there.

934.name: Nguyệt Tân Trấn
934.look: A timber-walled town on the river bank, its ferry stair running into the water beside rows of pitch-black barges.
934.lore: Nguyệt Tân Trấn ferries timber, pitch and pearls between the long lake and the inland villages. Its ferry runs only by moonlight in the busy season, so the day stays free for loading.

935.name: Hàn Kính Hồ
935.look: A dark, round forest lake that freezes clear as glass in winter, the trees and sky reflected perfectly in its ice.
935.lore: Its ice is so clear that the fish can be seen moving under it. Young cultivators of Hàm Nguyệt Trang come to sit on the ice and still their minds.

936.name: Sái Võng Thôn
936.look: Every path in this forest village is lined with tall frames of drying nets, so walking through it is like walking through a maze of grey lace.
936.lore: Its people twist net cord from nettle and birch bast and sell nets to fishers all along the lake. A net from Sái Võng is said to last ten winters.

937.name: Thúy Cái Mạch
937.look: On a forested ridge, a ring of spruces with unusually dense, deep-green crowns closes overhead like a roof, and the ground beneath stays dry in any rain.
937.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi rises under the ridge and feeds the spruces above it. Tùng Đào's wardens visit it each spring and keep the hunters from camping inside the ring.

938.name: Liệp Hộ Thôn
938.look: A cluster of log houses with racks of stretched pelts, antlers nailed over every door and hounds sleeping in the snow.
938.lore: Its families have trapped marten, fox and deer here for generations and sell their furs at the winter ice market. Every hunter swears never to take a beast's young.

939.name: Tàng Châu Đàm
939.look: A deep, reed-fringed pool beside the river, its dark water ringed with white mussel shells on the shore.
939.lore: A small bed of pearl mussels lives here, hidden from the Băng Tâm skiffs during the Long Lake War. Hàm Nguyệt Trang now keeps it as seed stock for its beds.

940.name: Phóng Phiệt Thôn
940.look: On a river bank, bound log rafts lie in rows on the mud, each branded with the pine mark of Tùng Đào's foresters.
940.lore: The villagers float windfallen and dead trunks down to the lake towns in spring flood. No raft leaves without a forester's brand, and a raft without one is burned.

941.name: Bạch Hùng Nguyên
941.look: Flat white tundra near the shore, pocked with snow dens and old seal bones, where great white shapes rise and lie down again in the wind.
941.lore: White bears come ashore here each autumn and den through the winter. Herders cross the plain only in midsummer, when the bears are out on the water.

942.name: Sơn Miêu Cương
942.look: A rocky knoll in thick pine, its boulders scratched and its snow marked by broad, furred tracks.
942.lore: Lynxes den among its boulders and hunt hares through the forest. Villagers say a lynx can see through a wall, and hang their meat high.

943.name: Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn
943.look: On the shore, the stone walls of a town lean inland, pushed over in long rows, with heaps of boulders shoved up among the house footings.
943.lore: The town greeted the moonrise over the water from its harbour wall for six centuries. In the spring of 1033 a storm drove the breaking ice ashore in a wall, flattening the harbour and half the town, and its people never rebuilt.

944.name: Tịch Ba Thôn
944.look: A row of grey-roofed houses facing the water, boats pulled up at the tide line and nets set out on poles in the evening calm.
944.lore: Its fishers go out only when the evening waves settle, a habit learned after the ice shove that crushed Nghênh Nguyệt Trấn. They sell their catch and winter ice at Quy Điểu.

945.name: Tuyết Tùng Lâm
945.look: A wood of broad cedars with layered branches that hold the snow in flat white shelves.
945.lore: Its cedar is fragrant and resists rot, and the lake villages build their shrines from it. Only a fallen cedar may be taken, by Tùng Đào's rule.

946.name: Tạc Băng Thôn
946.look: A shore village where great blocks of ice lie stacked under sawdust in long sheds, and saws and ice picks hang on every wall.
946.lore: In winter its people saw ice from the frozen shore and pack it in sawdust to keep fish all summer. Tùng Đào's stewards buy ice for the northern granaries.

947.name: Thính Tùng Lâm
947.look: An upland pine wood where flat stones have been set among the trunks as seats, and the wind in the crowns sounds like distant surf.
947.lore: Tùng Đào's disciples of the north come here to hear the pine waves when they cannot travel to the seat. The stones are said to have been set by the first steward of the north.

948.name: Sương Tùng Các
948.look: A three-roofed pavilion of dark pine stands on a frosty rise among old trees, and from every branch around it hang small paper lanterns painted with talismans.
948.lore: Sương Tùng Các is a small sect of talisman makers sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, who write their talismans on paper made from birch bark and pine resin. Its ward lanterns hang in the lake villages to keep beasts and frost spirits off the doors in winter.

949.name: Tùng Kiều Thôn
949.look: A village on both banks of a river, joined by a long bridge of whole pine trunks pinned with wooden pegs.
949.lore: The bridge was built from pines felled by one storm, and each family mends its own trunk. Pilgrims cross it on their way up to the listening wood.

950.name: Vân Sam Lâm
950.look: A dark, dense spruce forest whose tall spires vanish into low cloud on grey days.
950.lore: Spruce from here is light and strong and goes to make zither soundboards in the pine sea. Gum gatherers work its edge in summer.

951.name: Thạch Than Thôn
951.look: Grey-roofed houses above a wide, stony river where children wade the shallows with spears and mules wait on the bank.
951.lore: The river is too shallow for boats above the village, so goods come and go by mule. Its people spear fish in the shallows and gather spruce gum.

952.name: Hồng Tùng Lâm
952.look: A wood of tall, straight pines with reddish bark, their crowns far above a clear floor.
952.lore: These red pines give the best mast timber in the north, and only windfalls may be taken. Shipwrights from the lake towns come to choose their trunks in person.

953.name: Hồ Khẩu Thôn
953.look: A village of grey roofs where a river opens into the long lake, its jetties busy with fishing boats and timber barges.
953.lore: Every boat going up the river passes Hồ Khẩu, and the village lives by fish, reeds and the boatmen's custom. Tùng Đào keeps a toll post on its jetty.

954.name: Cổ Mộc Nhãn
954.look: In a clearing stands a single colossal pine, its trunk hollow at the base, and inside the hollow the air shimmers faintly green.
954.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi comes to the surface inside the old pine's hollow. Tùng Đào allows one disciple at a time to sit in it, for a month at most.

955.name: Tùng Tử Thôn
955.look: A hill village where pine cones lie drying in heaps on every roof and the smell of roasted nuts hangs in the air.
955.lore: Its people live by gathering pine nuts each autumn and pressing them for lamp oil. They leave one cone in ten for the squirrels, saying the squirrels plant the next forest.

956.name: Bàn Căn Lâm
956.look: On a steep hillside, pines grow from bare rock, their roots coiling over the stones like ropes.
956.lore: The roots hold the slope together, and the villages forbid cutting here. After Tà Dương Trấn slid away, no one argues with the rule.

957.name: Tà Dương Trấn
957.look: A raw scar of earth runs down a hillside, and at its foot the timbers and roofs of a small town lie broken in a heap of mud and stones grown over with birch.
957.lore: A hill town of honey and timber traders, built on a sunny western slope. In the long rains of 1104 the hillside slid away and buried half the town in a night, and the rest was left.

958.name: Sơn Ổ Thôn
958.look: Houses tucked into a sheltered hollow in the hills, log beehives on the slope and baskets of mushrooms drying on the eaves.
958.lore: Its people gather mushrooms and wild honey and keep a few goats. They remember Tà Dương Trấn and build only on rock.

959.name: Hệ Bì Thôn
959.look: A river village at the edge of Phản Cảnh Lâm, where bundles of birch bark strips hang by every door, ready to be tied to trees.
959.lore: Its woodcutters and guides tie bark strips on the ways into Phản Cảnh Lâm so the lost can follow the light out. Tùng Đào's patrols rest here and ask the guides what they have seen.

960.name: U Thúy Lâm
960.look: A deep wood of pine and fir where moss covers every stone and fallen log in a thick green fleece.
960.lore: The forest is so damp and quiet that herb gatherers find mosses here that grow nowhere else. Its paths lead up to the old academy's terraces.

961.name: Lãnh Hương Viện
961.look: On a wooded rise, terraces of overgrown herb beds climb to the roofless halls of an academy, its incense burners still standing in the moss.
961.lore: A small sect of incense makers who burned cold-flower herbs to calm the mind in cultivation. Its last master died in seclusion in 890 with no heir named, and Tùng Đào took in its disciples; its herbs still grow on the terraces.

962.name: Song Thụ Thôn
962.look: A river village gathered around two huge pines that grew from one root, their trunks splitting apart above the roofs.
962.lore: Villagers fish the river and gather incense herbs from the old terraces of Lãnh Hương Viện. Couples are married under the twin pines.

963.name: Tông Hùng Nhai
963.look: A forested crag above the gap, its caves marked by stripped bark and claw-torn stumps.
963.lore: Brown bears den in its caves through the winter and raid the beehives below in spring. The villagers leave a pot of honey at the foot of the crag each autumn, hoping to be left alone.

964.name: Dịch Lộ Trấn
964.look: High on a hill, the stone stables and inn walls of a post town stand roofless beside a paved road that runs into the forest and vanishes.
964.lore: Tùng Đào built the post town when it took Lãnh Nguyệt Lâm, on the hill road from the pine sea. When the lake road along the water was finished, the hill road was abandoned, and the town emptied by 868.

965.name: Phong Khẩu Thôn
965.look: Low stone-walled houses huddle in a windy gap in the hills, roofs weighted with rocks, goats sheltering in the lee.
965.lore: The wind through the gap never stops, and its people keep goats and gather pine nuts. They still keep the old post road's well, though few travellers come.

966.name: Hàn Lộ Huyệt
966.look: A shallow hollow in the tundra where frost forms on every blade of lichen even at midsummer noon, and the air smells of snow.
966.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi surfaces here, cold enough to freeze dew on a summer day. Tùng Đào's water cultivators come in the short summer, when the walk is possible.

967.name: Vĩnh Đống Huyệt
967.look: A sunken pit in the tundra lined with blue ice that never thaws, breathing cold mist even in summer.
967.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here so cold that the ground has not thawed in living memory. Tùng Đào's disciples who cultivate in it wrap themselves in fur and stay a day at most.

968.name: Bắc Minh Quán
968.look: On a bare shore, a ring of low stone cells stands around a fallen hall, its doorways facing the northern water.
968.lore: Hermits of water arts built this abbey to watch the northern water through the long dark. They never took more than a handful of disciples, and when Tùng Đào came north in 330 the last of them went to the palace and left the abbey empty.

969.name: Bạch Dạ Tuyền
969.look: A cold spring wells up among stunted larches and runs in a clear thread over the tundra, catching the low light of the summer nights.
969.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds this spring, strongest in the white nights of midsummer. The hermits of Bắc Minh Quán drank only from it.

970.name: Ngưng Sương Mạch
970.look: A low rise in the tundra is crusted with thick white frost in a long line, as though a frozen river ran just under the lichen.
970.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs under the rise and draws frost out of the air. Tùng Đào's disciples come to temper their bodies in its cold.

971.name: Tuyết Áp Lâm
971.look: A pine forest whose young trees are bent into arches under heavy snow, making tunnels across the paths.
971.lore: Snow lies so heavy here that the trees grow crooked, and the herders drive their reindeer through the arches. Bent pine from here makes the best sled runners.

972.name: Mục Lộc Thôn
972.look: Log houses and hide tents at the forest edge, reindeer corralled behind fences of split pine and antlers piled by the doors.
972.lore: Its herders are cousins of Tuyết Lộc's and keep their winter grounds here. They trade hides, antler and smoked meat south to the lake towns.

973.name: Cự Thỉ Cương
973.look: A knoll in the forest torn up as if ploughed, with trees rubbed bare at shoulder height and wallows of black mud.
973.lore: Boars the size of oxen root here and raid the village stores in lean winters. Hunters go after them only in groups of ten.

974.name: Bắc Ngạn Thôn
974.look: Grey-roofed log houses on the cold northern shore, sleds and harpoons stacked by the doors and seal hides stretched on frames.
974.lore: Its people hunt seals on the ice and fish through holes in winter. Seal oil from here lights the lamps of the northern villages.

975.name: Kim Điêu Đài
975.look: A flat-topped rock rises out of the forest, its edges heaped with great stick nests and the bones of hares and fawns.
975.lore: Golden eagles nest on the rock and hunt the forest and tundra for miles. Their fallen feathers are prized by fletchers, and villagers gather them under the cliff.

976.name: Băng Võng Thôn
976.look: A shore village where long lines of holes cut through the ice lead out from the beach, each with a net cord frozen to a stake.
976.lore: Its fishers feed long nets under the ice from hole to hole and haul them at dawn. They pay Tùng Đào in dried fish and eagle feathers.

977.name: Độc Thiềm Chử
977.look: Low mud shoals in a black marsh, their surface covered in warty toads the size of a man's head, croaking in a deep drone.
977.lore: Poison toads breed on the shoals in summer, and their venom blisters the skin. Alchemists' collectors come in late summer with gloves and jars.

978.name: Đan Mộc Lâm
978.look: A grove of small thorny trees on the grass below the red quarry, their cut stumps showing heartwood as bright red as the stone above.
978.lore: Its sappan wood is chipped and boiled for red dye and sold to the silk dyers of Tang Điền. The masons of Thạch Tượng say the trees drink the colour out of the red mountain.

979.name: Tạc Thạch Trấn
979.look: Burned walls on a red hillside above the quarry, the ground strewn with broken chisels.
979.lore: Xích Thành Môn's quarry town for Đan Thạch, burned in 588 in the War of the Vermilion Caves when the gate's men fired it rather than leave it. The quarrymen who stayed built Thạch Tượng below.

980.name: Thạch Tượng Thôn
980.look: A village of red-stone houses below the quarry, its yards full of half-dressed blocks and chisel sheds.
980.lore: Its masons dress the red stone of Đan Thạch for Phượng Minh's builders, and their own houses are made of the blocks that cracked.

981.name: Trầm Hương Lâm
981.look: Dark jungle where some trunks are scarred and oozing black resin, and the air smells of incense.
981.lore: Its agarwood is burned in Phượng Minh's halls. The gatherers wound a tree and wait twenty years before they cut it.

982.name: Thu Võng Thôn
982.look: A low shore village of stilted houses at the jungle's edge, long seine nets hanging on poles before every door and canoes drawn up on the grey sand.
982.lore: Its people haul seine nets from the beach at dawn, whole families on each rope, and in the dry season go into the forest behind for agarwood. The resin they bring out is burned in Phượng Minh's halls.

983.name: Đại Mãng Cốc
983.look: A jungle valley where broad smooth tracks run through the undergrowth and shed skins hang from the branches.
983.lore: A python longer than a boat lives here and takes deer, pigs and the occasional diver. Alchemists pay well for its shed skin.

984.name: Hải Sâm Thôn
984.look: A village on the mangrove edge where dried sea cucumbers hang in strings under the eaves.
984.lore: Its divers bring sea cucumbers up from the shallows and dry them for the city kitchens.

985.name: Thâm Lục Mạch
985.look: A hollow in the jungle where the leaves grow so thick and dark that it is green twilight at noon.
985.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein. Wood cultivators come to sit in the hollow and leave covered in moss.

986.name: Tân Lang Thôn
986.look: A coast village under tall straight areca palms, their nut clusters drying on mats.
986.lore: Its people sell areca nuts along the coast road; every guest is offered one at the door.

987.name: Cổ Dung Lâm
987.look: A jungle of vast banyans whose hanging roots have grown into whole new trunks, so that one tree looks like a forest.
987.lore: The town's traders leave a coin in the roots of the oldest banyan before a voyage.

988.name: Hương Liệu Thị
988.look: A small walled market town on the shore, its streets lined with sacks of pepper, cardamom and resin under awnings.
988.lore: The spice villages of the south coast bring their harvest here, and boats carry it on to Ngũ Thải and Thạch Cơ.

989.name: Viêm Hải Quán
989.look: Broken red-stone halls on the grassy shore, their sea wall blackened as if by fire.
989.lore: A sea hall of Xích Thành Môn, where its disciples practised fire arts over the water. It was abandoned when the gate fell in 590, and Phượng Minh never reopened it.

990.name: Tử Đàn Huyệt
990.look: A ring of old rosewood trees in the jungle, their fallen leaves deep and dark underfoot.
990.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein lies under the ring. Phượng Minh forbids cutting the rosewood here.

991.name: Sa Nhân Thôn
991.look: A shore village of thatched houses beside cardamom gardens planted in the shade of the jungle trees, with pods drying on woven trays in every yard.
991.lore: Its people grow cardamom under the canopy and sell the dried pods at Hương Liệu Thị. They will not walk on the grass shore by the old Xích Thành sea hall after dark.

992.name: Mộc Miên Lâm
992.look: A hillside of tall kapok trees that burst into huge red flowers on bare branches every spring.
992.lore: The coast calls them hero trees. Their floss stuffs the town's pillows and sails' seams.

993.name: Nam Tân Trấn
993.look: A small walled harbour town on a steep shore, its quay crowded with deep-sea boats.
993.lore: Boats sail from here to the far south and the islands. Its sailors say the great Bằng's wind starts at their quay.

994.name: Hương Phàm Trấn
994.look: Charred walls among jungle on the shore, a burned quay running into the sea.
994.lore: A spice port of the south coast, burned by Thôn Hải's pirates in 771. The Purge came ten years too late for it, and its trade moved to Hương Liệu.

995.name: Huyết Đằng Mạch
995.look: A jungle hilltop knotted with vines as thick as an arm, which bleed dark red sap where they are cut.
995.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein runs under the hill and the vines grow fastest over it. Healers of the coast tap the sap to stop bleeding, and wood cultivators who sit here say they can feel the vines growing.

996.name: Đậu Khấu Thôn
996.look: A shore village among nutmeg trees on the jungle hills, brown seeds wrapped in red lace drying on mats in every yard.
996.lore: Its people grow nutmeg and mace and fish within sight of Thôn Hải's old islet. Their grandparents' grandparents came from the burned spice town of Hương Phàm, and every house keeps a charred plank from it over the hearth.

997.name: Nam Minh Mạch
997.look: A rocky hilltop in the jungle with a clear spring that looks out over the open southern sea.
997.lore: A Thủy (water) vein named for the southern deep where the Bằng flies in the old book. The spring always runs a little south.

998.name: Bằng Trình Thôn
998.look: A jungle-edge fishing village whose long deep-sea boats are drawn up with their prows all pointing south.
998.lore: Its fishers sail further south than any others on the coast and say they follow the great Bằng's road.

999.name: Long Huyết Lâm
999.look: Squat umbrella-shaped trees on a jungle slope, their cut bark weeping dark red resin.
999.lore: Its resin, dragon's blood, is a medicine for wounds and a red varnish for the palace's zithers.

1000.name: Hồ Tiêu Thôn
1000.look: A hill village above the sea where pepper vines climb every tree, and red and black berries dry on mats along the paths.
1000.lore: Its people tend the vines on the jungle slope and carry the dried pepper down to the shore boats, which take it to Hương Liệu Thị and on to the cities. Every bride is given a vine to plant on her first day.

1001.name: Tàn Hỏa Mạch
1001.look: A patch of grass where the earth is cracked and faintly warm, a short walk from the ruined gate.
1001.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein that once fed Xích Thành's fire arts. Phượng Minh keeps an eye on anyone who sits here too long.

1002.name: Tân Sinh Thôn
1002.look: A coast village of red-stone houses on steppe below the red cliffs, a blackened old hearthstone set at its centre.
1002.lore: It was rebuilt on the ashes of one of the eleven villages Xích Thành burned, and its people keep the old hearthstone as a shrine. They herd goats and dry fish, and never graze the cliffs.

1003.name: Lãng Ôn Trì
1003.look: A rock pool on the shore where hot water wells up through black rock and mixes with the breaking waves.
1003.lore: At high tide it is warm, at low tide scalding; the villagers time their baths by the moon.

1004.name: Hồng Sa Thôn
1004.look: A few fishing huts on a beach of red volcanic sand, boats drawn up above the tide.
1004.lore: Its people fish and boil salt. Bathers come for the red sand, said to draw out fever.

1005.name: Hỏa Tích Nhai
1005.look: A black sea cliff beyond the town, its ledges crowded with great lizards basking in the sun.
1005.lore: Spirit monitor lizards that spit burning spittle nest here. The town's children are told never to climb it, and some do.

1006.name: Thiên Nhai Trấn
1006.look: A small walled harbour town on a grassy cape, with nothing beyond it but sea.
1006.lore: The last port before the open southern sea; ships take water here, and sailors carve their names on the quay before they leave.

1007.name: Luyện Vũ Huyệt
1007.look: A red-glowing crack high on the volcano's flank, breathing heat over a bare slope of black rock.
1007.lore: Phượng Minh holds it; its fire disciples come to temper their arts in the heat and say the vent forges feathers into flame. Its fire is Hỏa (fire) at its fiercest.

1008.name: Lưu Hỏa Các
1008.look: The upper halls of a red-stone pavilion jutting out of a tongue of black lava on the jungle slope.
1008.lore: A fire hall of Xích Thành Môn, abandoned when the gate fell in 590. In 845 lava from the vent above ran down over its lower courts, and only its roofs still show.

1009.name: Thanh Da Lâm
1009.look: A coastal grove of tall leaning coconut palms above a white beach.
1009.lore: Its palms give the village rope, oil and roofing; the boatmen say no pirate ever hid in it.

1010.name: Phá Lãng Thôn
1010.look: A jungle shore village of boatmen, its beach lined with small strong rowing boats.
1010.lore: Its boatmen row treasure seekers out to Thôn Hải's islet to dig in the ash for Kình Nha, and charge for the trip both ways in advance.

1011.name: Dư Ôn Mạch
1011.look: A low grassy hill where snow-white ash shows in the soil and the ground is warm after dark.
1011.lore: A Hỏa (fire) vein running out from the vents to the north. Phần Vũ's disciples rest here between sittings.

1012.name: Lô Hội Thôn
1012.look: A coast village of grass-roofed houses among rows of spiky grey-green aloe.
1012.lore: Its people boil aloe into salve and sell it to Phần Vũ Đường for disciples burned in the vents.

1013.name: Chức Hà Các
1013.look: A long red-timber pavilion on the grassy shore, its open halls hung with bolts of silk that glow red at dusk.
1013.lore: A minor sect of weavers sworn to Phượng Minh, founded in 1150, which weaves fire-silk robes and banners from Tang Điền's worms without the vents. It says it has rediscovered Xích Thành's lost craft by other means, and the palace has not yet decided whether that pleases it.

1014.name: Thanh Can Mạch
1014.look: A bamboo grove near the shore whose green canes grow twice as thick as any around it, creaking in the sea wind.
1014.lore: A Mộc (wood) vein lies under the grove. The villagers of Trúc Lâu cut its canes only for the main posts of their houses, and the weavers of Chức Hà Các come here to sit before a new loom is strung.

1015.name: Trúc Lâu Thôn
1015.look: A coast village of raised bamboo houses on stilts among rice and mulberry plots.
1015.lore: Its people grow rice and mulberry, and lately sell their cocoons to the weavers on the shore.

1016.name: Phí Thạch Thang
1016.look: A spring in the cane fields that boils hard among white stones, steaming day and night.
1016.lore: The villagers start the cane boiling with its water and cook eggs in it for travellers.

1017.name: Cam Giá Thôn
1017.look: A shore village surrounded by tall sugarcane, with an ox-driven cane press and a smoking boiling shed at its centre.
1017.lore: Its people crush the cane in the press, boil the juice down into cakes of brown sugar and ship them to Ngũ Thải and the cities. They start the boiling with water from the hot spring in the fields, which saves a day's firewood.

1018.name: Lục Phàn Trì
1018.look: A warm pool in the grass whose water is a cloudy green and whose rim is crusted with green crystals.
1018.lore: The dyers scrape its green vitriol to fix their colours, and alchemists buy it too.

1019.name: Kim Sa Trấn
1019.look: Sand-drifted walls on the shore, the lower streets under the sea at high tide.
1019.lore: A fishing and trading town on the golden beach, drowned by a great storm tide in 913. Its people moved inland, and their grandchildren became the dyers of Lam Điện.

1020.name: Lam Điện Thôn
1020.look: A shore village where vats of blue dye stand in every yard and cloth dries in long blue banners.
1020.lore: Its people grow indigo and dye cloth and silk; their hands are blue to the wrist.

1021.name: Phượng Vĩ Lâm
1021.look: A stand of spreading flame trees on the grass, their crowns blazing scarlet every summer.
1021.lore: The coast calls them phoenix-tail trees. Phượng Minh's disciples collect the fallen flowers for the summer rites.

1022.name: Lệ Chi Thôn
1022.look: A shore village among lychee orchards, its trees hung with red fruit in early summer.
1022.lore: Its lychees are rushed to the cities by fast boat, since they spoil in three days.

1023.name: Phi Hồ Cốc
1023.look: A jungle valley where the trees hang black with thousands of roosting giant bats.
1023.lore: Spirit flying foxes with wings wider than a man's arms roost here by day and strip the orchards by night.

1024.name: Bàn Căn Trấn
1024.look: Burned stilts and walls among mangrove roots on the shore, half swallowed by the tide.
1024.lore: A mangrove town of fishers and charcoal burners, burned by Thôn Hải's raiders in 767. The mangroves have taken it back.

1025.name: Quế Viên Thôn
1025.look: A jungle village in a clearing of longan orchards, the brown fruit drying over smoky charcoal racks under long open sheds.
1025.lore: Its people dry longans into the sweet brown rounds sold in every market of the coast, and burn the pruned wood into charcoal. They keep torches lit in the orchards at night against the flying foxes of the valley nearby.

1026.name: Triều Căn Nhãn
1026.look: A clear pool among mangrove roots inland, where the water rises and falls with no channel to the sea.
1026.lore: A Thủy (water) vein. Phượng Minh's scholars have added it to the puzzle of Hồ Tâm's lake.

1027.name: Bạch Diêm Thôn
1027.look: A flat coast village beside a grid of salt pans gleaming white in the sun.
1027.lore: Its people make salt and fish the shallows; its salt is whiter than any on the coast.

1028.name: Thải Phượng Phong
1028.look: A tall red crag above the west coast, its rock banded in red, yellow and grey.
1028.lore: It is said the five-coloured bird was seen over this peak in the old days, and the coast was named for it. Its qi runs Hỏa (fire).

1029.name: Đại Thát Chử
1029.look: Mud banks in the marsh channels are crossed by slides and heaped with fish bones where great otters feed.
1029.lore: Otters as large as a man fish these channels and fight anything that takes their catch. The villagers of Bồ Diệp leave them a share of each net.

1030.name: Bồ Diệp Thôn
1030.look: Low houses roofed with cattail thatch stand on stilts at the edge of a marshy bay, mats drying on every rail.
1030.lore: The villagers weave cattail mats and baskets and fish the shallows. Their mats line the floors of half the houses in Yên Ba.

1031.name: Thâm Bích Lâm
1031.look: Old broadleaf forest so dense that the light under it is green even at noon.
1031.lore: The charcoal burners cut only at its edges and leave the old heart alone. Lost travellers are told to walk downhill until they smell smoke.

1032.name: Tùng Chi Trấn
1032.look: Blackened stone footings and charred stumps lie among young trees, the outline of a small town still visible in the moss.
1032.lore: Resin tappers built the town and sold pitch for boats and torches. In the dry summer of 1061 a fire caught the resin stores and burned the town and the forest around it in one night; the tappers did not rebuild.

1033.name: Thiêu Thán Thôn
1033.look: A clearing of turf-domed kilns smokes among the trees, with black-faced burners and stacks of cut wood around it.
1033.lore: Its charcoal goes by cart to Hồng Lô Cốc, which pays well for wood that burns even. The burners say a good kiln is tended like a pill furnace.

1034.name: Bách Niên Lâm
1034.look: Ancient firs stand far apart above a floor of moss, each wider than a cart.
1034.lore: The town of Bích Tân cuts a tree here only once a century, for the main beam of its hall. Woodcutters say each tree knows when its year has come.

1035.name: Hoàng Bá Trấn
1035.look: Roofless houses of grey stone stand in a ring around an empty market, yellow-barked cork trees growing through their floors.
1035.lore: The town sold the yellow cork bark used against fevers, and grew rich on it. The coughing sickness of 760 killed most of its people, and the rest left before the cure of Lâm Tuyền was found.

1036.name: Bích Tân Trấn
1036.look: A walled timber town of grey roofs stands at a sheltered landing, log rafts tied along its shore.
1036.lore: Timber from the cape's northern forests is floated here and shipped out along the coast. Its harbour masters are paid in logs as often as in coin.

1037.name: Mật Hùng Lâm
1037.look: Lindens scored with claw marks stand over broken hives and trampled undergrowth.
1037.lore: Honey bears raid the hives here every summer, and some of them have eaten enough spirit honey to grow cunning. Hunters of Dã Mật go in pairs.

1038.name: Dã Mật Thôn
1038.look: Hollow-log hives hang from every tree around a small village of grey roofs, and bees fill the air above the paths.
1038.lore: The villagers gather wild honey and wax from the linden woods. Their wax seals the pill jars of Hồng Lô Cốc.

1039.name: Hoa Thụ Lâm
1039.look: A white-trunked birch forest grows on low ground behind the bay, bright even under grey skies.
1039.lore: The villagers of Hàn Loan strip its bark for baskets, boxes and roofing, taking only a strip from each tree. Peeled trunks heal into dark rings that mark the families who cut them.

1040.name: Hàn Loan Thôn
1040.look: A few grey-roofed houses stand on a low cold bay, boats drawn up among the birches behind them.
1040.lore: Its fishers haul their boats into the birch wood when the bay half freezes in winter. The women weave baskets of birch bark while they wait for the thaw.

1041.name: Du Thụ Lâm
1041.look: Tall elms with spreading crowns cover low ground just inland of the kelp shore.
1041.lore: In famine years the cape's poor eat elm seeds and inner bark from these woods, and the villagers of Hải Đới never forbid it. The custom dates from the winter of 860.

1042.name: Hải Đới Thôn
1042.look: Long racks of drying kelp line the shore in front of a small village, dark ribbons stirring in the wind.
1042.lore: The villagers cut kelp from the offshore beds and dry it for food. Hồng Lô Cốc buys the ash of burnt kelp for its salt washes.

1043.name: Đoản Vĩ Cương
1043.look: A rocky wooded ridge is crossed by narrow game trails and marked with claw-scored trunks.
1043.lore: Short-tailed spirit lynxes, the bobtails of the ridge's name, den in the rocks and hunt the herb gatherers' paths at dusk. The gatherers say a lynx will follow you for a day before it decides.

1044.name: Thái Dược Thôn
1044.look: A village of grey roofs on a forested slope, its yards full of baskets of roots and bundles of drying leaves.
1044.lore: Its people climb the high ground for roots and sell them to Hồng Lô Cốc and Thúy Vi's terraces. Every gatherer carries a bell so the others can find them in the haze.

1045.name: Lão Tùng Lâm
1045.look: Tall old pines with red bark grow on low hills behind the shipyards, the ground soft with needles.
1045.lore: The boatwrights choose keel trees here years before they cut them and bind a red cord around each one. No one else may cut a corded tree.

1046.name: Lam Triều Các
1046.look: On a rocky point the burnt shell of a stone pavilion faces the sea, its upper floors gone and its steps green with weed.
1046.lore: A small sect of water cultivators sworn to Thúy Vi studied the tides from this point. In 744 Thôn Hải's pirates landed at night, burned the pavilion and carried off its disciples; the boatwrights still light a fire on the point on that night.

1047.name: Thuyền Ổ Thôn
1047.look: Half-built hulls stand on wooden slips along a low shore, with pine logs stacked behind a village of grey roofs.
1047.lore: Most fishing boats on the cape were laid down here, from pines of the forest behind. A boat is launched only at high tide on a still day, and the whole village pushes.

1048.name: Ngân Điêu Đài
1048.look: A flat rocky terrace above the pines is riddled with dens, and silver-furred martens watch from the stones.
1048.lore: Silver martens with spirit-bright fur den on the terrace, quick enough to steal from a cultivator's sleeve. Their pelts fetch a high price in Yên Ba.

1049.name: Tùng Nhung Thôn
1049.look: A village of grey roofs in high pine woods, with mushrooms drying on flat baskets on every roof.
1049.lore: Each family knows its own mushroom grounds and tells no one, not even its neighbours. The dried mushrooms go to Yên Ba in autumn.

1050.name: Mê Vụ Lâm
1050.look: A low forest of hollows where the blue-green haze lies so thick that the trees fade a few steps away.
1050.lore: Travellers go around it, for paths there turn back on themselves. Thúy Vi's disciples are sent in to walk out without a guide, as a lesser Haze Walk.

1051.name: Tất Thụ Thôn
1051.look: A village of grey roofs among oaks and lacquer trees, the lacquer trunks scored with neat rows of cuts and cups.
1051.lore: The villagers tap raw lacquer and sell it to the craftsmen of Yên Ba. Newcomers break out in rashes for a year, and the villagers say that is the trees deciding.

1052.name: Hàn Tượng Nguyên
1052.look: Wide frozen flats are scored with long grooves where frost elephants have dragged their tusks through the ice.
1052.lore: Herds of woolly frost elephants cross the plain each year on the same path. Sealers say the herd will trample anything that stands in it, tent or cultivator.

1053.name: Thủy Hủy Chử
1053.look: Low muddy islets in the marsh are covered with shed snake skins and coiled shapes in the reeds.
1053.lore: Water vipers swarm here, and the largest are said to have spirit venom. Hồng Lô Cốc pays for their venom glands.

1054.name: Man Ngư Thôn
1054.look: Wicker eel traps hang drying on poles at a river mouth, beside smokehouses and a village of grey roofs.
1054.lore: The villagers trap eels in the river mouth and smoke them for Yên Ba. Smoked eel from here is a winter gift along the whole cape.

1055.name: Thúy Cái Lâm
1055.look: On the hill slopes broad crowns of oak and lime meet overhead in an unbroken green roof.
1055.lore: Under its canopy the haze gathers green, and Thúy Vi's herb-gatherers find shade herbs here. The stonecutters do not quarry above it.

1056.name: Đồng Sơn Trấn
1056.look: On a wooded mountain shoulder empty stone houses stand around green-stained spoil heaps and the black mouths of old adits.
1056.lore: Miners built the town on a copper seam and cast bells and pots for the cape. When the seam gave out in 1094 the town emptied within a few years.

1057.name: Thạch Công Thôn
1057.look: A village of grey stone houses sits below a quarried hillside, blocks stacked by the road for the carts.
1057.lore: Its stonecutters quarry grey rock for the walls and quays of Yên Ba. Every house is built from stones its owner rejected.

1058.name: Mãn Diệp Lâm
1058.look: A low oak and maple forest stands behind the town, knee-deep in fallen leaves each autumn.
1058.lore: The townsfolk rake its leaves for compost and bedding. Children say whoever walks through it in autumn without a sound will have a year of luck.

1059.name: Hải Thúy Trấn
1059.look: A small walled town of grey roofs stands above a bay where the sea runs pale green over sand.
1059.lore: It trades fish, timber and hemp rope with Mục Ca and Bạch Sa. Its people say the green of the water is Thúy Vi's haze sunk into the sea.

1060.name: Tĩnh Mộc Lâm
1060.look: A dense inland forest where the air is so still that leaves do not stir even on windy days.
1060.lore: Birds are quiet here, and the hemp farmers avoid it. Thúy Vi sends restless disciples to sit in it, as it sends others to Vân Khởi Quán.

1061.name: Thằng Tác Thôn
1061.look: Tall hemp stands in clearings around a small village, retting pools and rope walks between the houses.
1061.lore: The villagers make rope and sailcloth for the boatwrights of Thuyền Ổ and the sailors of Phong Phàm. A cape sailor will tell you whose rope he trusts.

1062.name: Hắc Tùng Lâm
1062.look: Dark black pines crowd the flat ground east of the river, their trunks streaked with resin.
1062.lore: Travellers on the cape road hurry through it, for robbers once hid there. Since Vụ Ẩn Môn was founded nearby, the road has been safe.

1063.name: Vụ Ẩn Môn
1063.look: Low grey halls stand in the forest east of the river, nearly invisible inside a ring of standing stones that breathes out a thin green mist.
1063.lore: A neutral gate of formation masters sworn to Thúy Vi, who lay mist arrays along the cape's roads to hide travellers and confuse robbers. Its founder learned the Haze Walk at Thúy Vi and left to make the haze useful.

1064.name: Phù Kiều Trấn
1064.look: A walled river town of grey roofs, its two halves joined by a bridge of boats chained across the stream.
1064.lore: The cape's main road crosses the river here, and the town lives on tolls, inns and river trade. The bridge is taken apart before every spring flood and rebuilt after.

1065.name: Hải Điêu Nhai
1065.look: A wooded cliff above the oyster beds is crowned with huge stick nests and splashed white below them.
1065.lore: Sea eagles with wings longer than a boat nest here and snatch fish from the rakers' baskets. One took a child in 1170, and the village has hated them since.

1066.name: Mẫu Lệ Thôn
1066.look: A low village of grey roofs stands on the mudflats, with white heaps of oyster shells and lime kilns along the shore.
1066.lore: The villagers rake oysters at low tide and burn the shells for lime. Lime from here whitewashes the walls of Bạch Sa.

1067.name: Tùng La Lâm
1067.look: Grey-green lichen hangs in long beards from every branch of a damp coastal pine forest.
1067.lore: Healers gather the lichen for wounds and coughs. The healers of the ruined hall nearby first taught the villagers its use.

1068.name: Thanh Nang Đường
1068.look: A walled compound of low halls stands empty in the woods, its herb beds gone wild and its medicine cabinets standing open.
1068.lore: A small sect of healers sworn to Thúy Vi tended the cape's sick here for three centuries. Its last head died in closed-door cultivation in 1101 without naming an heir, and its disciples went to Hồng Lô Cốc.

1069.name: Hàm Ngư Thôn
1069.look: Rows of split fish dry on racks along a shore of salt pans, beside a village of grey roofs.
1069.lore: Fish is salted and dried here for the whole cape, and the smell carries a long way out to sea. Sailors say they can find the village in fog by nose.

1070.name: Thiết Trư Lâm
1070.look: Churned earth and tusk-gashed trunks fill a lowland wood, with wallows of black mud between the roots.
1070.lore: Iron boars with hide like plate root here and charge anything that comes near. The villagers fence their fields with stone because wood does not stop them.

1071.name: Lô Từ Thôn
1071.look: Bamboo rafts with tethered cormorants line a rocky inlet below a village of grey roofs.
1071.lore: Its fishers fish with tame cormorants, a ring on each bird's neck. Every bird has a name, and old birds are buried in the village graveyard.

1072.name: Cổ Đằng Lâm
1072.look: Thick old vines hang from tree to tree in a low forest, making green walls and dark rooms.
1072.lore: The vines are cut for baskets and rope, but grow back faster than anyone can cut them. Hunters say a man lost in it can be found a year later, sitting quietly, not knowing the time.

1073.name: Lăng Giác Thôn
1073.look: A village of grey roofs stands among square marsh ponds covered in water-chestnut leaves, small tub boats floating between them.
1073.lore: Villagers kneel in round tubs to pick the chestnuts and sell them in Yên Ba. A boiled bag of them is the cape's autumn street food.

1074.name: Ngưng Lục Lâm
1074.look: A forest of evergreen oaks on high ground, where moss covers every trunk and stone in deep green.
1074.lore: Wood qi gathers here thickly enough to be felt, and Thúy Vi disciples come to meditate under the trees. The tea farmers take their seedlings from its edges.

1075.name: Trà Viên Thôn
1075.look: Neat rows of tea bushes climb the cleared hillsides around a village of grey roofs, half in the haze.
1075.lore: The villagers say the haze gives their leaves their green. Thúy Vi buys the first picking for its seat and leaves the rest for Yên Ba.

1076.name: Huyền Băng Nhãn
1076.look: A round pool of black ice lies in the white tundra, so clear that one can see deep into the dark below.
1076.lore: Water qi rises through the ice, and alchemists cut blocks from it to cool their furnaces. The pool refreezes overnight however much is taken.

1077.name: Hắc Diệu Khoáng
1077.look: Black glassy rock glints from the flank of a volcanic cone, broken into sharp terraces where miners pry out blocks.
1077.lore: Miners cut obsidian for blades, mirrors and furnace windows. Hồng Lô Cốc buys the clearest pieces to watch its fires without opening the furnace.

1078.name: Cự Yết Nhai
1078.look: A warm rocky cliff below the fire spine is pocked with crevices, and pale husks of shed shells lie at its foot.
1078.lore: Giant scorpions shelter in the warm rock, kept alive in the cold by the heat underground. The goats will not climb it, and the herders trust the goats.

1079.name: Nhũ Lạc Thôn
1079.look: A village of grey roofs clings to a narrow coast below steep slopes, goats picking along the rocks above it.
1079.lore: The villagers keep goats on the slopes and fish below. Goat cheese from here is rubbed with volcanic salt and keeps all winter.

1080.name: Lưu Hỏa Khẩu
1080.look: High on a volcanic cone a crack glows orange, and a slow tongue of lava creeps from it down the black slope.
1080.lore: Fire qi pours from the vent, and Hồng Lô Cốc's alchemists come to light furnaces from it without sailing to the isles. They carry the fire home in clay pots packed with ash.

1081.name: Hải Báo Chử
1081.look: Grey seals crowd the flat rocks of a shoal below wooded cliffs, barking at passing boats.
1081.lore: A colony of seals hauls out here every winter, among them a few great spirit seals. Fishers leave them alone, for the big bulls have sunk boats.

1082.name: Lật Thụ Thôn
1082.look: Old chestnut trees shade a small village of grey roofs on the southern shore.
1082.lore: The villagers gather chestnuts in autumn and fish the rest of the year. Their roasted chestnuts are sold in the streets of Yên Ba at the first frost.

1083.name: Hải Lăng Trấn
