1083.look: On the shore stand the tops of old walls half-buried in sand, a stone quay running out into nothing.
1083.lore: The old port of the cape's end stood on a mound by the sea. A great storm in 1152 broke its harbour and filled it with sand, and its people moved up the coast to Tận Giác.

1084.name: Sơn Lam Huyệt
1084.look: In a wooded hollow on the hill above the town, a green haze wells up from the ground and spills over the rim.
1084.lore: Wood qi rises with the haze, and Thúy Vi disciples stationed at the cape's end cultivate here. The townsfolk read the weather in how far the haze spills.

1085.name: Tận Giác Trấn
1085.look: A walled town of grey roofs stands on grass at the far western tip, a stone beacon tower on the point beside it.
1085.lore: Ships rounding the cape stop here for water and pilots, and the town trades wool and fish. Its beacon is lit on stormy nights at the town's cost.

1086.name: Dương Quyển Thôn
1086.look: Round stone sheepfolds and well-heads dot a dry coastal steppe around a few low houses.
1086.lore: The villagers keep hardy sheep and sell their wool in Tận Giác. Every family digs its own well and guards it.

1087.name: Hoàng Thổ Nhãn
1087.look: A round patch of bare yellow earth lies in the green grass near the shore, warm to the touch even in winter.
1087.lore: Earth qi rises here, and nothing but a fine yellow moss grows on it. Thúy Vi disciples of the earth arts sit here barefoot.

1088.name: Vân Tước Thôn
1088.look: A small village of grey roofs sits in open grass by the sea, with beehives along its walls and skylarks singing overhead.
1088.lore: The villagers keep flocks and bees. They say a year without skylarks is a year without rain, and remember three.

1089.name: Sương Kiếm Môn
1089.look: On the cold shore the stone walls of a small sect stand half-buried in drifted snow, a row of rusted sword racks along the yard.
1089.lore: A small sect of sword cultivators trained here in the cold before any great sect held the cape. The winter of 468 buried its halls to the roofs, and the disciples who lived went south and did not return.

1090.name: Hàn Lộ Tuyền
1090.look: A small spring rises among frozen tussocks, never freezing, with frost feathers thick on every stem around it.
1090.lore: Water qi rises with the spring, and alchemists carry its water south for pills that cool the blood. In the coldest winter its steam can be seen a day's walk away.

1091.name: Tuyết Hiêu Đài
1091.look: A low flat rise in the tundra is scattered with white feathers and owl pellets, and pale shapes sit motionless on its stones.
1091.lore: Snow owls large enough to take a fox roost here. Hunters say they see a cultivator's qi as easily as a hare's heat.

1092.name: Kình Cốt Đường
1092.look: On the cold shore stands a long hall framed in whale ribs, its hide roof long gone and snow drifted inside.
1092.lore: A small sect of sea hunters sworn to Thúy Vi hunted sea beasts from this shore. In 884 its head went out after a great spirit whale and never came back, and the remaining disciples joined Hồng Lô Cốc.

1093.name: Bạch Hùng Cương
1093.look: A low stony ridge in the tundra is dug with snow dens and scattered with seal bones.
1093.lore: White bears come ashore from the sea ice in winter to den here. Sealers count the dens each spring and keep their camps far away.

1094.name: Lôi Điểu Nguyên
1094.look: A white plain of frozen marsh where flocks of white ptarmigan burst up at a step.
1094.lore: The flocks winter here in thousands, and their wings crack like thunder when they rise. Hunters net them, and some say a few birds carry thunder qi.

1095.name: Thiết Cốt Phong
1095.look: A bare dark peak streaked with rust-red stone rises above the frosted ridges.
1095.lore: Metal qi gathers in its iron-bearing rock, and sword cultivators climb it to temper their blades. Lightning strikes it more often than any other peak on the cape.

1096.name: Cự Mi Lâm
1096.look: An open forest of birch and pine is crossed by broad trails, the bark stripped high where great elk feed.
1096.lore: Great elk with antlers as wide as a cart gather here in autumn to fight for mates. The sea hunters leave the woods alone in that season.

1097.name: Liệp Hải Thôn
1097.look: Grey-roofed houses stand on the cold shore, skin boats upturned on racks and seal hides stretched along the walls.
1097.lore: The villagers hunt seals and fish, as sealers have on this coast since the Wild Age. They say their forebears were the ones who named the cape of snow and fire.

1098.name: Hà Ly Chử
1098.look: Stick dams and lodges choke a side stream into a chain of still ponds among gnawed stumps.
1098.lore: Spirit beavers build dams strong enough to hold a flood. The raftsmen break them every spring and the beavers rebuild them every summer.

1099.name: Phiệt Công Thôn
1099.look: Log rafts lie lashed along a forest river below a village of grey roofs, with stacked timber on the bank.
1099.lore: The raftsmen float logs downstream to the coast. A raftsman's rank is counted by how many springs he has ridden the flood.

1100.name: Vô Thanh Lâm
1100.look: A forest of moss-hung trees where no bird sings and footsteps make no sound on the deep moss.
1100.lore: Villagers say the quiet of Không Sơn Viện drifted north and settled here. Vân Khởi Quán sometimes sends novices to sit in it for a day.

1101.name: Tân Cư Thôn
1101.look: A village of grey roofs stands on a river bend in the forest, each door with a jar of pine resin by it.
1101.lore: Fishers of the Cold Ford who left the coast under Tùng Đào's resin tax founded it in 675. It is still called the new homes, and the resin jars are a joke about the tax.

1102.name: Phấn Điệp Lâm
1102.look: In early summer clouds of white butterflies rise from an open oak forest, settling on every leaf.
1102.lore: They come for a week and are gone, and the villagers say a soul rides on each one. No one sweeps the dead butterflies from the paths.

1103.name: Hồ Đào Thôn
1103.look: Tall walnut trees shade a village of grey roofs, with nut husks drying in black heaps in every yard.
1103.lore: The villagers press walnut oil for lamps and sell husk dye to the scribes of Lam Yên. Each child is given a walnut tree at birth.

1104.name: Độc Phong Cốc
1104.look: A wooded hollow is hung with grey paper nests as big as barrels, and the air hums.
1104.lore: Spirit hornets nest here, and their sting can kill a mortal. The forest wardens of Hộ Lâm Đường take their nests for poison.

1105.name: Hộ Lâm Đường
1105.look: A hall of dark timber stands on a wooded rise, its roof grown over with moss and a tall lookout platform in the oak beside it.
1105.lore: A righteous hall of forest wardens sworn to Thúy Vi, who guard the northern woods and gather herbs and spirit wood for its furnaces. It was founded after the Cold Ford came home, to keep the northern forests for the sect.

1106.name: Thủy Ma Thôn
1106.look: A row of waterwheels turns along a forest river beside a village of grey roofs, sacks of flour stacked on the banks.
1106.lore: The mills grind grain for all the northern villages. Millers are paid in a tenth of what they grind, and the scoop is kept in the village shrine.

1107.name: Tông Hùng Lâm
1107.look: A riverside forest of marsh and alder is torn with claw marks, fish carcasses scattered along the banks.
1107.lore: Brown bears fish the river in autumn beside the papermakers' vats. The village keeps a drum to frighten them off.

1108.name: Tạo Chỉ Thôn
1108.look: Sheets of paper dry on wooden frames along a river village, beside vats of soaking bark.
1108.lore: The villagers beat mulberry bark and hemp into paper for the copied scripture of Lam Yên Thị. A sheet that tears in the vat is never sold.

1109.name: Thương Thúy Lâm
1109.look: Old grey-green pines stand on rising ground, thick with lichen and hung with haze.
1109.lore: Its oldest pines grow the best poria, and the villagers guard the roots jealously. Thúy Vi disciples walking the road north rest in its shade.

1110.name: Cổ Dịch Trấn
1110.look: A street of empty inns and a collapsed post stable line an overgrown road through the pines.
1110.lore: It was the post town on the old road from the Cold Ford to Lam Yên. When the road was moved east in 975, its inns closed one by one.

1111.name: Phục Linh Thôn
1111.look: A small village of grey roofs in pine forest, with baskets of white poria lumps drying under the eaves.
1111.lore: The villagers dig poria fungus from old pine roots and sell it to Thúy Vi's furnaces. They plant a pine for each one they dig.

1112.name: Sơ Hiểu Lâm
1112.look: A mixed forest of ash and oak echoes with birdsong from dawn until mid-morning.
1112.lore: Bird-catchers come here for songbirds to sell in Lam Yên. Thúy Vi forbids nets in the spring nesting season.

1113.name: Bạch Lạp Thôn
1113.look: Ash trees around a village of grey roofs are crusted white with insect wax on their branches.
1113.lore: The villagers raise wax insects and scrape white wax for candles and pill coatings. Thúy Vi buys most of it for its furnaces.

1114.name: Thanh Mộc Mạch
1114.look: A line of unusually tall trees runs straight through the forest, greener than the woods on either side.
1114.lore: Wood qi runs along the line under the ground, and trees planted on it outgrow all others. Thúy Vi's disciples follow the line to cultivate.

1115.name: Bối Độ Thôn
1115.look: A village of grey roofs sits beside a wide river that runs thin and white over flat stones.
1115.lore: Its people fish the shallows and carry travellers across on their backs. They know every stone of the ford by name.

1116.name: Bách Thảo Viện
1116.look: The scorched shell of an academy stands among wild herb beds, its central furnace hall blown open from inside.
1116.lore: A small herb academy sworn to Thúy Vi kept a hundred kinds of herbs in its beds. In 932 a cauldron of untamed pill fire burst and destroyed the halls; Thúy Vi took its herb books to the seat.

1117.name: Linh Lộ Tuyền
1117.look: A spring in the forest floor seeps into a mossy hollow where heavy dew lies on every leaf all day.
1117.lore: Wood qi rises with the water, and herbs gathered there with the dew on them are prized. Alchemists come before dawn to collect the dew itself.

1118.name: Tử Tô Thôn
1118.look: Plots of purple perilla and other herbs line the river below a small village of grey roofs.
1118.lore: The villagers grow herbs for the alchemists and learned their plots from the ruined academy nearby. Its purple leaves are dried for tea along the coast.

1119.name: Ngọc Trụ Phong
1119.look: A tall pale pillar of stone rises out of the cloud that fills the valleys around it.
1119.lore: Earth qi gathers in its pale rock. Hermits live in caves halfway up and come down only when the clouds lift.

1120.name: Hàn Uyên Nhãn
1120.look: A dark round hole in the tundra ice opens onto deep water that never freezes, breathing a thin mist.
1120.lore: Water qi wells up from far below, cold enough to numb a hand in a moment. Alchemists lower jars on long cords to fill them.

1121.name: Bạch Tinh Khoáng
1121.look: A narrow adit on a mountain slope spills white tailings glittering with crystal.
1121.lore: Miners dig clear quartz for formation stones and pill vials. Vụ Ẩn Môn buys its best crystals for its mist arrays.

1122.name: Tê Hạc Phong
1122.look: A grey rocky peak east of the seat, its ledges dotted with roosting cranes.
1122.lore: Metal qi gathers in the rock, and the cranes return to it each spring. Thúy Vi disciples climb it to practise sword forms among the birds.

1123.name: Vọng Bắc Bảo
1123.look: A small stone fort stands on a wooded spur above the north road, its walls intact and its gate gone.
1123.lore: Thúy Vi built it the year Tùng Đào took the Cold Ford, to watch the road north. After the Cold Ford came home in 905 it was left empty.

1124.name: Thụ Tâm Nhãn
1124.look: A vast old tree stands alone in a clearing, a hollow at its heart glowing faintly green at night.
1124.lore: Wood qi rises through the tree's hollow heart. Villagers leave buckwheat cakes at its roots, and Thúy Vi disciples sit inside the hollow.

1125.name: Hoa Mạch Thôn
1125.look: Clearings of white-flowering buckwheat surround a village of grey roofs deep in the forest.
1125.lore: Buckwheat grows where rice will not, and its flour goes to Lam Yên for noodles. The villagers bless the fields when the flowers open.

1126.name: Thâm U Lâm
1126.look: A dense coastal forest so dark under its canopy that moss grows on the paths.
1126.lore: Herb gatherers from the town find shade herbs here that grow nowhere else. They tie cords to the trees to find their way back.

1127.name: Minh Kính Đường
1127.look: A burnt hall stands in a ring of lightning-split trees, a cracked bronze mirror still hanging over its door.
1127.lore: A small sect of heart-mirror cultivators sworn to Thúy Vi. In 1066 its head tried to break through to Nguyên Anh, and his tribulation burned the hall and killed him; the disciples scattered.

1128.name: Lãm Thúy Trấn
1128.look: A walled town of grey roofs on the eastern shore, its quay stacked with timber and bales of herbs.
1128.lore: It trades timber, fish and herbs from the eastern forests along the coast. Its herb buyers are said to grade a root by smell alone.

1129.name: Nhạn Hồi Phong
1129.look: A sharp grey peak stands so high that migrating geese turn aside around it.
1129.lore: Metal qi gathers in its bare rock. Its south face is said to be too cold even for the geese.

1130.name: Vân Gian Trấn
1130.look: High on a mountain shoulder the roofs of a small stone town poke out of a slope of old rubble and grass.
1130.lore: A mountain town of herb growers and porters on the path to the western ridges. An avalanche in 1019 buried its upper street, and the survivors went down to Lam Yên Thị.

1131.name: Thương Ngọc Khoáng
1131.look: A cut in the mountain below the cliff shows bands of blue-green stone, with a ramp down to the road.
1131.lore: Thúy Vi opened it long after Bích Ngọc Khoáng, to dig a bluer, harder jade. Its stone is carved into talismans and furnace lids.

1132.name: Đoạn Vân Nhai
1132.look: A sheer grey cliff rises above the forest, and drifting clouds part around its edge.
1132.lore: Metal qi gathers in its sharp rock. Sword cultivators say the cliff cut the clouds before they learned to.

1133.name: Lãnh Thiết Khoáng
1133.look: A dark mine mouth on a sheer slope, with frost on the iron ore heaped outside even in summer.
1133.lore: Its iron stays cold to the touch long after forging. Thúy Vi uses it for furnace fittings that must not grow hot.

1134.name: Lăng Không Đỉnh
1134.look: A bare summit of grey rock juts out over a drop so deep that its foot is lost in haze.
1134.lore: Metal qi gathers in its rock. Thúy Vi elders stand on the edge to test their nerve before breakthrough.

1135.name: Nghiên Thạch Khoáng
1135.look: Small pits along a river bank show fine dark stone, with half-cut inkstones drying on the rocks.
1135.lore: Its fine black stone makes inkstones for the scholars of Lam Yên. Miners test each block by grinding ink on it before they sell.

1136.name: Hàm Vân Phong
1136.look: A rounded forested peak with a band of cloud resting on its shoulder most mornings.
1136.lore: Earth qi gathers in its stone, and the cloud seldom leaves. The monks of Vân Khởi say it holds what their own mountain lets go.

1137.name: Ngưu Bối Phong
1137.look: A long rounded peak by the river, shaped like the back of a lying ox.
1137.lore: Earth qi gathers along its spine. Herdsmen below say a cultivator who sleeps on it wakes heavier and calmer.

1138.name: Nhuyễn Thạch Khoáng
1138.look: A small pit at the foot of the ridge by the shore shows soft pale grey stone, with carved bowls drying on a rack.
1138.lore: Villagers dig soapstone here for bowls, moulds and pill moulds. They dig only at the foot, far below the academy.

1139.name: Độc Tọa Phong
1139.look: A narrow rocky peak above Không Sơn Viện, with a single flat stone at its top big enough for one person.
1139.lore: Earth qi gathers in its stone, and Không Sơn's masters sat on it alone. Thúy Vi lets no one climb it, and the stone is still clean.

1140.name: Quan Nhật Phong
1140.look: The highest bare peak of the ridges, its summit catching the first light long before the valleys.
1140.lore: Metal qi gathers in its rock. From its top one can see the cape and the eastern sea at once.

1141.name: Tuyết Thố Nguyên
1141.look: A white tundra plain crossed by countless small tracks, hares bounding away at every step.
1141.lore: Snow hares breed here in their thousands, and a few spirit hares are as quick as a sword cut. Foxes and owls hunt them from all over the north.

1142.name: Vạn Tùng Phong
1142.look: A high peak covered to its top in pines, dark green against the bare mountains around it.
1142.lore: Wood qi gathers in its pines. The soot burners of Tùng Yên cut only the dead trees on it.

1143.name: Tùng Yên Thôn
1143.look: A village of grey roofs on a forested slope, with long brick soot kilns climbing the hill behind it.
1143.lore: The villagers burn pine in long kilns and press the soot into ink. Their ink goes with the inkstones of Lưu Thúy to the scholars of three sects.

1144.name: Ngô Công Cốc
1144.look: A damp wooded valley above the orchards, with rotting logs crawling with red centipedes.
1144.lore: Giant centipedes live in its rot, and the biggest are as long as a man. Hồng Lô Cốc pays for their venom.

1145.name: Hải Đường Thôn
1145.look: Pink crabapple orchards surround a village of grey roofs on the coast.
1145.lore: The villagers fish and sell crabapple blossom and fruit in Lam Yên. The blossom is pressed into the pages of scripture beside Thu Diệp's leaves.

1146.name: Thanh Lang Lĩnh
1146.look: A wooded hill ridge where packs of grey wolves have worn paths along the crest.
1146.lore: Grey wolves hunt the ridge in packs, and the oldest are said to be clever as men. Villagers do not walk it after dark.

1147.name: Đồng Du Thôn
1147.look: Tung trees with white blossoms ring a village of grey roofs, and oil presses stand in every yard.
1147.lore: The villagers press tung oil for boats, paint and lamps. Every boat on the coast is sealed with it.

1148.name: Tuyến Thiên Hạp
1148.look: A limestone gorge so narrow and deep that only a thin line of sky shows overhead.
1148.lore: The lime-burners take a short cut through it to the coast. In the noon light alone the gorge floor is lit, and then only for a moment.

1149.name: Thiêu Hôi Thôn
1149.look: White lime kilns smoke among limestone knolls beside a small village of white-dusted grey roofs.
1149.lore: The villagers burn limestone for lime and sell it to builders along the coast. Their houses are the whitest in the ridges.

1150.name: Thận Lâu Các
1150.look: On the frozen shore the stone base of a tall pavilion stands empty, its upper floors fallen onto the beach.
1150.lore: A small sect that studied the mirages of the northern sea built its pavilion here. In 497 its head walked out on the sea ice after a mirage of a city and never returned, and the disciples left.

1151.name: Lăng Hàn Huyệt
1151.look: In the frozen tundra a small hollow of open water steams among frosted pines.
1151.lore: Water qi wells up and keeps the hollow ice-free all winter. Thúy Vi disciples of the water arts sit beside it through the coldest month.

1152.name: Hàn Thiềm Chử
1152.look: Black peat pools are ringed with frosted moss, and pale toads sit motionless at the water's edge.
1152.lore: Frost toads sing here all summer and sleep frozen in the mud all winter. Their skin is a cooling medicine.

1153.name: Dã Ngưu Chử
1153.look: A trampled marsh island in the forest, its mud churned by heavy hooves.
1153.lore: Herds of wild forest bison graze here in summer. The villagers hunt one each autumn and no more.

1154.name: Tĩnh Tuyết Tự
1154.look: Low stone halls stand half-buried in snow on the cold shore, a row of flat meditation stones before them.
1154.lore: Monks sat in the snow here and cultivated stillness. The last monk died in 455 with no novices, and the temple was left to the snow.

1155.name: Nghịch Triều Thôn
1155.look: A village of grey roofs stands on a river where the tide turns the current back upstream twice a day.
1155.lore: The villagers fish the river and its backwaters and time their boats by the returning current. Children learn the tides before they learn to count.

1156.name: Tuyết Bào Nguyên
1156.look: A tundra plain along a frozen river, crossed by the light tracks of roe deer.
1156.lore: Snow roe deer winter along the frozen banks. Hunters say they can run on thin ice without breaking it.

1157.name: Bão Nhất Quán
1157.look: On a high crag a few roofless stone halls stand around a dry spring, prayer stones scattered on the ground.
1157.lore: A small Daoist abbey older than Không Sơn Viện kept its hermits here. Its spring dried, and the last abbot went down to Không Sơn Viện as a guest in 488.

1158.name: Tùng Linh Mạch
1158.look: A grove of very old pines stands among the tundra, its needles greener than any other trees on the coast.
1158.lore: Wood qi rises under the grove. Hunters say the oldest pine has a spirit, and they leave a little food at its roots.

1159.name: Phi Thử Lâm
1159.look: A tall forest where flying squirrels glide from trunk to trunk at dusk.
1159.lore: Spirit flying squirrels nest here, and their skins make light gloves. They steal berries from the villagers' roofs.

1160.name: Hoành Kiều Trấn
1160.look: A stone bridge spans a dry hollow in the forest beside the empty walls of a small town.
1160.lore: The town grew around a bridge on the river. A flood in 1148 moved the river west and left the bridge over dry ground, and the town followed the water.

1161.name: Việt Quất Thôn
1161.look: A small village of grey roofs in northern forest, with red berries spread on mats on every roof.
1161.lore: The villagers pick lingonberries and trap fur. Berry jam from here keeps all winter and travels to Hàn Tân.

1162.name: U Lam Lâm
1162.look: A pine wood in a hollow where mist lies all morning, the trunks fading into grey.
1162.lore: The ink-makers say pine from the misty wood gives the softest soot. Travellers lose the path here easily.

1163.name: Tùng Mặc Thôn
1163.look: Low sheds with long clay flues climb a slope, black soot coating every roof, and rows of ink cakes dry on boards in the shade.
1163.lore: Villagers burn pine in long flues, scrape the soot and pound it with glue into ink cakes. Tùng Mặc ink is sold in every sect library of the north.

1164.name: Manh Nha Mạch
1164.look: A hillside where young pines grow thick and fast, and the snow melts weeks before anywhere else.
1164.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi wakes the hill early each spring. Tùng Đào's foresters gather seedlings here for replanting the cut slopes.

1165.name: Phạt Mộc Thôn
1165.look: A woodcutters' village with log slides running downhill and stacks of marked logs by the road.
1165.lore: Its woodcutters fell only trees marked by Tùng Đào's foresters. A tree cut without a mark costs the cutter a year's work.

1166.name: Lăng Vân Lâm
1166.look: On high slopes, tall firs rise through drifting cloud, their tops showing above it like masts.
1166.lore: The forest is often above the clouds, and Tùng Đào's disciples climb to cultivate in its thin air. The beekeepers will not go higher than its edge.

1167.name: Tùng Mật Thôn
1167.look: Hollow-log hives hang in the pines around a small village, and the air hums with bees.
1167.lore: Its beekeepers make a dark, resinous pine honey sold on the palace road. They say their bees learn the pine waves too.

1168.name: Huyền Báo Nhai
1168.look: A dark crag in the forest, its ledges strewn with bones and its rock marked with black hairs.
1168.lore: Black leopards den in its caves and hunt the forest by night. The mushroom gatherers carry bells to warn them off.

1169.name: Hương Khuẩn Thôn
1169.look: Racks of drying mushrooms line every house, and the village smells of earth and woodsmoke.
1169.lore: Its people gather mushrooms from fallen pine and dry them for the markets. They go out in pairs, for the leopards above.

1170.name: Hậu Thổ Mạch
1170.look: On a steep hillside, a broad shelf of dark earth holds no trees, only thick grass and a few heavy boulders.
1170.lore: A spirit vein of Earth qi runs under the shelf, heavy and slow. Tùng Đào's disciples who lean to earth come here, though few of them do.

1171.name: Cát Chi Thôn
1171.look: A valley village whose pines bear neat cuts above clay cups, and pots of golden resin cool on the doorsteps.
1171.lore: Its people tap pine resin for incense and varnish. The foresters count the cuts on every tree each autumn.

1172.name: Hải Vận Lâm
1172.look: A pine wood on a hill whose crowns roar in the wind exactly like surf on a beach.
1172.lore: Pilgrims who stop here sometimes never go on to the palace, saying they have heard enough. Tùng Đào's disciples call it the near sea.

1173.name: Hương Khách Thôn
1173.look: A village of inns and tea stalls on the pilgrims' road, incense smoke drifting from every door.
1173.lore: It lives by lodging pilgrims bound for the palace ridge. Innkeepers sell pine cones as keepsakes.

1174.name: Bạch Viên Lĩnh
1174.look: A high ridge of fir and rock where white-furred apes sit on the boulders, watching the valley.
1174.lore: White apes hold the ridge and throw stones at anyone who climbs. They drove out the ginseng diggers of Thải Sâm Trấn in 979.

1175.name: Thải Sâm Trấn
1175.look: On a high slope, the stone walls of a small town are tumbled and grown with ferns, and dug pits pock the ground around it.
1175.lore: Ginseng diggers built this town when the roots were plentiful. As the ginseng ran out they dug higher, into the apes' ridge, and in 979 the apes drove them out.

1176.name: Tiều Phu Thôn
1176.look: A hamlet of log houses on a high slope, firewood stacked to the eaves.
1176.lore: Its woodsmen sell firewood and charcoal to Vạn Hác. They keep clear of the white apes above.

1177.name: Ải Tùng Lâm
1177.look: On bare high rock, a low forest of dwarf pines no taller than a man crouches against the wind.
1177.lore: The dwarf pines are said to be as old as the palace. Shepherds shelter their flocks among them in storms.

1178.name: Dương Lan Thôn
1178.look: A high village of dry-stone sheepfolds, goats and sheep spread over the meadows above it.
1178.lore: Its shepherds graze goats and sheep in the clearings and high meadows and pen them at night against the apes and leopards. They make hard cheese for Vạn Hác.

1179.name: Xích Bì Lâm
1179.look: A wood of old pines with bright red bark, glowing in the evening sun.
1179.lore: These are among the oldest pines in the pine sea. Tùng Đào's foresters mark none for cutting.

1180.name: Phù Mộc Thôn
1180.look: A river village whose beaches are heaped with driftwood, bleached and sorted by size, and log booms tied along the bank.
1180.lore: Its people gather driftwood from the river and float logs downstream to the lowland towns. They build their houses only from wood the river has brought them.

1181.name: Thanh Hư Mạch
1181.look: A still grove of pine and bamboo on a high slope, where no wind moves the leaves.
1181.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi rises in the grove, and the stillness helps cultivators empty their minds. Vạn Hác's students come to rest their ears.

1182.name: Biên Trúc Thôn
1182.look: A village enclosed by woven bamboo fences, baskets and mats drying in every yard.
1182.lore: Its people weave bamboo goods and sell them at Cổ Độ. The bamboo here is the first of the south, and the villagers cut only stems older than three years.

1183.name: Vọng Triều Các
1183.look: On a bare shore, the stone base of a pavilion faces the sea, its steps running down into the water.
1183.lore: A small sect of water arts that cultivated the rhythm of the tide. Its last master walked into the winter sea in 468 to cultivate the tide and never came back; within two years its disciples went to Tùng Đào Cung.

1184.name: Lãnh Triều Tuyền
1184.look: In the woods behind the shore a cold spring wells up into a stone basin, its water salt-cold and smelling faintly of the sea.
1184.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring, its flow strongest at the high tide. The tide-watchers of Vọng Triều Các drew their water from it for two centuries.

1185.name: Bích Lạc Phong
1185.look: A bare rock peak above the pines, its summit standing in clear blue sky above the clouds.
1185.lore: A peak of Metal qi rises over sixteen hundred metres here. Tùng Đào's disciples climb it in summer to temper their arts in its thin, cold air.

1186.name: Bán Sơn Thôn
1186.look: A village of stone houses halfway up a forested mountain, terraced herb beds below it.
1186.lore: It lives by goats, herbs and the disciples who climb to the peak. Its people guide them up for a fee.

1187.name: Thúy Trâm Phong
1187.look: A slender, green-grey spire of rock rises above the forest like a hairpin thrust into the clouds.
1187.lore: A peak of Earth and Metal qi, its rock streaked with pale green. Climbers say it sings faintly in the wind, and the goat herders of Vân Ổ will not climb past its shoulder.

1188.name: Vân Ổ Thôn
1188.look: A village in a high hollow, often sunk in cloud, with goat pens and stone huts.
1188.lore: Its villagers herd goats and gather mountain herbs. They can find their way in cloud by the sound of goat bells.

1189.name: Thâm Vụ Lâm
1189.look: A high fir forest swallowed by mist most days, its trunks dripping.
1189.lore: The mist never lifts for long, and the villagers will not enter it without a rope. Mosses here are prized by alchemists.

1190.name: Hàn Thạch Trấn
1190.look: On a high mountain shelf, the roofs of a stone town poke out of a field of tumbled rock and old snow.
1190.lore: A quarry town that cut stone for Tùng Đào's halls. In the winter of 1151 an avalanche buried it, and the survivors moved down to Lạc Thạch.

1191.name: Lạc Thạch Thôn
1191.look: A village of stone houses among boulders under the crags, millstones stacked by the road.
1191.lore: Villagers quarry the stones that fall in spring and carve millstones. They remember Hàn Thạch Trấn.

1192.name: Tử Sam Lâm
1192.look: A dark wood of old yews with red, peeling bark and poisonous red berries.
1192.lore: The bowyers take only fallen branches. Cattle that stray in sicken from the berries.

1193.name: Thảo Pha Thôn
1193.look: A village on a grassy slope, cattle grazing around it and yew bows drying under the eaves.
1193.lore: Its people graze cattle and make yew bows. It is the warmest village in the pine sea.

1194.name: Phi Thử Nhai
1194.look: A high crag above the forest where big furred shapes glide from ledge to ledge at dusk.
1194.lore: Giant spirit flying squirrels nest in the crag and steal from the village stores. Villagers hang their food in sealed jars.

1195.name: Thạch Tỉnh Thôn
1195.look: Stone houses with slab roofs ring a deep well cut through the rock, its rim worn smooth by ropes, and green-stained copper diggings scar the slope above.
1195.lore: The village grew around the well, which has never run dry even in the drought years, and its people herd goats and dig a little copper ore for the smiths of Cổ Độ. Every family hangs a bell over the well on the night a child is born.

1196.name: Hôi Thiết Khoáng
1196.look: On a bare mountain slope, small mine mouths open in grey rock under the grey pines.
1196.lore: The mine digs grey iron ore from the high rock. Tùng Đào's watch on Thương Tùng Mạch guards it too.

1197.name: Độc Phong Lâm
1197.look: A wood humming with hornets, their paper nests hanging from the branches like lanterns.
1197.lore: Venom hornets as long as a finger nest here. Alchemists pay well for their venom.

1198.name: Tửu Phường Thôn
1198.look: A village of brewhouses and wine jars, the air sharp with pine.
1198.lore: Its brewers make pine-needle wine and sell it on the road to Cổ Độ. The wine is said to taste of the wind in the pines.

1199.name: Tỏa Thiết Khoáng
1199.look: On a high slope, black spoil heaps run down from a timbered adit, and rusted ore carts lie where the old track ends.
1199.lore: The mine digs dark iron ore; old miners say iron from here went into the chain of Thiết Tỏa Quan, which gave the mine its name. It is worked again today by the people of Quan Hạ.

1200.name: Đoạn Liên Phong
1200.look: A bare peak above the fort, from which the river road can be seen far below.
1200.lore: A peak of Metal qi, named for the chain that broke below it in 508. Tùng Đào's elders bring disciples to its summit to look down at the river.

1201.name: Quan Hạ Thôn
1201.look: A village of stone houses under the broken walls of Thiết Tỏa Quan.
1201.lore: Its people herd goats and work the iron mine above. They guide Tùng Đào's elders and disciples to the fort.

1202.name: Thương Lang Cương
1202.look: A forested knoll with wolf trails worn into the moss and bones scattered at its foot.
1202.lore: Grey wolves den here and hunt the forest and tundra. The fox hunters leave them carcasses each winter to keep the peace.

1203.name: Liệp Hồ Thôn
1203.look: A northern village of log houses, fox pelts stretched on every wall.
1203.lore: Its hunters trap foxes and fish the coast in summer. They pay the grey wolves a share of every winter's catch by leaving carcasses on the knoll.

1204.name: Tịch Tĩnh Lâm
1204.look: A still pine forest where the wind seems to stop at the edge.
1204.lore: Birdsong carries for a mile here. The monks of Khô Mộc Tự meditated among its trees.

1205.name: Khô Mộc Tự
1205.look: In the forest, the halls of a temple stand roofless around a huge dead tree, grey and bare.
1205.lore: A small sect that cultivated the stillness of withered wood. In 641 its abbot's art turned on him and he withered with his tree; his monks scattered, and the village kept the graves.

1206.name: Thủ Mộ Thôn
1206.look: A quiet village at the edge of an old temple's graveyard, its people sweeping the stones.
1206.lore: Its villagers keep the graves of Khô Mộc Tự and gather firewood and fungus. They were the temple's servants once.

1207.name: Lục Vân Lâm
1207.look: A misty green forest where moss hangs from every branch.
1207.lore: The fungus gatherers find their best logs here. It is green and misty even in late autumn.

1208.name: Hắc Nhĩ Thôn
1208.look: A damp village where logs stacked by the houses are crusted with dark wood-ear fungus, and baskets of it dry on the eaves.
1208.lore: Its people grow and gather black wood-ear fungus on fallen logs. Their dried fungus is sold at Tùng Gian Thành, and the best of it goes up to the palace kitchens.

1209.name: Thúy Ba Mạch
1209.look: Rolling green hills where the pines ripple like waves in the wind.
1209.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the hills. Tùng Đào's disciples cultivate here in spring.

1210.name: Tùng Hoa Thôn
1210.look: A village whose roofs turn yellow with pollen each spring, and cloths spread to catch it.
1210.lore: Villagers collect pine pollen for cakes and medicine. Tùng Đào's alchemists buy most of it.

1211.name: Thủy Sam Lâm
1211.look: A grove of tall dawn redwoods along the river, their feathery needles turning red in autumn.
1211.lore: These trees grow only by the river and are protected by the foresters. Their wood is light and floats well.

1212.name: Mộc Tập Trấn
1212.look: A river town of timber yards and log ponds, its wharves stacked with marked logs.
1212.lore: The timber of the north is gathered here and sold at a fair each spring. Tùng Đào's foresters check every brand.

1213.name: Trực Cán Lâm
1213.look: A forest of tall, straight pines like ship masts.
1213.lore: The mast pines are guarded by foresters and cut only for the shipyards. A crooked tree here is a rare sight.

1214.name: Lâu Thuyền Trấn
1214.look: A coastal town of shipyards and slipways, half-built hulls rising like ribs.
1214.lore: It builds Tùng Đào's coastal ships and Lãng Đào's sea-going barges. Its shipwrights are the best in the north.

1215.name: Tạp Mộc Lâm
1215.look: A rolling wood where pines stand among oak, birch and maple, the floor deep in acorns and broad fallen leaves.
1215.lore: The firewood gatherers of Thải Tân take its deadwood, and its acorns fatten the wild boar that the villagers hunt each autumn. Tùng Đào's foresters leave it unmarked, since its timber is too crooked for ships or halls.

1216.name: Thải Tân Thôn
1216.look: A plain village with firewood stacked along every road.
1216.lore: Its villagers gather firewood and sell it to the coast towns. They are proud of their plain lives.

1217.name: Hải Phong Lâm
1217.look: On the low coast, a pine forest stands bent inland by the wind, its seaward trees dwarfed and salt-burned and its inner trees tall and straight.
1217.lore: The fishers of Triều Thanh read the weather by the sound of the wind in its crowns, and they gather pine pitch here to caulk their boats. Its windbreak keeps the salt off the village gardens.

1218.name: Triều Thanh Thôn
1218.look: A fishing village of grey roofs by the sea.
1218.lore: Its fishers listen to the tide to know when to sail. The sea wind bends the pines around it.

1219.name: Tĩnh Thủy Quán
1219.look: In the woods, the mud-filled halls of an abbey stand with water marks high on their walls.
1219.lore: A small sect that cultivated the stillness of water. The great flood of 700 drowned it along with three villages, and the survivors went to Tùng Đào two years later.

1220.name: Nhu Thủy Mạch
1220.look: A hollow near the river where a spring seeps through moss into a pool so soft that stones on its bed are worn round as eggs.
1220.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here, gentle and slow. Tùng Đào's water cultivators come to learn patience at it, and the drowned monks of Tĩnh Thủy Quán once did the same.

1221.name: Điếu Đài Thôn
1221.look: A river village whose bank is stepped with flat stone terraces, each with a fisher sitting on it and a long rod over the current.
1221.lore: Each family owns its own terrace and passes it down with the house. The village sells its catch at Đào Thanh, and the oldest terrace is said to be older than the levees.

1222.name: Phong Thụ Lâm
1222.look: A maple forest behind the village that turns red in autumn.
1222.lore: The villagers tap maple sap in spring and boil it into syrup for the river towns. Cormorant fishers judge the autumn fish run by how red the leaves have turned.

1223.name: Lô Chu Thôn
1223.look: A river village of grey roofs where black cormorants perch on the gunwales of narrow boats, rings around their necks.
1223.lore: Its people fish the slow reaches with trained cormorants that bring back fish they cannot swallow. They sell their catch at Đào Thanh and give each bird the seventh fish.

1224.name: Dã Ngưu Nguyên
1224.look: A broad clearing in the forest, its grass grazed short and churned by hooves, where shaggy dark oxen stand in a wary herd.
1224.lore: Wild oxen graze here and charge anyone who comes between them and their calves. Hunters of Phủ Tạc take one or two in winter, and the carpenters buy their horn for glue.

1225.name: Phủ Tạc Thôn
1225.look: A forest village of open-sided workshops where boat ribs, cartwheels and roof beams lie half-shaped in the wood shavings.
1225.lore: Its carpenters build boats, carts and houses for the river towns and are hired as far as Tùng Gian. Each apprentice carves his own mallet before he may touch a chisel.

1226.name: Du Âm Lâm
1226.look: A strip of old elms between the fields and the north wind, their broad crowns throwing deep shade.
1226.lore: The elms shelter the fields of Mạch Hương from the wind. In hard years the villagers eat the young elm seeds, and they call the wood their second granary.

1227.name: Mạch Hương Thôn
1227.look: A river village of grey roofs among fields of barley and wheat on the flood flats, with threshing floors by every house.
1227.lore: Its people sow the flats as soon as the spring flood drains and send their grain to the granaries of Lâm Hạ. At harvest the whole bend smells of bread.

1228.name: Hắc Hoa Lâm
1228.look: A damp riverside wood of dark-barked birches, their trunks grey-black and shaggy with curling bark.
1228.lore: Black birch bark is stripped here for roofing the riverside houses. The ferrymen cut their poles from its straight young trees.

1229.name: Hoành Độ Thôn
1229.look: A river village where a broad flat ferry hauls across the river on a rope, and carts wait in line at the landing.
1229.lore: Its people run the ferry across the Nine-Bend River here and fish between crossings. Lãng Đào takes a share of the fares and keeps the rope in repair.

1230.name: Cự Hoan Cương
1230.look: A knoll dug full of badger burrows, their mouths ringed with heaps of fresh earth.
1230.lore: Giant badgers dig here and raid the ox feed. Their burrows can break an ox's leg.

1231.name: Giá Ngưu Thôn
1231.look: A village of ox pens and yoke sheds in a forest clearing, its lanes deep in hoof-churned mud.
1231.lore: Its people breed and drive oxen for the river towns' carts. Oxen from here haul the timber down to the river.

1232.name: Bích Lưu Mạch
1232.look: A green pool beside the river, fed by a current that runs clear and jade-green even when the river beside it is brown with flood.
1232.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi runs here, and the villagers of Hà Đê say it never floods. Tùng Đào's disciples cultivate on the levee above it.

1233.name: Hà Đê Thôn
1233.look: A village behind a long earth levee, its houses below the level of the river in flood.
1233.lore: Its people farm the flats and mend the levee every spring. The levee was raised after the flood of 700.

1234.name: Sương Diệp Lâm
1234.look: A wood of oak and maple behind the village whose leaves turn red with the first frost, weeks before the rest of the river.
1234.lore: The villagers watch it to know the season: when its leaves turn early, they say, the winter will be hard. Its fallen oak wood feeds the mill fires.

1235.name: Thủy Xa Thôn
1235.look: A river village where tall bamboo waterwheels creak on the bank, lifting buckets of water into wooden troughs that run to the fields.
1235.lore: Its people lift river water to their fields with the wheels and grind grain with a smaller wheel by the mill. Each wheel is rebuilt every ten years from the same pattern.

1236.name: Bách Thảo Mạch
1236.look: A hillside clearing so thick with herbs of every kind that its air smells bitter and sweet at once.
1236.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi feeds the herbs, and plants grow here that grow nowhere else in the basin. Thải Chi Cốc's alchemists prize them and send a gatherer each spring.

1237.name: Bối Dược Thôn
1237.look: A hill village where tall carrying baskets hang by every door and herbs dry in bundles from the eaves.
1237.lore: Its people gather wild herbs on the hills and carry them on their backs down to Thải Chi Cốc. Herb gatherers come from all over the basin.

1238.name: Thương Bách Lâm
1238.look: A wood of grey-green cypresses on the hill above the village, their scent sharp in the cold air.
1238.lore: Cypress from here is used for coffins and shrine beams. The villagers of Thạch Lũy bury their dead under its trees.

1239.name: Thạch Lũy Thôn
1239.look: A village with stone walls around its fields, built from the stones they cleared.
1239.lore: Its people build stone walls from the stones they clear. They farm and gather firewood.

1240.name: Hàn Tinh Tuyền
1240.look: A cold spring in the open tundra, its still pool so clear that on winter nights it holds the stars like a second sky.
1240.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring. Tùng Đào's disciples come in summer, the only season the walk is possible.

1241.name: Cựu Đạo Lâm
1241.look: A long, narrow wood of willow and alder growing in a winding line across the meadow, following the dry bed of the old river.
1241.lore: The trees took root on the bed the river left in 280, and their line still shows its old bends. Since the flood of 1198, children from Tân Lưu dig among the roots for coins of Đông Lưu Thành.

1242.name: Tân Lưu Trấn
1242.look: A river town on the new course of the river, its wharves busy with boats.
1242.lore: It grew on the new current after the river left Đông Lưu Thành. Its people fish, farm and trade.

1243.name: Ngư Ưng Đài
1243.look: A rock above the river where ospreys nest, their great stick nests piled on its ledges.
1243.lore: Ospreys nest here and fish the river. The villagers watch them for the fish runs.

1244.name: Độc Mộc Thôn
1244.look: A river village on both banks, joined by one huge pine trunk laid across a narrow, rocky stretch of the river, with dugout canoes pulled up below.
1244.lore: Its people cross the river on the log and carve dugout canoes from single trunks. When the log rots, the whole village goes up the hill together to fell the next one.

1245.name: Vân Tùng Lâm
1245.look: A pine forest high on the hill, its crowns lost in low cloud on most mornings and dripping with mist.
1245.lore: Tùng Đào's disciples climb here to cultivate in the mist among the pines. The villagers of Sài Môn gather pine nuts only on its lower edge.

1246.name: Sài Môn Thôn
1246.look: A quiet hill village of thatched houses, each with a gate of woven brushwood and a pine-nut tree in the yard.
1246.lore: Its people gather firewood and pine nuts and keep to themselves. Retired outer disciples of Tùng Đào sometimes settle here to grow old in quiet.

1247.name: Thiên Trụ Lâm
1247.look: A forest of tall, straight, branchless pines standing like the pillars of an endless hall, their crowns far overhead.
1247.lore: The pines are so straight that Tùng Đào's builders once came here for hall pillars, and the stumps of that cutting still show. The truffle diggers of Tùng Lộ work its roots.

1248.name: Tùng Lộ Thôn
1248.look: A hill village with truffle pigs in pens.
1248.lore: Its people dig pine truffles with trained pigs. The truffles sell well in Đào Thanh.

1249.name: Thần Mộc Lâm
1249.look: On the hilltop, a grove of colossal old trees whose trunks are wrapped with red cords and hung with small votive boards.
1249.lore: The bowyers of Cung Tiễn hold the trees sacred and never cut them, and they bring each new bow here to be blessed before it is sold. They say an arrow fletched with a feather found in the grove never misses.

1250.name: Cung Tiễn Thôn
1250.look: A hill village of bowyers, bow staves seasoning under every roof.
1250.lore: Its people make bows and arrows for hunters and Tùng Đào's guards. They hunt too.

1251.name: Thanh Ngưu Cốc
1251.look: A high valley of mountain meadow where massive oxen with dark green-tinged coats graze among the boulders.
1251.lore: Spirit oxen live here, gentle unless their calves are threatened; then they charge like a landslide. Herbalists gather the rare grasses they leave ungrazed.

1252.name: Lăng Tiêu Các
1252.look: High on the mountain, the burned shell of a pavilion stands against the sky.
1252.lore: A small sect of alchemists. A fire in its pill hall in 1066 burned the pavilion, and its disciples scattered.

1253.name: Thạch Lâu Thôn
1253.look: A mountain village of goat pens and stone huts gathered under a squat stone watchtower with a fire basket on top.
1253.lore: Its people herd goats and gather herbs on the high slopes. The tower is lit when the green oxen come down the valley, so the herders can drive their flocks clear.

1254.name: Thiết Sam Lâm
1254.look: A dark hemlock forest climbing the mountain, its drooping branches heavy with snow half the year.
1254.lore: Hemlock wood here is hard and does not split, and the weavers of Ma Bố make their loom frames from it. Few go deeper than the woodcutters' paths.

1255.name: Ma Bố Thôn
1255.look: A high village of narrow hemp fields and stone houses where looms clack in every doorway and retting pits steam in the stream.
1255.lore: Its people grow hemp on the slopes and weave a coarse, hard-wearing cloth for sails and sacks. They sell it at Đào Thanh.

1256.name: Kiếm Xỉ Lĩnh
1256.look: A forested ridge whose trunks are scored with deep claw marks, and deer bones lie cracked in its hollows.
1256.lore: Sabre-toothed cats den on the ridge and hunt deer in the valley below. Hunters of Lâm Khẩu go in groups of six, and a fang from here buys a cow.

1257.name: Lâm Khẩu Thôn
1257.look: A village of log houses at the mouth of a forest valley, a tall palisade on the forest side.
1257.lore: Its people hunt and gather in the valley behind. They keep the palisade high because of the sabre-toothed cats on the ridge.

1258.name: Ưng Sào Nhai
1258.look: A grey crag above the village, its ledges crowned with stick nests and whitened by droppings.
1258.lore: Great hawks nest on the crag and take young goats from the slopes. Vân Biên's herders climb up each spring to take chicks for taming, and the hawks remember them.

1259.name: Đoạn Vân Viện
1259.look: On a cliff, the cut halls of an academy lie broken.
1259.lore: A small sect that cut its halls into the cliff. An earthquake in 1134 broke them, and the survivors went to Tùng Đào.

1260.name: Vân Biên Thôn
1260.look: A high village of stone huts on a shelf above the forest, where the clouds often lie below the houses like a white sea.
1260.lore: Its people herd goats and gather herbs on the crags. They guard their kids against the hawks of the crag above.

1261.name: Hổ Văn Khoáng
1261.look: A mine in banded rock like a tiger's stripes, its adit now dark and silent.
1261.lore: The mine dug banded iron ore. The tiger of Hổ Khiếu Cương drove the miners out.

1262.name: Thạch Khẩu Trấn
1262.look: A miners' town in ruins on the mountain, its stone houses roofless.
1262.lore: The miners' town of the tiger-stripe mine. The ore ran thin and the tiger took miners, and it emptied in 1161.

1263.name: Bắc Hoa Lâm
1263.look: A thin birch wood on the tundra's edge, its trees bent low by the north wind and its floor white with lichen.
1263.lore: The birches shelter the ruins of Tuyết Thiền Tự. Reindeer herders camp here in summer and strip bark for their tents.

1264.name: Tuyết Thiền Tự
1264.look: In a gully, the stone halls of a temple stand roofless under snow.
1264.lore: A small sect of monks who meditated in the snow. In the hard winter of 261 most of them starved, and the last walked south to Tùng Đào Cung the next spring.

1265.name: Quải Đài Lâm
1265.look: A high, misty forest of old firs hung so thick with grey-green lichen that the branches look like bearded old men.
1265.lore: The lichen grows only where the air is clean and damp, and alchemists of Thải Chi Cốc buy it for wound salves. The villagers of Tầng Điền gather it in autumn.

1266.name: Cô Hạc Quán
1266.look: A sealed abbey high on the mountain, its main door still closed under a faded seal.
1266.lore: A small sect of hermits. Its abbot died in closed-door cultivation in 1010, and no one could break his seal; the disciples scattered.

1267.name: Tầng Điền Thôn
1267.look: A high village under stair-stepped terraces of barley and buckwheat, held up by dry-stone walls that climb the whole slope.
1267.lore: Its people farm the terraces and rebuild a wall or two each spring after the frost heaves them. They carry earth up in baskets to replace what the rains wash down.

1268.name: Ngân Tuyết Khoáng
1268.look: A timbered adit high on bare rock, its spoil heaps glittering with silver ore under the snow.
1268.lore: The mine digs silver from the high rock in the short summer and closes in winter. Tùng Đào posts a guard on the ore road down to Đào Thanh.

1269.name: Vọng Xuyên Phong
1269.look: The highest peak of the basin, a bare grey summit near two thousand metres, from which the whole river shines in its nine bends.
1269.lore: A peak of Metal qi, cold and sharp. Tùng Đào's disciples climb it to cultivate, and river pilots say a man who has counted all nine bends from its top will never lose his way on the water.

1270.name: Nê Giao Chử
1270.look: Low mud shoals among grey reeds where long, ridged backs lie half sunk like logs, and the mud is scored with drag marks.
1270.lore: Mud dragons (giao) lurk in the shoals and drag deer and stray reindeer down into the mud. No one cuts reeds within sight of them, and the coast fishers row wide of the marsh mouth.

1271.name: Tiễn Trư Lâm
1271.look: A wood of gnawed pines, bark stripped in rings and the ground scattered with long black-and-white quills.
1271.lore: Porcupines as big as dogs live here and kill the young pines by gnawing their bark. Their quills are gathered for arrows and fish lures.

1272.name: Tùng Tâm Thôn
1272.look: A pine forest village where bundles of split, resin-soaked heartwood stand drying against every wall.
1272.lore: Its people split the resinous heartwood of fallen pines into torches that burn for hours. They sell them at Đào Sa for the night washers.

1273.name: Tẩm Thủy Lâm
1273.look: A swamp wood of alder and willow standing knee-deep in still brown water, the trunks stained dark to the flood line.
1273.lore: The villagers of Ô Bồng pole their boats between the trees and set eel traps among the roots. In spring the water rises to the low branches.

1274.name: Ô Bồng Thôn
1274.look: A coastal village of reed houses where narrow boats with arched black-tarred awnings lie in rows at the water's edge.
1274.lore: Its people fish the coast and the marsh channels from the awninged boats and sleep in them in the fishing season. They gather reeds for thatch and mats.

1275.name: Băng Lưu Huyệt
1275.look: A hollow in the tundra where a frozen stream of blue ice pours out of the ground and spreads in a fan that never melts.
1275.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi rises here, so cold it freezes its own water as it flows. Tùng Đào's disciples sit on the ice to temper their bodies in the summer.

1276.name: Thanh Điêu Lâm
1276.look: A coastal pine wood where blue-grey martens flicker through the branches, and stripped pine cones litter the ground.
1276.lore: Blue martens hunt squirrels here, and their pelts are prized in the winter markets. Trappers of Bạch Thạch take them only in deep winter, when the fur is thickest.

1277.name: Bạch Thạch Thôn
1277.look: A coastal village of white stone houses on a pale rocky shore, boats drawn up between the quarry heaps.
1277.lore: Its people fish and quarry the white stone of the shore, which goes by boat to Đào Thanh for steps and quays. The whole village glows at sunset.

1278.name: Thùy Dương Lâm
1278.look: A wood of weeping willows along the river bank, their long branches trailing in the current.
1278.lore: The willows hold the bank against the spring floods. The helmsmen of Đà Công rest in their shade between voyages and cut withies here for baskets.

1279.name: Đà Công Thôn
1279.look: A river village of helmsmen, steering oars racked by every door.
1279.lore: Its people serve as helmsmen for Lãng Đào's ferries. They know every bend of the river.

1280.name: Hồi Thanh Lâm
1280.look: A pine forest in a ring of low hills, where every call comes back twice, a little later each time.
1280.lore: Sounds echo strangely among its trees. The villagers of Ngọa Ngưu come on the night of the dead to call their dead by name and listen for the answer.

1281.name: Phân Thủy Môn
1281.look: In the woods, the fallen gate of a sect.
1281.lore: A small sect of boatmen. Its boats sank in a feud in 788, and the survivors joined Lãng Đào Môn two years later.

1282.name: Ngọa Ngưu Thôn
1282.look: A river village under a low hill shaped exactly like an ox lying down, its fields reaching to the bank.
1282.lore: Its people farm and fish, and they leave a bundle of hay on the hill's head each new year. They say the day the ox rises, the river will flood.

1283.name: Tức Ngưu Sơn
1283.look: A broad round-backed mountain of grey rock above the forest, shaped like an ox lying down to rest.
1283.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, slow and steady, and shepherds say flocks grazed on its flanks never stray. Cultivators of Earth arts sit on its back to settle their foundations.

1284.name: Cao Mục Thôn
1284.look: Stone sheepfolds and low turf-roofed houses on an open steppe shoulder, with flocks spread over the slope below.
1284.lore: Its shepherds drive their sheep to the high grass each summer and down into the woods for winter. Wool and cheese go down to Bích Khê on market days.

1285.name: Sơn Trư Cương
1285.look: A wooded ridge rooted bare in great furrows, with trees scarred waist-high by tusks.
1285.lore: Spirit boars as big as oxen live here and dig up the forest floor for roots. Their bristles make fine brushes, and hunters who take them seldom try twice.

1286.name: Chi Hương Trấn
1286.look: Blackened stone walls and the stumps of a gate tower in a clearing of young pines, with charred beams still lying in the lanes.
1286.lore: A resin town that boiled pitch for the coast from 330. In the dry summer of 712 a fire began in its pitch yards and burned the town and the forest around it; no one rebuilt.

1287.name: Lâm Biên Thôn
1287.look: Log houses where the timber tracks leave the forest, with stacked trunks and sawpits along the lane.
1287.lore: Woodcutters live here and work the edge of the deep forest. They go into the high woods only in groups, with dogs, because of the boars.

1288.name: Cung Sam Lâm
1288.look: Tall dark firs on the high ridge, often wrapped in cloud, their trunks bearded with grey lichen.
1288.lore: The fir here is light and springy, and the Pivot's bowyers and formation masters buy it for bows and frames. Cloud sits in the forest most mornings until noon.

1289.name: Nhân Sâm Thôn
1289.look: A forest village of bark-roofed houses with racks of drying roots under every eave.
1289.lore: Its people dig wild ginseng and sell it to Thiên Xu's alchemists at Khai Dương. A digger's patch passes only from parent to child, shown once, on the parent's last climb.

1290.name: Ẩn Tinh Phong
1290.look: A narrow grey peak above the river forest, whose summit is lost in cloud on most nights.
1290.lore: It is named for the hidden assistant star of the Dipper, which star-readers say can only be seen from here on one night a year. Its qi runs to Metal, sharp and cold.

1291.name: Quần Lang Cương
1291.look: A wooded ridge of broken rock with dens under every boulder and old bones scattered in the leaves.
1291.lore: Grey spirit wolves den here in packs of twenty or more and hunt the horse herds in winter. Phóng Mã's riders burn torches along the pasture edge on the longest nights.

1292.name: Phóng Mã Thôn
1292.look: Timber stables and paddock fences on a steppe glade ringed by forest, with herds grazing loose beyond.
1292.lore: Its people breed sturdy forest horses for Thiên Xu's couriers on the northern road. The herds are turned out loose in summer and rounded up by riders working in pairs.

1293.name: Đại Hùng Lâm
1293.look: Old forest high on the ridge, with trunks clawed bare and beehives torn open in the branches.
1293.lore: Great spirit bears live here, named by the villagers for the stars of the Dipper, which they call the Great Bear. Each autumn the ink-makers leave a cake of honey at the forest edge, and the bears have not come down in living memory.

1294.name: Mặc Yên Thôn
1294.look: Soot-black houses around long brick kilns that smoulder day and night, with ink cakes drying on boards in the sun.
1294.lore: Its people burn pine in closed kilns, gather the soot and press it into ink sticks for Thiên Xu's clerks. The best sticks are scented with musk and stamped with the Dipper.

1295.name: Thiết Mộc Mạch
1295.look: A wooded slope where the trees grow slow and black, their wood so hard that axes ring off it.
1295.lore: A vein whose qi runs to Wood and Metal together. Thiên Xu's ironworkers bring their tools here to be tempered, and the ironwood is cut only for array frames.

1296.name: Lý Ngư Thôn
1296.look: A river village of grey roofs with fish traps of woven willow set in the shallows and log rafts tied along the bank.
1296.lore: Its people trap carp and guide timber rafts down the river. A carp that leaps the weir in spring is let go, for luck.

1297.name: Giả Thiết Khoáng
1297.look: Rust-red pits in the mountainside above the river, with ore heaps and a log slide down to the water.
1297.lore: Crews dig red iron ore here in summer and slide it to the river for rafting to Cự Môn. They leave before the snow and never winter on the ridge.

1298.name: Xích Quan Phong
1298.look: A ridge-top of jagged red-grey rock teeth standing above the forest like a rooster's comb.
1298.lore: Crane riders steer by it on the way to Tinh Tủy Mạch, and rest their mounts on its teeth in bad weather. Its qi runs to Metal, and cultivators who sit among the teeth find their sword intent grows keen and quick to anger.

1299.name: Mật Tùng Lâm
1299.look: A dense forest of black-barked pines, so close-grown that it is dusk under them at noon.
1299.lore: The coast road has never been cut through it, and travellers go round by the shore. Resin tappers work only its edges and say the middle is full of fallen trunks no one has ever cleared.

1300.name: Hải Tùng Thôn
1300.look: A handful of tarred timber houses on the shingle under leaning pines, with resin pots smoking by the boats.
1300.lore: Its families fish the coast and tap the pines for pitch, which they sell to the boatyards. Every boat here is caulked with pitch from the family's own trees.

1301.name: Noãn Thổ Mạch
1301.look: A low swell of steppe where the grass stays green through winter and frost never lies on the ground.
1301.lore: Its qi runs to Earth, warm and deep, like the ground the first shepherds of Dao Quang found. Herders bring their flocks here in the hardest winters, and the Pivot lets them.

1302.name: Chiên Mao Thôn
1302.look: Round felt-roofed houses on the open steppe, with wool spread on mats and women beating it with sticks.
1302.lore: Its herders make felt for tents, boots and saddle cloths and sell it down the northern road. Felt from here is said to keep out rain for ten years.

1303.name: Tàng Kim Mạch
1303.look: A forested hollow among bare hills where thin gold seams glint in a rock face under the roots.
1303.lore: A vein whose qi runs to Metal, found by a prospector who could not dig the gold out. The gold, the Pivot's assayers say, is the qi itself made visible, and will not come away.

1304.name: Xích Sam Phong
1304.look: A forested peak whose red-barked firs grow almost to the summit rock.
1304.lore: Its qi runs to Wood, unusual so high in the ranges. Woodcutters who climb it to cut firs leave the topmost tree standing.

1305.name: Vọng Tinh Bảo
1305.look: A square stone fort on a forested height, its gate burned and its walls still standing to the parapet.
1305.lore: Phá Quân Môn built it in 742 to watch the southern roads. When the rebellion was crushed in 874 its garrison surrendered without a fight, and the fort was burned and left.

1306.name: Duyên Ngân Khoáng
1306.look: Grey spoil heaps below a few adits, with a small smelting hearth and a heap of lead pigs by the path.
1306.lore: Lead and a little silver are dug here and smelted on the spot. The crews are paid in Thiên Xu's silver coin, which they like to say they dug themselves.

1307.name: Khiếu Lang Phong
1307.look: A sharp white-grey fang of rock above the eastern forests, where the wind howls in the cracks.
1307.lore: Its qi runs to Metal, keen and restless. Sword cultivators climb it to sharpen their intent.

1308.name: Vi Thành Trại
1308.look: Earth banks and rotted palisade stakes in a ring on a mountain shoulder, with fire pits still black inside.
1308.lore: Thiên Xu raised this camp in 871 to besiege Phá Quân Môn and abandoned it when the rebel gate fell in 874. Soldiers' names scratched on its stones can still be read.

1309.name: Bạch Tích Khoáng
1309.look: A few small adits on a low mountain slope, with ore washed in a cold stream and spread to dry on flat stones.
1309.lore: Tin from here is carried to Khai Dương and alloyed into bronze for the Pivot's bells and mirrors.

1310.name: Chấp Bút Phong
1310.look: A slender rock summit standing upright above the ridge like a brush held to paper.
1310.lore: Scholars of the Pivot climb it to write poems on the summit. Its qi runs to Metal.

1311.name: Tuyết Ngọc Khoáng
1311.look: A small cut high on a bare slope near the ice, with blocks of pale stone roped on sledges.
1311.lore: White jade is cut here in a short summer season and sledged down over the snow. The Pivot's seal-cutters take the best of it.

1312.name: Thị Tinh Phong
1312.look: A great white glacier peak standing just east of Trích Tinh Phong, a little lower, like an attendant beside a throne.
1312.lore: Pilgrims call it Trích Tinh's servant. Its qi runs to Metal and Water, cold as its ice.

1313.name: Hồng Câu Khoáng
1313.look: Green-stained pits in red rock, with a line of water jars carried up from far below.
1313.lore: Copper is dug here and carried north by mule. Water is so short that the crews bring every drink up the gully.

1314.name: Chu Bình Phong
1314.look: A long flat-faced red cliff peak above the badland gullies, glowing at sunset.
1314.lore: Its qi runs to Earth with a warmth of Fire. Copper crews read the time of day by the colour of its face.

1315.name: Chỉ Nam Khoáng
1315.look: A dark adit under a rock overhang, its mouth bristling with iron nails that have flown to the stone and stuck.
1315.lore: Lodestone from here goes to the Pivot's formation masters and to compass makers. The crews work under the overhang, out of sight of the roc.

1316.name: Thạch Cổ Phong
1316.look: A round, drum-shaped knob of rock on the badland terraces, hollow at its base.
1316.lore: Wind in its hollow booms before storms, and herders drive their flocks to shelter when it sounds. Its qi runs to Earth.

1317.name: Hồ Đào Lâm
1317.look: Broad walnut trees on the drier hills, their ground thick with husks in autumn.
1317.lore: The walnut harvest is Mộc Phiệt's second crop. The trees are counted and owned by families, and some have been owned by the same family since before the Pivot came.

1318.name: Mộc Phiệt Thôn
1318.look: Long timber sheds and log booms on a river bend, with great rafts being lashed together on the bank.
1318.lore: Each spring its people float the winter's timber down to the coast on huge rafts and walk home along the bank. A raftsman who loses his raft walks home without speaking.

1319.name: Mặc Nghiên Khoáng
1319.look: A small quarry of black slate on the mountainside, with split slabs stacked and rough inkstones lined up to dry.
1319.lore: Its slate makes the inkstones Thiên Xu's clerks grind their ink on. A stone from here is said to grind ink without a sound.

1320.name: Huyền Vũ Phong
1320.look: A dark, heavy peak of black slate above the forests, shaped like a tortoise's shell.
1320.lore: It is named for the northern constellation of the Black Warrior. Its qi runs to Water and Metal.

1321.name: Thạch Tích Đài
1321.look: A red badland ledge where lizards the size of dogs lie unmoving in the sun, grey as the rock.
1321.lore: Stone lizards bite and do not let go, and their skin turns arrows. Their shed skins are used to line armour.

1322.name: Hàn Mạch Thôn
1322.look: Stone houses among small walled fields of pink-flowering buckwheat on a high forest edge.
1322.lore: Its people grow buckwheat where wheat will not ripen and keep goats on the badland slopes. Their buckwheat noodles are sold as far as Thanh Bách.

1323.name: Bích Lăng Khoáng
1323.look: Shallow pits in copper-stained mountain rock, with sky-blue turquoise chips glittering in the spoil.
1323.lore: Turquoise from here is carved into beads and inlays at Bích Khê. The crews keep the best chips in their cheeks until they are paid.

1324.name: Hồng Nha Phong
1324.look: A lone red rock tooth standing out of the badland gullies, its base worn hollow by the wind.
1324.lore: Travellers steer by it across the gullies, and the turquoise crews camp in its shade. Its qi runs to Earth, dry and stubborn, and Earth cultivators who sit in its hollow find their foundation settles slowly but does not crack.

1325.name: Hợp Giác Phong
1325.look: Two sharp horns of grey rock rising from one mountain above the split-stone fields.
1325.lore: Herders say the horns lean a little closer each century, and that the world ends when they touch. Its qi runs to Metal, split between the two summits, and a cultivator who sits in the gap between them feels pulled two ways at once, a hard test of a steady mind.

1326.name: Lộc Giác Phong
1326.look: A forested peak with branching rock ribs at its summit, like a stag's antlers.
1326.lore: Hunters will not shoot within sight of it, for the deer of Lộc Uyển are said to climb it to die. Its qi runs to Wood, and herb gatherers find antler moss and deer-horn mushrooms among its rock ribs that alchemists buy for healing pills.

1327.name: Chu Tùng Lâm
1327.look: Tall red-trunked pines on the high ground above the river, their bark peeling in papery strips.
1327.lore: The pine nuts and resin feed Huyền Chi through the winter. Talisman (phù lục) makers buy the resin to fix their ink.

1328.name: Họa Tinh Đường
1328.look: A low hall of dark timber in a forest clearing, its walls hung with long paper strips painted with the Dipper and drying in the wind.
1328.lore: Talisman makers who paint the stars of the Dipper onto paper founded this hall in 910 and swore to Thiên Xu. They grind their ink from Mặc Yên soot and fix it with pine resin, and a talisman from here will not run in the rain.

1329.name: Huyền Chi Thôn
1329.look: Damp bark-roofed houses in the forest with mushroom logs stacked under the trees and drying racks along the lanes.
1329.lore: Its people grow and gather wood-ear and dark lingzhi and sell them dried at Khai Dương. They tap the pines above the village for resin in the dry months.

1330.name: Phục Tùng Lâm
1330.look: Pines bent flat along the ground by the sea wind, their trunks crawling over the dunes.
1330.lore: The wind off the northern sea has laid these trees down. Hải Đê's people gather driftwood and pine cones here and nothing else.

1331.name: Hải Đê Thôn
1331.look: Thatched houses on low ground behind a long grassy earth dike, with fishing boats drawn up on the seaward side.
1331.lore: Its fields lie below the level of the sea, and the whole village mends the dike together each autumn. A child born in a storm is called a dike child and is first to carry earth.

1332.name: Long Cốt Lâm
1332.look: Tall, straight hemlock firs on the flat behind the bay, with skid roads cut down to the water.
1332.lore: Its hard firs make the keels of Tạo Chu, and its name is the shipwrights' word for a keel. A tree is marked for a keel ten years before it is cut.

1333.name: Tạo Chu Trấn
1333.look: A walled town on a sheltered bay with ship hulls on slipways along the shore and fir logs seasoning in great stacks.
1333.lore: Its yards build fishing boats and coasters of fir for the northern coast and for Khai Dương's merchants. Every keel is laid facing the dawn, as in Khai Dương.

1334.name: Thanh Đằng Mạch
1334.look: A hillside wrapped in green vines thick as arms, flowering out of season.
1334.lore: Its qi runs to Wood. The vines grow back overnight when cut, and the Mật Phong beekeepers set their hives at its edge.

1335.name: Mật Phong Thôn
1335.look: A forest village whose walls are lined with hollow-log hives, the air humming all summer.
1335.lore: Its people sell honey and wax as far as Thạch Kiều Thành. Bees that forage on the vein above the village make a darker honey that alchemists buy by weight.

1336.name: Ngân Dương Lâm
1336.look: Pale-barked poplars on the hillsides, their leaves flashing silver in the wind.
1336.lore: Charcoal-burners let this wood grow back between cuttings. Its fast-growing poplar is the cheapest fuel in Dao Quang.

1337.name: Tích Thán Thôn
1337.look: Smoky clay kilns among the trees, with sacks of charcoal piled by the lane and every face streaked black.
1337.lore: Its people burn charcoal for the smiths of Khai Dương and Thanh Bách, cutting the forest in a twenty-year ring.

1338.name: Hắc Thạch Trấn
1338.look: Empty stone houses of dark slate stepped up a bare mountain slope, their doors gone and their hearths cold.
1338.lore: Phá Quân Môn's miners built this town in 760. When the rebel sect was destroyed in 874 the town passed to Cửu Cao Phái with the other holdings, but its people had already fled to Cự Môn, and none came back.

1339.name: Hải Vụ Mạch
1339.look: A forested hollow near the coast where sea fog gathers and lies all day, beading every leaf.
1339.lore: Its qi runs to Water. Fishermen of Cự Môn say the fog here never lifts until the tide turns.

1340.name: Cự Môn Trấn
1340.look: A stone-walled harbour town between the forest and the cliffs, its gate set between two great boulders.
1340.lore: Named for the Dipper's second star-lord, it ships timber and red iron and supplies the patrols bound for the high ranges. Its people took in the miners of Hắc Thạch Trấn after 874.

1341.name: Quan Triều Phong
1341.look: A steep grey peak over the sea cliffs, often capped with a single cloud.
1341.lore: Fishermen of Cự Môn read the weather by its cloud: a white cap means fair seas, a grey one a storm by night. Its qi runs to Water, rising and falling with the tide below, and cultivators of Water arts sit on its sea face to time their breathing to the waves.

1342.name: Thụ Tâm Mạch
1342.look: A vast hollow pine stands in the oldest grove, green light seeping from cracks in its bark.
1342.lore: A Wood vein rises through the heart of the old tree. The resin tappers never cut it, and they say its sap heals burns.

1343.name: Lịch Thanh Thôn
1343.look: Log houses stand in a clearing of scarred pines, the air thick with the smoke of pitch kettles.
1343.lore: The villagers tap pines for resin and boil it into pitch. Every pitch kettle in the village is lit from the same fire, which has not gone out since the village was founded.

1344.name: Mặc Sam Lâm
1344.look: Firs so dark they look black stand close together, and little light reaches the snow below them.
1344.lore: Băng Khổng cuts its boat timber here. Children are told the ruined abbey's ghosts walk under these trees.

1345.name: Tuyết Ẩn Quán
1345.look: Three roofless stone halls stand in a forest clearing, with a meditation platform heaped with snow in the middle.
1345.lore: A small band of ice hermits founded this abbey in 520. In 690 its last master went into seclusion and never came out; his few disciples went down to the coast, and the abbey fell in.

1346.name: Băng Khổng Thôn
1346.look: Wooden houses stand on a cold shore lined with racks of nets, and in winter a row of fishing holes runs out across the sea ice.
1346.lore: Its fishers set nets under the sea ice and haul them through holes. They learned the craft from Hàn Giang's fishers long ago and still say a word for them before each haul.

1347.name: Hoa Bì Lâm
1347.look: White birches stand in frozen bog, their peeling bark bright against the snow.
1347.lore: Hunters cut the bark to roof shelters and make canoes. The wood is the last before the open tundra.

1348.name: Điêu Cừu Trấn
1348.look: A row of collapsed log warehouses lines an iced-in harbour on the tundra shore, a rusted fur press still standing among them.
1348.lore: This fur town grew from 620 on the sable trade of the north coast. By 1065 the sable were trapped out and the harbour iced in each year, and the last families moved south to Hòe Âm.

1349.name: Ngọa Tùng Lâm
1349.look: Pines bent flat by the sea wind crawl over the ground, their crowns all pointing inland.
1349.lore: The sea wind is so steady here that Hải Báo's hunters steer by the pointing pines when fog hides the shore. Seals drag themselves up under the low branches to give birth, and the village does not hunt inside the wood.

1350.name: Hải Báo Thôn
1350.look: Low stone houses roofed with turf crowd a rocky shore, seal hides stretched on frames between them.
1350.lore: The villagers hunt seals for oil, meat and hide. A seal skull is nailed above every door, and the village takes no more seals than it can eat in a winter.

1351.name: Trầm Mộc Lâm
1351.look: Dead grey trunks stand in still black water below sea level, with living firs on the higher ground around them.
1351.lore: The wood floods with snowmelt every spring. Its sunken logs are cut out for timber that never rots.

1352.name: Côn Bố Thôn
1352.look: Long racks of drying kelp line a low shore, and the houses behind them smell of the sea.
1352.lore: The villagers cut kelp from the cold shallows and dry it for food, fodder and medicine. Băng Tâm's alchemists buy the finest blades for cold pills.

1353.name: Trầm Vụ Lâm
1353.look: Firs and swamp pools vanish into a white fog that lies low on the ground and rarely lifts.
1353.lore: People who wander from the path here are found days later, if at all. The fishers of Bộc Ngư go in only roped together.

1354.name: Bộc Ngư Thôn
1354.look: Racks of split cod hang drying along a foggy shore in front of plank houses, and a bell hangs on a post at the village edge.
1354.lore: Its people salt and dry cod for the winter and for the tax. The bell is rung at dusk so no one is lost in the swamp fog.

1355.name: Mi Lộc Lâm
1355.look: A swampy wood with broad trails trampled through it and young trees stripped of bark at head height.
1355.lore: A spirit elk with antlers wide as a cart lives here. Loggers cut around its trails, and when it bellows in autumn they stay out of the wood.

1356.name: Phiệt Mộc Thôn
1356.look: Great rafts of fir logs lie moored along the shore below a village of loggers' huts.
1356.lore: The villagers fell timber and float it down the coast in rafts. A raft master must make the trip to Hòe Âm ten times before he may build his own raft.

1357.name: Hải Thiết Khoáng
1357.look: Adits open in a rust-red cliff just above the surf, beside the rotted stumps of a wooden chute and landing.
1357.lore: Iron ore was once loaded straight onto boats here. The salt wind rusted every tool, and the last miners left saying the iron was rust before it was dug.

1358.name: Kình Bối Phong
1358.look: A long, smooth grey summit humps over the sea like the back of a surfacing whale.
1358.lore: Metal and Water qi meet on its bare rock above the sea. Sailors on the eastern coast steer by it.

1359.name: Vọng Triều Bảo
1359.look: A broken tower of grey stone stands on a cliff edge above the sea, its seaward wall gone.
1359.lore: Băng Tâm built this watch fort around 650 against the pirates of Thôn Hải Môn. After the Pirate Purge of 781 it was not needed, and the garrison was withdrawn in 790; storms have broken it since.

1360.name: Khô Tùng Nhai
1360.look: A sheer cliff of pale rock with a single dead pine hanging upside down from a crack near the top.
1360.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the bare rock. Hunters of Hòe Âm say the pine was already dead when Băng Tâm came.

1361.name: Nguyệt Thạch Khoáng
1361.look: A small mine on a mountainside above the sea, its spoil heap glittering faintly blue at night.
1361.lore: Băng Tâm digs moonstone here, a cold milky stone that holds the qi of Băng Phách Mạch nearby. Miners work in pairs because of the beasts that roam toward the vein.

1362.name: Băng Trụ Phong
1362.look: A lone pillar of blue ice stands above the flat glacier, streaked white by the wind.
1362.lore: Its Water qi is cold and clean, and novices sent to the plain sit at its foot. Those who last the night carve a mark in its base.

1363.name: Hàn Thiết Khoáng
1363.look: A single shaft opens in a snowfield under a timber shed, with frost thick on the ore carts.
1363.lore: The iron here takes and keeps cold, and Băng Tâm's smiths use it for sword cores. The miners leave before the first snow.

1364.name: Hàn Ưng Phong
