1364.look: A hooked summit of dark rock juts out over the valley like an eagle's beak.
1364.lore: Metal qi gathers in its hard rock. Eagles nest under the hook and attack anyone who climbs near.

1365.name: Bão Tuyết Phong
1365.look: A high peak whose two arms of rock curve around a deep bowl of snow.
1365.lore: Water qi gathers in the snow bowl. Băng Tâm disciples train their sword forms in the wind on its rim.

1366.name: Lũng Đầu Trại
1366.look: A ring of fallen stone walls stands at the head of a pass, with the burned stumps of timber gates.
1366.lore: Hồ Thiên Phái built this stockade around 260 to guard the pass to its coast. After the eruption of 425 buried the school, the garrison went home and never came back.

1367.name: Phong Diệp Lâm
1367.look: A wood of maples climbs the valley side and turns blood red for a few weeks each autumn.
1367.lore: Hàn Khê's charcoal burners work here. The red leaves are said to mark the last warm ground before the ice.

1368.name: Hàn Khê Thôn
1368.look: Stone houses and barley strips line a fast clear river, with charcoal mounds smoking on the slopes above.
1368.lore: Its people fish trout, burn charcoal and grow barley. They send their charcoal down to Hòe Âm and their sons up to the mines.

1369.name: Ngân Lũ Khoáng
1369.look: A small mine at the forest edge, where thin silver veins show like threads in the quarried rock.
1369.lore: Miners from Hàn Khê work the silver in summer. The threads are thin, and the mine has never made anyone rich.

1370.name: Kiếm Tích Phong
1370.look: A thin, sharp ridge of grey rock runs up to a narrow summit like the spine of a blade.
1370.lore: Its Metal qi draws Băng Tâm's sword cultivators, who walk the edge as a test of balance.

1371.name: Bích Trâm Phong
1371.look: A slender spire of green-grey rock rises above a glacier like a hairpin.
1371.lore: Metal qi gathers in the spire. Lê Hoa Am's nuns say the first abbess dropped her hairpin from here.

1372.name: Thủ Tuyết Bảo
1372.look: A square stone fort in a high pass, its gate torn off and long claw marks scored down its walls.
1372.lore: Băng Tâm built this fort in 760 to guard the road to Băng Phách Mạch. In 1102 ice beasts drawn by the vein's cold overran it, and the Pavilion did not rebuild.

1373.name: Băng Tinh Quật
1373.look: A cave mouth in grey rock opens onto a hall lined with clear rock crystal.
1373.lore: Clear crystal is cut here for formation plates. The miners say the crystal is ice that froze so long ago it forgot how to melt.

1374.name: Băng Kỳ Phong
1374.look: A high peak that trails a long plume of blown snow from its top like a banner.
1374.lore: Water qi streams off its summit with the snow. Climbers read the weather from the banner's direction.

1375.name: Tích Thạch Khoáng
1375.look: Small pits and a stream sluice dot a valley floor below the great peak, the gravel black with tinstone.
1375.lore: Tin is washed from the stream gravel here. Băng Tâm's smiths mix it into bronze for bells and mirrors.

1376.name: Thùy Thiên Phong
1376.look: An immense white peak rises nearly four thousand metres from the sea, its top usually lost in cloud.
1376.lore: Its Metal and Water qi are strong and cold. Few have climbed it, and none have come down with the same face.

1377.name: Hàn Ngân Khoáng
1377.look: A cluster of stone huts and an adit sit at the foot of a glacier.
1377.lore: Silver is mined here at the edge of the ice. Miners say the ore is coldest in summer, when the glacier sweats.

1378.name: Kim Quan Phong
1378.look: A high peak with a ring of rock towers at its top, which catches the first sun and glows gold.
1378.lore: Its Metal qi is strongest at dawn. Băng Tâm's sword cultivators climb to greet the first light on it.

1379.name: Từ Thạch Khoáng
1379.look: A mine on a bare slope where tools left on the rock creep slowly toward the adit mouth.
1379.lore: Lodestone is mined here for compass needles and formation plates. Miners carry no iron underground.

1380.name: Huyền Băng Phong
1380.look: A high peak sheathed in old dark ice, so dense it looks black.
1380.lore: Its Water qi is heavy and old. Ice cultivators cut cores from the black ice for their meditation.

1381.name: Bạch Thủ Phong
1381.look: A round white hill of ice rises at the tip of the cape like an old man's head.
1381.lore: Seal hunters steer by it and call it the old man. Its weak Water qi draws nothing but seabirds.

1382.name: Hàn Kim Quật
1382.look: A cave high on a cliff face, reached by a ladder of iron spikes, with gold showing in the quartz of its walls.
1382.lore: Băng Tâm works the gold vein only in high summer. Two miners fell from the ladder in its first year, and their names are cut at its foot.

1383.name: Vô Điểu Phong
1383.look: A sheer high peak of pale rock where no bird flies and no wind sound carries.
1383.lore: Its Metal qi is so strong that birds turn away from it. Sword cultivators come here to sit in its silence.

1384.name: Đoạn Tuyết Quan
1384.look: Only the top of a gatehouse roof and one watch tower show above a slope of old avalanche snow.
1384.lore: Băng Tâm built this fort in 530 to hold the high pass from the desert into the ice mountains. An avalanche buried it with its garrison in the winter of 1012, and it was never dug out.

1385.name: Mã Não Quật
1385.look: A cave mouth in a cliff of banded rock, its floor scattered with chips of red and white agate.
1385.lore: Agate is cut here for seals and ornaments. Miners come from Băng Tâm's side only and never cross the ridge.

1386.name: Hàn Tinh Phong
1386.look: A high peak whose ice glitters like stars on clear nights.
1386.lore: Its Metal qi runs toward the vein in the valley below. From the top one can see Tinh Tủy Mạch and the cranes that circle it.

1387.name: Khuy Tinh Bảo
1387.look: A small stone watch fort on the ridge, its doors sealed with plain wooden bars.
1387.lore: Băng Tâm built this watch fort around 1100 to look down on Tinh Tủy Mạch. After its claim to the vein was rejected and Thiên Xu doubled its guard in 1189, the Pavilion withdrew the watchers and barred the doors so as not to look like it was preparing a war.

1388.name: Đồng Lục Quật
1388.look: Red and green stained adits open in the gully wall above the icy brook.
1388.lore: Copper is mined here where the mountain meets the desert. The ore goes down to the desert towns by camel.

1389.name: Túc Nhạn Phong
1389.look: A high peak above a southern gully, where migrating geese rest on its snowfields in spring.
1389.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the bare upper rock. Hunters say geese that land here in autumn never fly on.

1390.name: Lang Yên Bảo
1390.look: A beacon fort on a spur above the gully, its walls glazed black by fire and its beacon tower split.
1390.lore: Băng Tâm built this beacon fort in 520 to pass warnings along the caravan road. Phượng Minh's fire broke it in 726, the same year Cô Thành fell.

1391.name: Ngân Bình Phong
1391.look: A long wall of snow-covered summit stands like a silver screen above the southern sea.
1391.lore: Its Metal and Water qi meet over the sea cliffs. Seabirds nest on its walls in their thousands.

1392.name: Phong Tuyết Đỉnh
1392.look: A broad ice summit always wrapped in blowing snow, its top seen only on a few still days a year.
1392.lore: Băng Tâm's ice cultivators sit here for the pure Water qi of the endless freeze. The wind has taken more than one careless disciple off the top.

1393.name: Băng Bích Nhai
1393.look: A cliff of grey rock sheathed in a curtain of ice faces the sea.
1393.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the ice curtain. Hunters shelter at its foot in summer storms.

1394.name: Bắc Đình Thành
1394.look: Low stone walls trace a square on the tundra shore, half buried in moss, with the stump of a gate tower facing the sea.
1394.lore: Hồ Thiên Phái built this fur and ivory city on the northern shore around 260. After the eruption of 425 buried the school, the trade died and the last families left within a few years.

1395.name: Đống Thủy Nhãn
1395.look: A perfectly round pool in the moss tundra that never fully freezes, its black water steaming faintly in the cold.
1395.lore: A Water vein rises here through the frozen ground. Băng Tâm has never built over it, and hunters drink from it only after making an offering.

1396.name: Tuyết Hiêu Nguyên
1396.look: Open tundra dotted with boulders, each one crowned with white droppings and small bones.
1396.lore: Snow owls as big as eagles hunt here, led by a spirit owl that flies by day. Trappers never cross the plain in the open.

1397.name: Hoàng Tùng Lâm
1397.look: A thin wood of larches on wet ground that turns bright gold every autumn and stands bare all winter.
1397.lore: Hàn Trạch's trappers set their lines here. Larch wood does not rot, and the village's bog paths are laid with it.

1398.name: Hàn Trạch Thôn
1398.look: Turf-roofed houses on a dry rise above the bog, with stacks of black peat drying beside every door.
1398.lore: The villagers cut peat, pick cranberries and trap fur. They say the bog keeps everything, and now and then they cut out a perfectly kept bone or blade.

1399.name: Tùng Tuyết Mạch
1399.look: A ring of tall pines stands green in a land of stunted trees, and snow melts in a circle around them.
1399.lore: A Wood vein feeds the ring of pines. Băng Tâm's herb gatherers pick the cold-root that grows only here.

1400.name: Kim Hạt Cương
1400.look: A ridge of yellow dunes pocked with holes, and golden shells glinting in the sand at noon.
1400.lore: Spirit scorpions with golden shells hunt here at night. Their poison is sold to alchemists, and the men who catch them rarely live to old age.

1401.name: Phí Sa Thang
1401.look: Hot water bubbles up through the sand into a shallow pool ringed with white crust.
1401.lore: Fire qi rises with the water. Caravans water their camels here after it cools, and Băng Tâm keeps a cairn of water jars beside it.

1402.name: Dã Đà Nguyên
1402.look: Flat sand along the river, tracked by broad two-toed hoofprints and dotted with dung.
1402.lore: Wild spirit camels graze the river edge, led by a white bull. Caravan breeders try to catch its calves.

1403.name: Liệt Dương Huyệt
1403.look: A bowl of red rock in the desert where the air shimmers even in winter.
1403.lore: A Fire vein rises here. Băng Tâm's disciples come to train the ice heart against heat.

1404.name: Chiên Trướng Thôn
1404.look: A ring of round felt tents on the steppe, with felt drying on frames and flocks grazing all around.
1404.lore: The herders move the village twice a year. They make felt for the seat's winter halls and the caravans.

1405.name: Khổ Thủy Trì
1405.look: A warm pool in the steppe, its water cloudy and its edges stained white and yellow.
1405.lore: Its water is too bitter to drink, but salt-boilers soak their cracked hands in it. Its Fire qi is weak and its Water qi bitter.

1406.name: Chử Diêm Thôn
1406.look: Low mud houses on a salt shore, with iron pans steaming over dung fires along the waterline.
1406.lore: The villagers boil sea water into salt and sell it to caravans and to Hồi Lan. Every child learns to tend a pan before they can read.

1407.name: Tùng Thạch Khoáng
1407.look: Small pits dot a red hillside, with chips of blue-green stone in the spoil.
1407.lore: Turquoise is dug here for ornaments and caravan trade. Desert people say it guards a rider from falling.

1408.name: Thạch Kiếm Phong
1408.look: A tall blade of red rock stands upright on the ridge.
1408.lore: Its Metal qi draws Băng Tâm's sword cultivators. The raiders of Dạ Quang used it as a lookout.

1409.name: Huyết Đao Trại
1409.look: A burned stockade of red stone and timber in a side valley, its walls blackened and its gate burned out.
1409.lore: Dạ Quang's raiders hid their loot here from 975. Băng Tâm burned it in 1121, at the end of the campaign, and Hạng Dạ Bôi knelt soon after.

1410.name: Hắc Môi Khoáng
1410.look: Black spoil heaps and a timber headframe stand among pines at the foot of the mountain.
1410.lore: Coal is dug here for the forges of the seat. The miners' faces are always black, and they are called the crows.

1411.name: Hạc Lập Phong
1411.look: A slim grey peak rises alone above the pines like a crane standing on one leg.
1411.lore: Its Metal qi is mild and steady. The ruined sect below once held its morning practice here.

1412.name: Lãnh Hương Các
1412.look: A small ruined pavilion among pines, its roof fallen and a grove of wild plum gone feral around it.
1412.lore: A small sect of plum-blossom sword cultivators founded this pavilion in 600. In 724 all its disciples rode to break the siege of Cô Thành and none came back.

1413.name: Ngân Hồ Lâm
1413.look: A forested slope with fox earths between the roots and silver hairs caught on the bark.
1413.lore: Silver spirit foxes live here and steal from the village. Mộc Kiều's people leave them a share of grain to keep them from the houses.

1414.name: Mộc Kiều Thôn
1414.look: Log houses on both banks of a river, joined by a long timber bridge on stone piers.
1414.lore: The village keeps the bridge on the road from the seat to the coast, and Băng Tâm pays it in grain. Its loggers fell timber in the hills above.

1415.name: Dương Chi Khoáng
1415.look: A mine in a dry stream bed where white stones like congealed fat lie in the gravel.
1415.lore: White jade is dug from the stream bed and the cliffs above. Băng Tâm carves its seals from it.

1416.name: Tuyết Tôn Phong
1416.look: A massive white summit over four and a half thousand metres high, towering above the western desert.
1416.lore: Its Metal and Water qi are fierce. Few have reached the top, and Băng Tâm's elders climb it before a breakthrough.

1417.name: Phong Sa Nhãn
1417.look: A ring of standing stones in the desert, where small whirlwinds of sand rise even on still days.
1417.lore: An Earth vein lies under the ring. The caravan drivers of Đà Linh say storms are born here.

1418.name: Đà Linh Trấn
1418.look: A river town of mud-brick inns and camel yards, ringing with camel bells.
1418.lore: Caravans gather here before the long crossing. The town makes the bronze bells every caravan camel wears.

1419.name: Viên Nhật Huyệt
1419.look: A round hollow on the steppe by the river, its red earth glowing as if the setting sun lay in it.
1419.lore: A Fire vein rises here. The old caravan song says the long river and the round setting sun meet in this hollow.

1420.name: Thạch Tháp Mạch
1420.look: A flat slab of yellow rock as big as a courtyard lies on a steppe rise, bare of snow and warm to the touch even on frost nights.
1420.lore: An Earth vein rises under the slab and keeps it warm. The shepherds of Dương Bằng bed their ewes on it in the lambing frosts, and Băng Tâm's earth cultivators come to sit on it in summer when the flocks are away.

1421.name: Dương Bằng Thôn
1421.look: Stone pens and low houses on the steppe, ringed by grazing sheep.
1421.lore: The shepherds sell wool to the seat and to Hồi Lan. They count sheep at dusk with a song that no outsider understands.

1422.name: Băng Quan Phong
1422.look: A huge peak capped with a crown of ice above the desert.
1422.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the ice. Băng Tâm's ice cultivators come to sit in its cold.

1423.name: Ngưng Băng Bảo
1423.look: Low mounds of slumped ice and stone stand in a high pass, the shape of walls still visible.
1423.lore: Tần Ngưng Sương's first disciples built this fort of ice blocks in 450 to guard the pass, keeping it frozen with their arts. When she died in 1010 no one renewed the ice, and the walls slumped.

1424.name: Hồng Thạch Phong
1424.look: A cracked red peak rises over the badlands, split into great blocks by summer heat and winter frost, with fallen slabs heaped at its foot.
1424.lore: Its Earth qi is heavy and dry and gathers in the split rock. Sand vipers shelter in its cracks, and caravan drivers who climb it for a lookout tap every handhold with a stick first.

1425.name: Mai Sa Bảo
1425.look: Only the top of a watch tower shows above a dune in a mountain pass.
1425.lore: Băng Tâm built this caravan fort in 600. The sandstorm of 1050 that buried Mã Minh's wells buried it too, and it was not dug out.

1426.name: Noãn Thạch Khoáng
1426.look: A quarry of jade-green stone on a snowy slope, where snow melts as it touches the cut faces.
1426.lore: Băng Tâm quarries warm stone here to floor its cave abodes. The stone is the same as at Noãn Ngọc Tuyền nearby.

1427.name: Đoạn Băng Nhai
1427.look: A cliff of grey rock capped with old ice rises over the tundra, split by cracks wide enough to walk into.
1427.lore: Its Water qi gathers in the cracks of the old ice. Every thaw great blocks break off and roll onto the plain, and hunters camp well away from its foot.

1428.name: Lẫm Đông Thành
1428.look: Empty stone streets on a tundra shore, with the ribs of crushed ships frozen in the harbour.
1428.lore: This port city was founded around 420. In the winter of 655 the sea froze to the horizon and crushed its ships in the harbour, and its people moved to Mộc Lan.

1429.name: Thùy Băng Lâm
1429.look: Firs hung with icicles from every branch, tinkling in the wind.
1429.lore: The icicles stay until late spring. Ngân Ngư's children are told not to shout here.

1430.name: Băng Hỏa Môn
1430.look: A ruined sect in the forest, half its halls burned and half split by frost.
1430.lore: A small sect founded in 710 to cultivate both the fire and frost of Sương Diễm Sơn. Its fire and water disciples quarrelled until the sect split and burned itself out in 980.

1431.name: Ngân Ngư Thôn
1431.look: Plank houses on the shore, with silver ice-fish drying on racks.
1431.lore: The villagers net ice-fish under the winter ice and sell them in Mộc Lan. They learned the craft from Hàn Giang's fishers.

1432.name: Quả Tùng Lâm
1432.look: Tall red-barked pines stand in deep snow, pine cones as big as fists on the ground.
1432.lore: The charcoal burners do not cut these pines. Squirrels and bears feed on their nuts.

1433.name: Mộc Thán Thôn
1433.look: Log houses in a forest clearing, surrounded by smoking charcoal kilns.
1433.lore: The villagers burn charcoal for the coast cities and the forges. Their faces and houses are black with soot.

1434.name: Mê Tung Trấn
1434.look: Collapsed log houses in the forest, young firs growing through their roofs.
1434.lore: Loggers built this town in 560 at the edge of Vô Tung Lâm. Too many of its people were lost in the forest, and by 1012 the last families had moved to Tiều Lộ.

1435.name: Bì Thuyền Thôn
1435.look: Hide boats lie upturned on the shore in front of log houses.
1435.lore: The villagers build hide boats and hunt seals along the coast. Trạc Anh's sea hunters buy their boats.

1436.name: Tuyết Báo Nhai
1436.look: A cliff of grey rock above the fir forest, with paw prints in the snow on its ledges.
1436.lore: Snow leopards den on the ledges and hunt deer in the forest below. Their pelts fetch a high price in Mộc Lan.

1437.name: Hải Vụ Lâm
1437.look: Firs hung with grey moss stand in a sea fog that rarely lifts.
1437.lore: The moss is gathered for bedding and wound dressing. The fog makes the wood easy to get lost in.

1438.name: Lãnh Ngạn Thôn
1438.look: Stone houses on a foggy shore under cliffs white with seabirds.
1438.lore: The villagers gather mussels from the shore and seabird eggs from the cliffs. They climb on ropes of twisted hide.

1439.name: Lạp Mai Lâm
1439.look: Wild plums bloom white among the firs in late winter.
1439.lore: Tuyết Đăng's people come to see the plums when the snow is still deep. The fruit is made into sour wine.

1440.name: Tuyết Đăng Trấn
1440.look: A timber town on the north-east coast, with snow lanterns lit along its quay on winter nights.
1440.lore: The town ships logs and furs down the coast. Each winter its people carve lanterns from snow to guide boats home.

1441.name: Tuyết Điêu Lĩnh
1441.look: A ridge above the forest with huge nests on its crags.
1441.lore: Snow eagles nest here and take lambs and seals. Vọng Phàm's people keep their children indoors when the eagles fly low.

1442.name: Hắc Ngạn Trấn
1442.look: Empty stone houses on a shore of black ash, their wells filled with grey silt.
1442.lore: This fishing town was founded in 505. When Sương Diễm Sơn breathed fire for a week in 700, ash fell on it and its wells went bitter, and its people left.

1443.name: Vọng Phàm Thôn
1443.look: Stone houses on the west coast, with a lookout platform on the cliff above.
1443.lore: The villagers fish and watch for sails from the cliff. They light a fire on the platform to guide boats home.

1444.name: Cực Quang Phong
1444.look: A glacier peak at the top of the frost coast, under green curtains of light on winter nights.
1444.lore: Its Water qi is strongest under the aurora. Ice cultivators come here on the longest nights.

1445.name: Sóc Phương Thành
1445.look: Stone walls and empty houses stand in a rocky bay, with seal-oil vats rusting on the quay.
1445.lore: Hàn Giang Môn built this seal-oil city around 340. After the War of the Frost Coast, Băng Tâm moved its people south to Liên Giang in 498 and it was left empty.

1446.name: Xuân Manh Huyệt
1446.look: A hollow in the forest where green shoots push up through the snow even in midwinter.
1446.lore: A Wood vein rises under the hollow and keeps the ground soft through the winter. The mushroom pickers of Thái Cô cut its shoots for medicine and sell them to Băng Tâm's alchemists in spring.

1447.name: Thái Cô Thôn
1447.look: Log houses in the forest, with strings of dried fungus hanging from the eaves.
1447.lore: The villagers gather wood-ear fungus and mushrooms and sell them dried. They know every rotting log in the forest.

1448.name: Chiết Liễu Phố
1448.look: Rotting piers in a silted bay, with empty warehouses behind them.
1448.lore: This harbour town was founded in 650, and travellers broke willow twigs here in farewell. Its harbour silted up and the ships went to Liên Giang, and by 1140 it was empty.

1449.name: Sam Âm Mạch
1449.look: A stand of tall firs behind the shore where the ground under the trees stays green with moss while snow lies all around.
1449.lore: A Wood vein lies under the firs. Băng Tâm's herb gatherers pick a cold green moss here that stops bleeding, and Triều Bình's people will not cut a single tree in the stand.

1450.name: Triều Bình Thôn
1450.look: Wooden houses on a sheltered shore, with barley strips behind them.
1450.lore: The villagers fish and farm a little barley. The gentle tide here lets them fish all year.

1451.name: Hàn Lục Lâm
1451.look: A dense fir forest on the slopes above the coast that stays dark green under the snow.
1451.lore: Lư Ngư's people cut straight firs here for boat keels and masts. Red deer winter in its shelter, and the village takes only what it needs for the year's boats.

1452.name: Lư Ngư Thôn
1452.look: Plank houses on the east coast, with perch drying on racks.
1452.lore: The villagers fish for perch in the river mouths and sell them in Liên Giang. Perch soup is their pride.

1453.name: Cổ Căn Huyệt
1453.look: A hollow under a fallen giant tree, its roots arching overhead.
1453.lore: A Wood vein rises among the roots of the fallen tree. The best wild ginseng of the frost coast grows around it, and Tàng Sâm's diggers say a root from here is worth a year of ordinary digging.

1454.name: Tàng Sâm Thôn
1454.look: Log houses deep in the forest, with ginseng roots drying on trays.
1454.lore: The villagers dig wild ginseng and sell it to Băng Tâm's alchemists. They never tell outsiders where it grows.

1455.name: Thùy Lăng Phong
1455.look: A peak above the village, its cliffs hung with long icicles.
1455.lore: Its Water and Metal qi feed the cold of Băng Lăng Khoáng below. The icicles never fall, even in summer, and the miners of Thiết Chùy touch the nearest one for luck before going underground.

1456.name: Thiết Chùy Thôn
1456.look: Stone houses on the coast, ringing with the sound of hammers.
1456.lore: The villagers mine and work the cold metal of Băng Lăng Khoáng. They wrap their boots in felt underground.

1457.name: Không Thanh Khoáng
1457.look: A small mine in a fold of the forested mountain, its spoil heaps streaked bright blue against the snow.
1457.lore: Azurite is dug here in summer and ground into the blue pigment called stone blue. Băng Tâm paints the ceilings of its ice halls with it, and the miners' hands stay blue until midwinter.

1458.name: Hàn Nha Phong
1458.look: A bare grey peak stands above the forest, its ledges black with roosting crows at dusk.
1458.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the bare rock. Crows roost on it in their thousands through the winter, and the azurite miners below read the weather from when the flocks leave.

1459.name: Chiến Diệp Lâm
1459.look: White-barked aspens cover the low hills, their leaves shivering in the faintest wind and turning gold in autumn.
1459.lore: Xích Quả's people cut aspen for firewood and for the light boxes they pack their berry sweets in. Hawthorn grows thick along its edges, and the village's pickers work the wood from first frost until the berries fall.

1460.name: Xích Quả Thôn
1460.look: Log houses on a hillside among hawthorn bushes red with berries.
1460.lore: The villagers make hawthorn sweets and wine and sell them at Tống Khách market. Travellers carry them for the road.

1461.name: Nham Bách Lâm
1461.look: Twisted junipers cling to the rocky slopes of the mountain.
1461.lore: The juniper is burned as incense in Băng Tâm's halls. Its smoke is said to calm the mind.

1462.name: Ôn Khê Thôn
1462.look: Stone houses along a steaming brook, with green vegetable beds in the snow.
1462.lore: The brook is warmed by the fire below the mountain. The villagers grow early vegetables and sell them in Liên Giang.

1463.name: Hồng Nê Mạch
1463.look: A patch of red clay on the steppe, warm and soft underfoot.
1463.lore: An Earth vein lies under the clay and keeps it from freezing hard. Hoàng Dương's people dig it for pots and for the red wash on their houses, and herders let their sheep lick it for salt.

1464.name: Hoàng Dương Thôn
1464.look: Felt tents and mud houses on a river bank in the steppe.
1464.lore: The villagers herd sheep and hunt gazelle. They sell hides and meat to the frost coast.

1465.name: Bắc Minh Nhãn
1465.look: A deep round pool in the tundra, its black water never freezing.
1465.lore: A Water vein rises from the deep. Reindeer herders avoid it, saying it has no bottom.

1466.name: Sương Hoa Tuyền
1466.look: A spring in the tundra ringed with frost flowers that grow on the ice.
1466.lore: A Water vein rises with the spring, and its cold grows feathery frost flowers on the ice each night. Băng Tâm's ice cultivators sit beside it, and a disciple who melts a flower with a careless breath must start the night again.

1467.name: Huyền Ngọc Khoáng
1467.look: A small adit in the bare wind-cut hills, its spoil heaps glossy black and its hut roofs weighted with stones against the gale.
1467.lore: Raven-black jade is cut here in the short summer and carried south on sledges before the snow. Băng Tâm's elders wear it as plain belt plaques, and the miners say the stone drinks the wind's cold.

1468.name: Lang Nha Phong
1468.look: A sharp peak of grey rock rising above the tundra like a fang.
1468.lore: Its Metal qi gathers in the sharp rock. Snow wolves from Tuyết Lang Nguyên howl from its foot on winter nights, and the black jade miners leave the hills before the packs come down.

1469.name: Mao Ngưu Nguyên
1469.look: Flat tundra trampled by herds of shaggy yaks.
1469.lore: Wild spirit yaks graze here in summer, led by a huge black bull. Trappers keep their distance.

1470.name: Cố Ngạn Bảo
1470.look: A broken stone fort on the coast, its walls split and its gate fallen.
1470.lore: Hàn Giang Môn built this fort around 400 to guard its coast. Băng Tâm stormed it in 497, the year before the Frost Coast fell.

1471.name: Kính Băng Nhãn
1471.look: A small round pool frozen as clear as a mirror in the tundra.
1471.lore: A Water vein rises under the pool and keeps its ice as clear as glass. Băng Tâm disciples sit on it to meditate, as their elders did on Phiến Băng Hồ, and say they see their own faces looking back.

1472.name: Điêu Thử Lâm
1472.look: A dense fir and swamp forest where the snow is stitched with the small paired tracks of sable.
1472.lore: Bộ Điêu's trappers set their lines here, each family on its own marked trees. Sable are still plentiful, and the village keeps a rule to take none in spring so the wood is never trapped out.

1473.name: Vụ Trạch Phái
1473.look: Ruined stilt halls in a misty marsh on the coast.
1473.lore: A small school founded in 560 to cultivate the marsh's Water qi. In 870 a cold fever came off the marsh and none of its forty disciples saw the spring.

1474.name: Bộ Điêu Thôn
1474.look: Log houses in the forest, with furs stretched on frames.
1474.lore: The villagers trap sable and fox and sell the fur in Mộc Lan. Every trapper has his own line.

1475.name: Đông Thanh Lâm
1475.look: A forest of holly and fir, green and red in winter.
1475.lore: Kình Cốt's people cut holly for the feast that ends the whaling season and hang it over the whalebone doorways. Thrushes and waxwings winter in the wood on its red berries.

1476.name: Tê Nhạn Quán
1476.look: An empty abbey on the marsh shore, geese roosting in its halls.
1476.lore: A small abbey founded in 880. In 1095 its last abbot joined Trạc Anh Đài with his disciples, and the halls were left to the marsh.

1477.name: Kình Cốt Thôn
1477.look: Houses framed with whale ribs on the coast.
1477.lore: The villagers hunt whales in summer with Trạc Anh's sea hunters. They build with the bones.

1478.name: Độc Điệt Trạch
1478.look: A cold marsh of black water and grey reeds where leeches as long as a hand ripple through the shallows toward any footstep.
1478.lore: Poison leeches infest the marsh, and their bite leaves a numb welt for days. Thải Chi's herb gatherers wrap their legs in oiled cloth, and the valley's alchemists collect the leeches for a blood-thinning draught.

1479.name: Long Quang Mạch
1479.look: A high badland ridge where at night a pale light rises from cracks in the red rock, like the glow of buried swords.
1479.lore: A Metal vein runs under the ridge, named for the old line in which the dragon light of buried swords shoots up at the stars. Thiên Bảo Trai holds it and lets its refiners cultivate here before great workings.

1480.name: Trận Thạch Khoáng
1480.look: A neat old quarry below the lowest hall, its walls cut in square steps, with a few round stone blanks still stacked and never carved.
1480.lore: The Pivot's array discs were once cut from this stone, close-grained and heavy with the blessed land's qi. The good seam is spent; the last blanks were weighed at Thiên Quyền Thị and never sent for carving.

1481.name: Xu Trụ Phong
1481.look: A sheer pillar of grey rock above the seat's terraces, green with moss to a height no moss should reach.
1481.lore: It stands over Tử Vi Mạch inside the blessed land, and its qi runs to Metal and Earth. Only the Pivot's elders may meditate on its summit.

1482.name: Lâm Linh Đỉnh
1482.look: A bare dark summit just north of the Tower's cone, crowned by a single bronze bell hung from a stone frame, its rim worn bright by the rain.
1482.lore: Metal (Kim) qi gathers on this crag, and Thính Vũ's sword disciples come here in long rains to listen to the bell ring under the drops until they strike in time with it. The bell was cast for Phó Tiêu Tương and is never struck by hand.

1483.name: Thạch Thán Khoáng
1483.look: A black adit below the forges, with coal baskets carried up a stair cut in the slope.
1483.lore: Its hard black coal feeds Thối Tinh Môn's forges. The porters climb the stair a hundred times a day and are paid by the basket.

1484.name: Thiết Châm Phong
1484.look: A flat-topped peak of dark rock above the forges, shaped like an anvil and often ringed with forge smoke.
1484.lore: Thối Tinh Môn's smiths say the sky hammers stars on it. Its qi runs to Metal, hard and ringing, and smiths sit on its flat top to temper their own bodies before forging a great blade.

1485.name: Kiếp Trúc Lâm
1485.look: Among the grave mounds a grove of grey-green bamboo grows in twisted stems, each joint marked with a black scorch ring.
1485.lore: The grove sprang from roots scorched by the lightning of Hầu Xuân Lôi's tribulation, and its bamboo still holds a trace of that thunder. Thu Phần Các cuts the slips for its poems from it, and no one else may.

1486.name: Quy Tịch Phong
1486.look: A bare rock peak rises south of the twin summits, standing clear above the haze on most days.
1486.lore: Earth qi gathers in its rock, and Thúy Vi's elders go up it for closed-door cultivation. From its top the whole spiral of the Haze Walk can be seen.

1487.name: Thương Lãng Lâm
1487.look: Birch and fir along a clear stream, with stumps where drying poles have been cut.
1487.lore: Trạc Anh Đài cuts its drying poles here. The wood is named from the song: when the water is clear, wash your hat strings in it.

1488.name: Trúc Thử Nguyên
1488.look: A stretch of grassland pocked with burrow mounds, the bamboo around it gnawed to stumps.
1488.lore: Spirit bamboo rats the size of dogs breed here and raid Trúc Thực Viên's beds whenever the seed is heavy. The garden's disciples hunt them each seeding year, and the rats come back each year.

1489.name: Thính Đào Nhãn
1489.look: Just below the long gallery, a round hollow among the pines holds a still pool, and the sound of the pines falls into it like surf.
1489.lore: A spirit vein of Wood and Water qi rises in the pool. New disciples of Tùng Đào sit by it to learn to hear the pine waves before they are taught a single art.

1490.name: Bích Hác Sâm
1490.look: High on the ravine rims, a dark forest of fir and pine clings to the edges, its roots hanging over the drops.
1490.lore: Vạn Hác's students climb here to play into the ravines and hear the echoes return. Zither makers take their soundboard wood only from trees that have fallen into the ravines.

1491.name: Cầm Tượng Trấn
1491.look: At the foot of a ravine wall, broken workshop roofs and half-carved zither bodies lie under a slope of fallen rock.
1491.lore: Zither makers settled here to serve Vạn Hác Viện soon after its founding. In 1012 the ravine wall gave way and buried half the town, and the survivors moved to the academy rim.

1492.name: Thủy Cùng Phong
1492.look: A high rocky peak stands above the abbey, the thin stream rising toward it and vanishing into a cleft halfway up.
1492.lore: Earth qi gathers in the stone above the place where the water ends. Abbot Tống Tọa Vân sends his oldest students up it to sit and watch the clouds rise.

1493.name: Quan Lan Bảo
1493.look: A square stone fort stands on a mountain spur above the sea, its gate open and its watch platform broken.
1493.lore: Thúy Vi built it to watch for Thôn Hải's pirate sails on the south coast. After the Pirate Purge of 781 it was no longer needed, and the garrison left within a decade.

1494.name: Thiết Trượng Phong
1494.look: Above Xuyên Lâm Môn's gate a thin, straight peak of dark rock rises like a staff planted in the ridge.
1494.lore: Metal (Kim) qi runs through its dark rock. A new guide of Xuyên Lâm must climb it with a staff and no rope before leading a traveller through the forest.
